PART-VII 


63.GENERAL GREY IRON CASTINGS (GRADE A).— (]) The castings shall be cast from metal melted or 
refined in any metallurgical plant other than an iron ore smelting furnace, for the use of which furnace permission 
in writing must be received from the Inspecting Authority. 


(2) The Composition of the iron as cast shall be left to the discretion of the manufacturer but the maximum 
percentage of phosphorus or sulphur or both may be specified by the Inspecting Authority, if it so desires. 


(3) The castings shall be accurately moulded in accordance with the pattern or working drawings supplied by 
the Inspecting Authority with the addition of such letters, figures or marks as may be specified and the 
drawings shall include the tolerances specified in the regulation. 


(4) (a)The castings shall be sound, clean out of twist and free from blow holes distortion and all surface and 
other defects. 
(b) They shall be well dressed or fettled and shall be machinable by normal methods. 


64. Provision of test bars.—(|) Prior to testing, the Inspecting Authority shall state whether it requires tensile or 
transverse tests, or both, and it may also specify cast on bars where the design of the casting and method of running 
permit. 

(2)(a) When the test bars are cast separately they shall be poured at the same time and from the same 
ladle, or metal as the casting or castings they represent. 

(b) The number of test specified in regulation 69 shall be applicable to all castings of each melt. 

(3) When the bars are cast-on, the mould for the casting and the mould for the test piece shall be joined 
together in such a manner that the liquid metal fills both moulds at the same operation. 

(4 ) All test bars shall be cast in green sand or dry sand or in loam moulds according to whether the 
casting or castings they represent are moulded in green sand, or in loam or dry sand, respectively. 

(5) The test bars shall not be subjected to any heat treatment after leaving the moulds.

PART-VIII 


7l.COVERED ELECTRODES FOR SHIELDED METAL ARC WELDING.—(I) (a)(i)This regulation shall 
apply to covered electrodes of sizes 2.0 mm and larger in diameter for shielded metal arc welding of carbon steel, 
low alloy steels, stainless steels and non-ferrous materials; 

(ii)Electrodes of less than 2.0 mm in diameter shall not be used in boilers. 


(b) The covered electrode shall comply with the requirements specified in these regulations. 


(c) The characteristics and behaviour under ordinary working conditions shall be such that satisfactory 
weld deposits can be made by a welder of average skill and experience and that the following 
characteristics are obtained, namely:- 


(i) relative ease in the control of the slag and weld metal during welding; 
(ii) good degree of stability of the arc; 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण

(2) 


(3) 


(4) 


(5) 


(6) 


(7) 


(iii) no undue degree of spatter; 

(iv) desired rate of deposition and depth of penetration. 
(v) easy removability of the slag; 

(vi) no undue tendency to under-cut; 

(vii) desired contour of the weld deposits: and 

(viii) low internal porosity of the weld metal. 


The covered electrodes shall be classified into following categories and in accordance with applicable 
Specifications for Filler Alloys (SFA) of American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Part IIC 
specifications or AWS (American Welding Society) specifications or equivalent: 


(a) Carbon steel electrodes 

(b) Low alloy steel electrodes 

(c) Stainless steel electrodes 

(d) Nickel and nickel-alloy welding electrodes 


Covered electrodes may be made by any method that shall yield a product conforming to the requirements 
of these regulations and relevant Specifications for Filler Alloys (SFA) or American Welding Society 
(AWS) specification. 


(a)The nominal size of the covered electrodes shall refer to the diameter of the core wire and the length 
shall not exceed 450 mm with provision for end gripping. 

(b)The tolerance on the specified diameter of the core wire of the electrodes shall be + 0.05 mm. 

(c)The tolerance on the length of the electrodes shall be ऊ+0 mm or as specified in relevant Specifications 
for Filler Alloys (SFA) or American Welding Society (AWS) specifications. 


(a)The core wire and covering shall be free from defects that would interfere with the uniform deposition 
of electrode. 

(b)The flux covering shall be sufficiently robust to withstand the normal conditions of transport, storage, 
handling and use, without damage and shall be uniform in thickness all over so that it fuses evenly. 

(c) The covering shall be concentric with core and the permissible variation on maximum core plus one 
covering shall not exceed the minimum core plus one covering as under: 


(i) For diameter up to 2.5 mm 7 % of mean dimension, 
(ii) For diameter 3.2 to 4.0 mm 5 % of mean dimension, and 


(iii) For diameter 5 mm and larger 4 % of mean dimension. 


At least one imprint of electrode classification shall be imprinted at the covering within 65 mm of grip 
end. The imprinting shall be legible both before and after welding. 


(a)Covered electrodes shall be suitably packed to guard against damage during transportation. When 
stored, the electrodes shall be kept in their original bundles or packing in a dry store room and under 
such conditions, the electrodes shall be capable of giving results similar to those which they would have 
given on the date of their dispatch from the manufacturer for a period of two years or as recommended 
by the electrode manufacturer whichever is less. Usage of electrodes beyond this period may be permitted 
after conducting check tests as per specification, provided it is not restricted by the electrode 
manufacturer. 


(b)Each package shall be marked with the following information. 


(i) Name of the Manufacturer. 
(ii) Trade name / Brand name of the electrodes. 
(iii) Size and quantity of electrodes. 


554 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(iv)Batch Number and date of manufacture. 
(v)Recommended current range. 
(vi) AWS Classification. 


(8) (a) The electrodes shall be subjected to initial tests and periodic check tests to ensure that the 
requirements of these regulations are fulfilled. 


(b) Electrodes intended for use with more than one type of current or polarity shall be tested using 
each type of current and polarity shall be tested using each type of current and polarity. 


(c) Where any test specimen fails to satisfy the requirements of any particular test, two further test 
specimens shall be prepared using the electrodes from the same batch and submitted to the same test. 


(d) The batch of electrodes shall be accepted as having passed the test provided that the tests of 
both the additional specimens are satisfactory. 


(9) Test certificate provided by the manufacturer of covered electrode shall fulfil the requirements of the 
specification. The manufacturers, when called upon, shall produce the results of the most recent periodic 
check test carried out within the preceding !2 months, for electrodes supplied. 


PART-IX 


72.RODS AND ELECTRODES FOR GAS SHIELDED ARC WELDING .—(|)(a)This regulation apply to 
electrodes and rods of sizes 0.8 mm and larger in diameter for gas shielded arc welding of carbon steels, low alloy 
steels, stainless steels and non-ferrous materials used in these regulations. 
(b) The rods and electrodes shall comply with this regulation and the applicable requirements of AWS or SFA 
specifications. 
(c) Their characteristics and behaviour under ordinary working conditions shall be such that satisfactory weld 
deposits can be made by a welder of average skill and experience with following characteristics. 
(d) The rods and electrodes shall be suitable for manual, semi-automatic and machine welding. 
(i) relative ease in the control of the molten pool during welding; 
(ii) desired degree of stability of the arc; 
(iii) no undue degree of spatter; 
(iv) desired rate of deposition and depth of penetration. 
(v) no undue tendency to under-cut; 
(vi) desired contour of the weld deposits: and 
(vii) low internal porosity of the weld metal. 
(2) The electrodes and rods shall be classified into following four categories, namely:- 
(a) Carbon steel Electrodes and rods; 
(b) Low-alloy steel electrodes and rods; 
(c) Stainless steel electrodes and rods; and 
(d) Nickel and nickel-alloy welding electrodes and rods 


(3) Electrodes and rods shall be made by any method to yield a product conforming to the requirements of 
these regulations and relevant Specifications for Filler Alloys (SFA) or American Welding Society 
(AWS) specification. 


(4) The size and tolerance of the electrodes and rods for straight length and coils form shall meet the 
appropriate Specifications for Filler Alloys (SFA) or American Welding Society (AWS) specification. 


(5) (a)The rods and electrodes shall have smooth finish and reasonably free from slivers, depressions, 
scratches, scale, seams, laps and foreign matter so that these do not affect the properties of the weld 
metal.

75.(\) Initial tests of each brand of electrodes shall be carried out in accordance with these regulations and relevant 
AWS or SFA specification. 
(2) (a) All weld metal tensile test specimens shall be prepared and tested in accordance with the method 
described in Appendix-C. 
(b) The ultimate tensile stress, yield stress and elongation of each test specimen shall meet the relevant 
AWS or SFA specification. 
(3) One fillet weld hot cracking test shall be carried out as specified in Appendix-C. 


(4) (a)The electrodes shall be deemed to be satisfactory provided no hot cracking occurs under the conditions 
of test. 
(b)Crater cracks may be neglected provided they do not run into the full section of the weld. 


(5) One transverse tensile test shall be carried out for each welding position for which the electrode is 
recommended by the manufacturer except two tests shall be required for the flat position. The ultimate 
tensile stress shall meet the relevant AWS or SFA specification. The method of preparation of the test 
pieces is specified in Appendix-C. 


(6) Two bend tests one with the face and the other with the root in tension shall be carried out for each 
welding position for which the electrode is recommended by the manufacturer, except that two in each 
shall be carried out for those intended for flat position only. The method of preparation and carrying out 
the test shall be in accordance with Appendix-C. The electrode shall be deemed to be satisfactory 
provided that on completion of the test, no crack or defect at the outer surface is greater than 3 mm 
measured across the specimen or |.6 mm measured along its length. Premature failures at corners of the 
test specimen shall not be considered a cause for rejection. For nickel alloy electrodes three transverse 
side bend test shall be carried out as per the applicable AWS or SFA specification. 


(7) Five impact test specimens are required for carbon steel and low alloy steel electrodes only. The size of 
the electrode shall be as per the relevant AWS or SFA specification. Charpy V notch testing shall be 
carried out as per the applicable AWS or SFA specification. 


(8) Each classification of electrode shall be tested for the chemical analysis of undiluted weld metal as per 
the relevant AWS or SFA specification. 


(9) (a) All weld test plate shall be radiographed to evaluate the usability of the electrode and the soundness 
of the weld deposits prior to taking up for other tests. 
(b) For the purpose of radiography, the backing plate shall be removed and both the surfaces of the weld 
metal shall be machined or ground smooth and flush without reducing the thickness of the weld metal. 
(c) Test procedure and acceptance norms shall be in accordance with the relevant AWS or SFA 
specification. 
(d) A length of 25 mm from both the ends of the test plate shall be discarded and need not be considered 
in evaluation of the radiograph.

(ii)One Tee joint fillet weld hot cracking test as mentioned in sub-regulation (3) of regulation 75.

PART-I 


77. Preparation of plates — (|)The edges of all plates and butt straps shall be machined or flame cut by machine 
and the caulking edges shall be bevelled to an angle not sharper than 20° to the plane of the plate and between 70° 
and 80°wherever practicable. Gusset Plates may be sheared except on those edges, which are to be welded. 


(2) Plates which are to be flame-cut by machine without heat treatment or subsequent grinding or machining 
shall not have a carbon content higher than 0.25 per cent. 


(3) Where the carbon content exceeds 0.25 percent, heat treatment, grinding or machining shall be carried 


out. 


(4) The edges of all plates shall have a smooth finish. 


(5) Before commencing welding of the joint (apart from tack welding), it shall be ascertained that the 
chamfered edges are in alignment and that the defects in alignment between the surfaces of the plates do 


not exceed as given in the table 3/I:

78. Normalising or stress relieving of steel plates — (l) All plates which have been dished or flanged shall be 
stress relieved as components when cold worked and normalized when hot worked fully or partially. 


(2) Stress relieving of components may be combined with final stress relieving when stress relieving is 
envisaged later. 


79. Minimum thickness of plates.— No boiler plate shall be less than 6 mm in thickness.

PART-II 


80. Cylindrical shells.— (.) Each ring shall be formed from not more than two plates and rolled to cylindrical 
form to the extreme ends of the plate. The bending shall be done entirely by machine. Local heating or hammering 
shall not be used for correction of profile. 


(2) The longitudinal seam or seams may be placed in any suitable position but the seams in successive 
rings shall not fall in line and shall be staggered by minimum |50 mm. 


(3) In the case of brick set boilers the seam or seams shall be kept as far as practicable clear of the 
brickwork. 


8. Position of longitudinal seams.— Each ring of plate forming the shell, barrel or drum shell, where practicable, 
be in one piece and have its longitudinal seam well out of line with those of the adjoining rings. In Lancashire, 
Cornish, and other types of boilers, where parts of the shell are exposed to flame, the longitudinal seams shell, 
where practicable, be in the steam space, arranged alternately on each side of the crown and clear of the brick 
work. 


82. Circumferential and end seams.— Joint efficiency of circumferential seams shall be determined as detailed 
in sub-regulation (() of regulation !69.In the event of tube holes forming a ligament at the location of 
circumferential seams, the joint efficiency shall be calculated as per regulation 7]. 


83.Angle rings.— Angle rings for the attachment of end plates to shell plates and/or flue sections shall be rolled 
or machined so that they fit closely to the flat and cylindrical surfaces to be connected, and shall be machined or 
machine gas cut on the caulking edges. 


84. Thickness of shell angle rings— Where shell plates and end plate are connected by means of an external 
angle ring, the angle rings shall not be less in thickness than as follows:

mm. 


85.Welded shell plates— The requirements of welded shells shall be covered by the provisions made in 
regulations in Chapter -4 or Chapter -2, as the case may be. 


PART-II 


86. Flat end plates.— (|) Wherever practicable, the flat or dished end plates of boilers shall be in one piece made 
from one rolled plate. Where diameter of boiler is so large as to make this impracticable, the flat end plates may 
be made from two pieces by fusion butt-welding. (See figures !2/l and 2/2). In the latter case, the line of welding 
shall be parallel to the horizontal axis of the boiler and shall be subjected to full radiographic examination. 


(2) Flanging of plates shall be done by machine. Cold forming of flanged end plate shall be followed by heat 
treatment. Such flanging shall be done hot, preferably in one operation, but where this is impracticable 
creep machine flanging may be used provided that the plate is worked at a suitable temperature and 
heated for an adequate distance beyond that portion of the plate under immediate treatment. 


562 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(3) Hot forming of welded plates shall be permitted provided that the welded joint is subjected to 00 percent 
radiographic or Ultrasonic examination after hot forming. 


(4) Welded plates up to and including 20 mm thickness can be cold formed provided it complies with 
following conditions. 


(a) Before cold forming, the weld reinforcement shall be ground smooth, and the manufacturer shall 
take precautions, where necessary, in order to avoid crack formation in the weld metal or the 


heat affected zone. 


(b 


wm 


If the inside radius of curvature after forming is less than |0 times the thickness, stress relieving 
shall be carried out. 


(c) After cold forming, the welded joints shall be visually examined and subjected to 00 percent 
radiographic or Ultrasonic examination throughout their length. Joints of any thickness which 


have been cold formed to a radius less than 0 times the thickness. 


(d 


wm 


Knuckles shall be inspected for cracks by magnetic particle or penetrant methods. 


(e) After completion of the flanging operation flanges shall be of true peripheral contour (either 
circular or straight as necessary to ensure accurate alignment with the connecting parts), and of 
good surface, free from bulges, grooves or other local irregularities; flat portions of the plate 
shall be free from set or distortion. 


(5) In the construction of unfired boilers when the dished ends do not form a part of the heating surface cold 
spun dished ends conforming to IS: 2825 may be used. 


(6) Care shall be taken to see that the flanges are circular and of good surface, free from local irregularities, 
and that they are parallel and square with the flat part of the plate. 


(7) Flat portions of end plates, on completion of all flanging and machining operations, shall be flat and free 
from set or distortion. 


87. Strengthening of flat end plate at manhole.— () In all cases, the front end plate gusset stays below the 
furnaces shall be placed as closely as possible to the mudhole frame. 


(2) Where flat end plates are flanged for connection to the shell, the inside radius of flanging shall be not 
less than .75 times the plate thickness, with a minimum of 38 mm. 


88. End Plates in steam spaces.— When the end plates of boilers situated in the steam space are liable to contact 
with hot gases, the end plates shall be efficiently shielded from such contact. 


89. Hemispherical crowns.— (l) The segments for hemispherical shell crown plates shall be pressed in one heat 
to correct curvature and shall be butt-welded together in accordance with Figures |2/3, 2/4, 2/5 or 2/6. The 
cylindrical portion of the crown shall be tangential to the hemispherical portion. 


(2) Where hemispherical furnace crowns are pressed from one plate, they shall be pressed to form by machine 
in progressive stages without thinning and shall be annealed on completion. 


90. Dished end and crown plates.— (|) The dished end plates of boilers shall be preferably in one piece made 
from one-rolled plate. If this is impracticable, owing to the large diameter, the dished end plate may be made 
from two plates, fusion butt welded together and in such cases the requirements of stress relieving and

radiographic examination as provided for in regulation 86 shall apply and the line of weld shall be parallel to the 
horizontal axis of the boiler. 


(2) The inside radius to which a plate is dished shall not be greater than the external diameter of the shell to 
which it is attached, except in the case of Lancashire and Cornish boilers when the radius shall not exceed 
% times the diameter of the shell. 

(3) The inside radius of curvature of the flanges to the shell or firebox shall not be less than four times the 

thickness of the crown or end plate and in no case less than 63 mm.

(5) Bunged mouth-pieces may be welded on to end plates in place of the orthodox flanging for the attachment 
of furnace tubes. Such welding shall comply with provisions of regulation 97. 


(6) Manhole frames may be similarly welded on the front end plates, and will be subject to provisions of 
regulation 97. 


9] 770९ plates.— Smoke box tube plates shall be flanged for attachment to the barrel or shell and shall be flat 
and connected thereto by welding. 


92. Parts of flat tube plates within the tube nests.—(|) Where the total area of all tube nests in directly fired 
multi-tubular boilers exceeds 0.65 square meters, stay tubes shall be fitted. 


(2) Where the total number of tubes in horizontal multi-tubular waste heat boilers and direct fired loco type 
boilers is arranged in one nest, the area of which exceed |.95 sq. m stay tubes shall be fitted. 


(3) Inall cases where the total number of tubes is arranged in more than one nest, stay tubes shall be fitted. 


(4) The parts of tube plates which lie outside the nests of tubes shall be stayed or supported wherever the size 
of the area of plate subject to steam pressure necessitates staying or support, either by marginal stay tubes 
or other means. 


93.Flanging of end plates.— All flanges shall be a good fit to the shell and flues. Flogging and/or hammering in 
the fitting of these parts is prohibited. The caulking edges of all flanged plates shall be machined or machine gas 
cut. 


PART-IV 
94. Furnaces.—()No furnace or firebox top, whether plain or corrugated, shall exceed 22 mm in thickness, and 
all circular sectioned furnaces when new, shall be as near the truly circular form as the type of joint will permit. 


(2) The use of Z angle rings for furnace foundation seams shall be prohibited. 


(3) Furnace crowns, uptakes and other plates not in tension may be joined by fusion welding provided the 
conditions laid down in regulation 95 to l0 are complied with. The end connections of such plates to 
the shell or shell crown shall also comply with such conditions. This construction shall not apply to 
furnaces of Lancashire and Cornish type boilers consisting wholly or plain sections. 


95. Furnaces of horizontal boilers— () The sections of the internal flues shall each be in one plate and shall 
be bent while cold to circular form and shall be welded longitudinally. 


(2) The maximum permissible variation in diameter at any cross-section shall not exceed the thickness of 
the plate. 


564 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(3) The weld shall be placed at the lower part of the flues, and shall break joint in successive sections by at 
least 305 mm. 


(4) Each flange for the circular seams shall be formed at one heat by suitable machinery. 
(5) The sections shall be allowed to cool gradually to avoid internal stresses. 
(6) The caulking edges of all flue flanges shall be machined or machine gas cut. 


(7) The circular seams shall be arranged so that they do not fall in line with those of the adjacent flue or with 
the circumferential seams of the shell and are at least !52 mm apart. 


(8) When flues are flanged for attachment to both end plates the total length of each completed flue shall 
not exceed the length of the shell measured from the inner surface of the back end plate to the inner 
surface of the front end plate, both adjacent to the shell. 


(9) Where the flues are flanged for attachment to the end plates, the end sections shall be !.5 mm thicker 
than the remaining sections, except in cases where the calculated thickness is over 2] mm, when the end 
section shall be 22 mm in thickness. 


(0) The flanged portion of furnace rings shall have radius of curvature of not less than 25 mm on water side. 


() Sections of corrugated flues may be fusion butt welded circumferentially and afterwards stress relieved 
by heat treatment. 


((2) As an alternative to adamson flanges, furnaces which are partly fitted with corrugated sections shall be 
strengthened by means of suitable stiffening rings adequately welded to the furnaces. In no case shall a 
flat stiffener be less than 63 mm x |3 mm. 


96. Furnaces of vertical boilers— (.) The furnaces of vertical boilers may be constructed in one or more 
lengthwise sections, each section being rolled from one plate to a full circle. In such cases, the component sections 
may be jointed circumferentially by electrically butt welding and shall be stress relieved in accordance with 
regulation |23. 


(2) In the case of vertical boilers where tube plates form part of the firebox, the tube plate portion may be 
constructed in two vertical sections and the vertical seams when welded shall be stress relieved. The 
maximum permissible variation in diameter, at any cross-section shall not exceed 6 mm for fireboxes up 
to 900 mm in diameter, or !0 mm for fireboxes over 900 mm in diameter, or half the thickness of the 
plate whichever is greater. 


(3) Circular furnaces shall preferably be tapered, a tapper of 38 mm in diameter per 300 mm of height being 
recommended. The minimum water space at the bottom between the furnaces and the shell shall not be 
less than 50 mm for boilers up to 760 mm in diameter and shall be not less than 63 mm for boilers over 
760 mm diameter. 


(4) The method of welding shall be in accordance with regulation !5!. Flats formed in the firebox for the 
insertion of water tubes shall have ample radius at the junction of the flat and the curved surfaces and 
shall be free from sharp comers or tool marks. The plate shall not be unduly thinned. 


(5) Ogee flanging where integral with the firebox or in a separate ring shall preferably be formed in one heat 
by suitable machinery and shall be allowed to cool gradually to avoid internal stresses. Rings of fire holes

(6) Furnaces of vertical type boilers may be attached to the shell at the fire hole by a circular ring of 
substantial section fusion welded to shell and firebox. The opening in the shell for fire hole shall be 
substantially compensated by a ring welded on the outside of the shell plate. 


(7) At the fire hole the firebox plate and the shell plate may be flanged and fusion welded together. 


97. Fusion butt welded longitudinal seams.— Where the longitudinal seam is fusion butt welded, the precautions 
shall be observed as follows: 


(i) Plates 20 mm and above in thickness shall be bevelled from both sides of each abutting edge but the bevel

may be bevelled from one side only of each abutting edge (see Figs. 3/3 and 3/4).The included angle of the

In order to obtain full penetration of the weld metal, a gap shall be maintained between the plates when they 
are being welded. Joints shall be welded from both sides, and the slag shall be removed after making each 
run. Before the second side of the joint is welded any slag or defect at the bottom of the first run shall be 
removed by grinding, chipping or machining. There shall be no appreciable undercutting of the plate. 


For the purposes of relieving internal stresses, the plates adjacent to a fusion weld shall be efficiently 
annealed after welding. 


98. Furnace crown.— (l) The furnace crown shall be made from one plate and the seam connecting it to the 
furnace shall not fall in line with any circumferential seam of the boiler shell. 


(2) The furnace crown may be welded to the vertical portion of the firebox. The joint shall be fusion butt 
welded by the electric arc process, provided the conditions for fusion welding under regulation 97 are 
observed. Where the joint is to be welded, the edges of the furnace crown and the firebox body shall be 
bevelled in accordance with Fig. 3/3 or Fig. 3/4. The depth of the flange of the furnace crown plate from 
the commencement of the curvature of the flanging radius shall be not less than four times the plate 
thickness with a minimum of 38 mm. On completion of welding the firebox shall be effectively stress 
relieved by heat treatment (also refer regulation l00). 


99. Cross tubes.— (l) Cross tubes shall be made from seamless steel pipes or from plate or strip rolled and electric 
resistance or fusion butt welded into pipes by electric arc process. The fusion welding shall conform to the 
requirements of Chapter-!2. Tolerances on these pipes shall conform to the requirements of regulation 25]. 
Where welded pipes are used, the longitudinal welds shall be so situated that they are not exposed to the direct 
impact of flame. 


(2) Cross tubes shall not exceed 305 mm internal diameter. The minimum thickness shall be 8 mm. 


(3) Where welded construction is employed, the tubes shall be of sufficient length to enter the furnace plate 
and the flush with the water side all round or project not less than 6 mm and not more than 6 mm into 
the water space at any part of the circumference. Where the tubes are fusion welded in position, the

PART-V 


02. Bar stays.— Bar stays shall not be welded at any part. They shall preferably have plus threads and the ends 
of the stays being upset or the middle portion being reduced for this purpose. Stay bars which have been worked 
in the fire shall be subsequently annealed. 


03. Longitudinal stays.—() Longitudinal and similar solid screwed stays shall be efficiently secured with nuts 
at each end and not merely riveted over. Where they are over 3657 mm in length, they shall be supported at 
intervals of 829 mm along its length. 


(2) Where the stay is screwed through both plates, the stay and holes shall have a continuous thread and 
fitted with nuts and washers on the outside. Where the stay passes through clearing holes and internal 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


567 


nut and washer shall also be fitted. Where the stay is not normal to the surface of the plate the washer 
shall be shaped so as to form a true surface for the nuts or a knuckle joint may be fitted. 


(3) In vertical boilers the stays shall either be screwed into both crown plates or screwed into the furnace 
crown plate and passed through clearing holes in the shell crown plate. 


04. Nuts and Washers for Stays.— (l) The washers shall be at least 2/2 times the diameter of the threaded 
portion of the stay and not less than 6 mm in thickness. 


(2) The thickness of the external nuts shall be at least equal to the diameter of the threaded portion of the 
stay. Where bar stays pass through clearing holes in end plates, internal nuts of a thickness not less than 
two-thirds of the diameter of the threaded portion of the stay shall be fitted. 


05. Jointed stays— Where jointed longitudinal stay are fitted, they shall, where practicable, be fitted with pins 
having an effective sectional area 25 percent in excess of that of the stay. If the pins are slack in the holes, the 
total slackness shall not be more than .6 mm. The pins shall be as close as possible to the shoulder of the eye 
forging. The shoulder of the forging shall be at least 3 mm wide all round, i.e. the diameter at the shoulder shall 
be not less than the diameter of the hole plus 25 mm. 


06. Diagonal bar or rod stays.— The sectional area of diagonal rod or bar stay shall bear the same proportion 
to that of a direct stay as the length of the diagonal stay bears to the length of the perpendicular line from the end 
of the diagonal stay to the surface supported. The ends of diagonal stays, shall not be bent, but shall be attached 
to the plate with bevelled washers and nuts or with riveted tee, blocks or angles and shackle pins (refer regulation 
05 for eyes and pins). 


PART-VI 
07. Screwed stays.— (|) Screwed stays and the holes for these shall be screwed with a continuous thread. 


(2) The screwed threads of the stay shall be clean and free from checks or imperfections, of full depth, correct 
whitworth form and a good fit in the holes. The middle portion shall preferably be turned down to the 
bottom of the thread. 


(3) The stays shall be screwed with fine threads of not less than | threads per 25 mm. 


(4) The diameter of the stay over the threads shall not be less than 9 mm or twice the thickness of the firebox 
plate whichever is the greater. 


(5) The pitch of the stays at the furnace of vertical boilers shall not exceed |4 times the thickness of the furnace 
plate. 


(6) Where the stays are not fitted with nuts, the ends shall be riveted over to form substantial heads. 
Alternatively stays may be screwed through the shell and firebox plates and the projecting ends shall be 
substantially fillet welded in an approved manner. The projection of the end of the stay from the surface 
of the plate shall be not less than one quarter of the diameter of the stay but in no case less than 6 mm. The 
full end of the stay shall be visible on completion of the welding. 


(7) Crown stays of Loco type boilers shall either be fitted with nuts or riveted over on the fire side. 
08. Axial drilling.— All screwed stays less than 355 mm long should preferably be drilled with a tell-tale hole 5 


mm diameter to a depth of 3 mm beyond the inner face of the plate. Stays which are obscure on one side shall 
preferably be made from hollow stay bar. 


568 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


09. Stay nuts.— (.) Nuts of screw stays in combustion chambers and firebox shall not be less than !9 mm thick 
for stays up to 38 mm diameter over threads, 22 mm thick for 4 mm and 44 mm stays, 25 mm thick for 47 mm 
and 5] mm stays, and 28 mm thick for stays over 5] mm in diameter. 


(2) The nuts shall be made of solid mild steel or of iron which shall be without weld, if exposed to flame. 


0. Spacing of end stays-allowance for curves, etc.— For the tops of fireboxes and combustion chambers, the 
distance between the rows of stays nearest to the tube plate or fire hole plate or back plate, as the case may be, 
and the commencement of curvature of these plates at their flanges shall not be greater than the horizontal pitch 
of the stays. 


PART-VII 


l. Girder stays for firebox and combustion chamber crowns.— (|) Each girder when of the normal type, 
fitted with stay bolts and nuts, shall be of the double plate interconnected type of sufficient strength to support its 
proportion of the load on the crown to support plate independently of the crown plate, and the bolts or weld 
attachments shall have sufficient cross-sectional area to carry the applied load. 


(2) The clear waterway between the crown plate and the underside of the girder bars shall be as large as 
practicable but in no case less than 38 mm as in Fig.3/8. 


(3) The ends of the girders shall not rest on the landing of the flat crown plate but shall be carefully fitted to 
bed directly on the bends of the corners of the vertical end or side plates. 


(4) The toes of the girder plates shall be solid with the girder plates and not separate pieces attached thereto. 
(5) Girders shall be properly attached to the crown plate by bolts or screws. 

Where an all welded firebox is fitted, the girder stays may be welded to the firebox prior to stress relieving. 
The girder stays shall be recessed for waterways as in sub-regulation (2) (Fig. 3/6 and Fig. 3/7). Such 


girders shall be securely welded by an approved method to the firebox crown. The method of welding and 
the proportions of attachment shall be to be satisfaction of the Inspecting Authority.

PART-IX 
6.Boiler tubes subject to external pressure.— Both plain and stay smoke tubes may be made either of wrought 
iron or steel and may be electric-resistance-welded or seamless. 


7. Fitting of plain tubes.—() Plain tubes shall be expanded at both ends. The expanding shall be parallel 
throughout the full thickness of the tube plate. Plain tubes may also be bell-mouthed, beaded, or welded at the 
gas inlet end. 


(2) Where stay tubes are not fitted, the ends of the tubes shall be beaded over at the fire box end and beaded or 
bell-mouthed at the other end. If bell-mouthed, the tubes shall protrude not less than 3 mm beyond the tube 
plate. 


PART-X 
8. Screw threads of stay tubes.—() Stay tubes shall be screwed at both ends with continuous threads, and the 
holes in the tube plates shall be tapped with continuous threads. The pitch of the threads shall not be finer than 
] threads per 25 mm. The stay tubes shall be expanded by roller expanders and not made right by caulking only. 


(2) Stay tubes may be attached by welding in which case they shall not be adjacent within the same tube nest 
except in local areas, where not more than two adjacent stay tubes may be attached by welding. The form of 
attachment shall be such that there is a mechanical hold in addition to the welding, as shown in Fig.3/l0. On 
completion of welding the stay tubes shall be lightly re-expanded.

9. Stay tubes.—(|) Stay tubes are tubes having a weld depth equal to the nominal tube thickness plus 3 mm. 
These stay tubes are not required within tube nests except when the tube nests comprise tubes which are expanded 
only. 


(2) If tube nests comprise plain tubes that are expanded and beaded, expanded and belled or expanded and

welded, welded stay tubes shall be used in boundary rows in sufficient numbers to carry the flat plate 
loadings outside the tube area. 


For plain tubes or stay tubes exposed to flame or gas temperatures exceeding 600°C, the ends of welded 
tubes shall be dressed flush with the welds. If not so exposed, the ends of welded tubes shall extend a 
maximum of |0 mm beyond the weld or, in the case of expanded tubes the tubes shall project beyond the 
tube plate up to a maximum of 5 mm. 


Each stay tube shall be designed to carry its due proportion of the load on the plates which it supports. 


The thickness of stay tubes welded into tube plates shall be such that the axial stress on the thinnest part of 
the tube does not exceed 7.4 kg/mm/.

20. Thickened ends of stay tubes.— If stay tubes are required to have their thickness increased at the screwed 
ends so that the thickness at the bottom of the threads is approximately the same as in the body of the tube the 
thickening shall be attained by upsetting and not by welding process, and the tubes shall be annealed after the 
upsetting. 


2. Load on stay tubes and stay bars.— Stay tubes shall be designed to carry the whole load due to pressure on 
the area to be supported. In each case the area to be calculated is as follows: 


(i) 


(ii) 


For a stay tube within the tube nest the net area to be supported shall be product of the horizontal and 
vertical pitches in mm of the stay tube less the area of the tube holes embraced. Where the pitch of the 
stay tube is irregular the area shall be taken as the square of the mean pitch of the stay tubes (i.e. the square 
of 4 of the sum four sides of any quadrilateral bounded by four adjacent stay tubes) less the area of the 
tube holes embraced. 


For a stay in the boundary row the net area to be supported shall be the area enclosed by lines passing 
midway between it and the adjacent points of support less the area of any tubes embraced. The adjacent 
points of support may be other stay tubes or the commencement of curvature of flanging of center line of 
the circle or rivets securing the end plate to the shell angle. 


572 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(iii) In the case of bar stay where there are no stay tubes in the tube nest the area to be supported shall extend 
to the tangential boundary of the tube nest.

22.Boiler and super heater tubes subject to internal pressure steel tubes.— (l) All tubes which are subject 
to internal pressure of water or steam shall be cold drawn or hot finished seamless or electric resistance welded in 
accordance with Chapter-2. Except as provided for in sub-regulation (2) below, they shall be without joint. 


(2) Tubes having an external diameter not exceeding !27 mm may be jointed and such joints may be flash welded, 
machine forge welded arc or gas welded. Tubes above !27 mm diameter may also be welded provided they 


are located outside the furnace. Such welds must conform to the requirements of Chapter-7.

flow area shall be ensured by conducting ball test using nearest ball diameter of 75% of the nominal Internal 
Diameter of the tube size.

All butt weld of tubes shall be tested as required hereunder: 


(i) For tubes greater than 78 mm bore, all welds shall be non-destructively tested by radiographic 
or other approved methods. 


(ii) For tubes greater than !02 mm bore and up to and including 78 mm bore, ten (l0) per cent of 
the welds by each welder, selected at random with a minimum of 2 welds per welder, shall be 
subjected to non-destructive examination by radiographic or other approved method. 


(iti) For tubes 02 mm bore and under, sample welds simulating the production welds shall be 
provided for mechanical testing either at a rate of 2 per cent or after each !50 welding hours with 
a minimum of one sample weld per welder. 


(iv) Alternatively, 5 per cent of the welds made by each welder selected at random, with a minimum 
of one weld per welder, shall be subjected to non-destructive examination by radiographic or other 
approved method. This rate may be reduced to 2 per cent by arrangement with the Inspecting 
Authority after initial satisfactory results have been produced. 


(v) In the event of any non-destructive test not meeting the requirements, defects in the welds 
represented by that test shall be rectified and the Inspecting Authority may call for an increase in 
the number of non-destructive tests until such time as a satisfactory standard is achieved. 


(9) — Butt welded joints as indicated in sub-regulation (8) shall be subjected to non-destructive examination by 
radiographic, radioscopy or other approved methods such as ultrasonic testing including phased array 
ultrasonic testing, magnetic particle inspection or liquid dye penetrant inspection. When radioscopic

a base metal of equivalent analysis. 


The nominal thickness to be considered for determining Post Weld Heat Treatment and soaking time 
shall be defined as: 


(i) For full penetration butt welds, the nominal thickness is the thinner of the parts being joined. 


(ii) For full penetration corner welds, the nominal thickness is the depth of the weld. 


(iii) For partial penetration groove and material repair welds, the nominal thickness is the depth of the 


weld. The total depth of partial or full penetration groove welds made from both sides shall be taken 
as the sum of the depth of both sides at a given location.

(iv) For fillet welds, the nominal thickness is the weld throat. When a fillet weld is used in conjunction

dimension, whichever is greater. 


(v) Except as stipulated in clause (vi) below, the nominal thickness is the depth of the groove, if present, 


through the shell or nozzle or reinforcing pad, or the throat of any fillet weld, whichever is greater. 


(vi) When multiple openings form a ligament where the spacing between centres is less than twice the 


average diameter, the nominal thickness of a combination groove and fillet weld shall be the sum of 
the groove depth and fillet weld throat. 


(vii) The thickness of the pressure part at the point of attachment where a non-pressure part is welded to 


a pressure part, in case of butt welds; 


(viii) The thickness of the fillet weld at the point of attachment where a non —pressure part is welded to 


a pressure part, in case of fillet welds.

24. Attachment of Steel Tubes.— (|) Steel tubes shall be connected to the tube plates by one of the following 
methods:- 


(2) 


(3) 


(4) 


(5) 


(6) 


(7) 


(i) Expanding. 
(i) Strength welding. 
(iii) Mechanical bolted ball joint. 


Drift or roller expanded tubes shall project through the neck or bearing part in the holes by at least a 
quarter of 25 mm and shall be secured from drawing out by being bell mouthed to the extent of 0.8 mm 
for each 25 mm in diameter plus |.6 mm. 


Tubes may be seal welded into fittings or headers for both boilers and super heaters after they have been 
expanded and flared provided the material in the fittings or headers does not contain carbon in excess of 
0.35 per cent. 


In the case of drifted or roller expanded tubes, the tube holes in the tube plates of drums, pockets, or 
headers shall be formed in such a way that the tubes can be effectively tightened in them. Where the tube 
ends are not normal to the tube plate, there shall be a neck or belt of parallel seating of at least 3 mm 
depth measured in a plane normal to the axis of the tube at the holes. 


Where tubes are strength welded direct to the tube plates, the technique followed shall be approved by 
the Inspecting Authority and all welds shall be suitably heat treated. In the case of plates below 22 mm 
thickness, the requirement of stress relieving by heat treatment after welding of the tubes may be waived 
provided the weld satisfies the requirements of the maximum hardness and also the requirements 
concerning the impact values of the weld metal. The welding procedure adopted and the weld sequence 
selected shall also be subject to the approval of the Inspecting Authority. This provision in applicable to 
only shop welding of tubes at the Manufacturers Works. 


Tubes spacers, supporting clips and lugs may be welded to the tubes. Flash welding of studs for 
supporting refractories, etc, is also permissible. 


The tubes shall be so arranged that they are accessible for cleaning internally and externally.

PART-XII 


25. Headers, mud boxes, etc. of water tube boilers.—(.) (a) Headers and mud boxes, etc. of water tube Boiler 
may be of seamless or welded steel or of cast steel complying with the requirements of the provisions contained 
in regulations 49 to 57. Where welded, the welding shall be stress relieved, radio graphed or ultrasonically 
examined and in all respects shall be to the satisfaction of the Inspecting Authority as per Table 3/5 of regulation 
23. 


(b) Open ends of seamless steel tube headers may be closed by forging or the ends may be secured by 
bolting, screwing or welding in an approved manner. Bolting shall not be used where the bolts are 
exposed to or are swept by gases of combustion. 


(c) The method of attachment of the ends shall be subject to the ends shall be subject to the approval of 
the Inspecting Authority. 


(2) Each piece prior to being fitted in place shall be subjected to hydraulic tests to one-and-a-half times the 
design pressure of the boiler into which it is to be fitted. 


3) (9) The sighting hold doors and header caps shall be substantial and be capable of being removed 
or replaced from time to time without loss of efficiency of safety. They may be held in position 
either by means of bolts or by seal welding. 


(b) The bolts by which they are held in place shall be fitted to them in such a way as to satisfy the 
above conditions. 


(c) The doors shall be so designed that they will not blow out in the event of breakage of the bolt. 


(d) Circular holes also may be provided in addition to elliptical holes, if provision is made to prevent 
the door bolts from turning, while securing the joint. 


(4) All flanges shall have a fillet with a radius of curvature at least equal to the thickness of the necks to 
which they are attached. 


PART-XIII 


26. Stand pipes and pads etc..—Stand pipes and seating for carrying mountings shall be made of wrought, cast 
of fabricated steel. These shall take the form of short stand pipes, pressed steel plate saddles, forged pads or pads 
cut from round rolled bar as may be most convenient and secured to the boiler by welding. Where short stand 
pipes are used they shall be of solid forged, fabricated or cast steel. They shall be carefully bedded to the shell 
before attachment. The jointing faces to which mountings are to be bolted shall be machined. Pads shall have 
sufficient thickness to allow the drilling of stud holes for mountings without the inner surface being pierced and 
the length of the screwed portion of the stud in the pad shall be not less than the diameter of the stud. 


27. Design of stand pipes.— The design of the branches and stand-pipe shall be regulated in the following 
manner: 


(i) in order to withstand the maximum allowable working pressure, the minimum thickness of branch and 
stand-pipe shall be determined in accordance with the provisions specified in sub-regulation (l) of 
regulation 244; 


(ii) Compensation requirements for openings in the main pressure parts shall be determined in accordance with 
the provisions of regulation 79; 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


(iii) The additional thickness shall be considered to withstand superimposed loading due to connecting pipe- 
work or fittings. 


(iv) The minimum thickness of the branch or standpipe shall be the greatest of the values required above and 
shall not be less than 0.0i5 do plus 3.2 mm where, d, is the outside diameter of the branch (in mm); 


Provided that the provisions of the regulations shall not apply to such tube stub which have been 
designated as tubes. 


28. Pressed plate saddles.— Where pressed plate saddles are employed they shall be formed to bed closely to 
the boiler and machined on the face jointing the mounting and on the edges. The studs for attachment of 
mountings, if screwed through the saddle, shall each be fitted with a nut on the inside having a thickness equal to 
the diameter of the stud. Where the stud holes do not penetrate through the saddle, the length of the screwed 
portion of the stud in the plate shall not be less than the diameter of the stud. 


29. Seatings for mountings.— (]) For pressures not exceeding 8.7 kg/cm?(g), mountings with the screwed ends 
not exceeding | inch S.P.T.(Straight Pipe Threads) may be used; the screwed portion of any such mounting being 
not less than 5 mm. 


(2) |The mountings may be screwed: 
a. Directly into the boiler shell plate, nuts being fitted on the water side, or 


b. Into steel distance pieces the length of thread engaged being in no case less than the bore of the mounting 
plus 6 mm. 


(3) The distance pieces shall be made from solid mild steel. They shall be screwed into the plate and fitted 
with nuts on the water side. The walls of the distance pieces shall be not less than 6 mm thick at the 
bottom of the thread. 


30. Attachment of mountings.— (l) Mountings may be attached directly to any shell or end plate where the 
plate is of sufficient thickness to allow a suitable surface to be obtained for the attachment of the boiler mountings. 


(2) The minimum thickness at the hole in the shell or end plate shall be not less than the thickness required 
for the maximum allowable working pressure considering the plate as being unpierced. 


(3) Where the boiler mountings are secured by studs, the studs shall have a full thread holding in the plate 
for at least one diameter. If the stud holes penetrate the whole thickness of the plate. The stud shall be 
screwed right through the plate and be fitted with a nut inside having a thickness equal to the diameter 
of the stud. Where bolts are used for securing mountings they shall be screwed right through the plate 
with their heads inside the shell or end plate. 


3. Insufficient thickness of end plates.— (|) In cases where the thickness of the end plate is insufficient for 
this purpose the mountings shall be joined to suitable steel seatings as provided in regulation 26. 


(2) The following constructions as to stand pipes attached to shells and end plates shall be permissible: 


(i) Where the internal diameter of the stand pipe does not exceed 25 mm, the standpipe may be 
screwed into the plate and fitted with a nut on the waterside. 


(ii) Where the internal diameter of the standpipe exceeds 25 mm but does not exceed 5 | mm, it may 
be screwed in and seal-welded. 


(iii) Where the diameter of the standpipe exceeds 5] mm, it may be welded to the end plate. 


582 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(3) | The foregoing provisions as to the stand pipe shall be regulated by the following conditions: 
(i) When stand pipes are screwed, the screwing shall be of Standard Pipe Thread, 


(ii) Where stand pipes, saddles or other forms of seatings are fabricated by fusion welding they shall be 
stress relieved by heat treatment before attachment to the boiler, 


(iii) Where the bore of the stand pipe or seating and the hole in the plate do not exceed 27 mm plus 
twice the thickness of the plate, the seating may be welded to the plate without subsequent heat 
treatment of the weld so made. Where the hole in the plate exceeds !27 mm plus twice the thickness 
of the plate, the plate to which seating is attached shall be stress relieved by heat treatment. 


32. Attachment of water and pressure gauges— Water gauge and pressure gauge siphons may be attached 
direct to the front end plates without the intervention of a pad or stand pipe, provided they are flanged and secured 
by studs. If the studs are screwed through the plate, nuts shall be fitted on the inside of the plate. 


33. Mountings on flat places— Where the flanged mountings are attached direct to a flat plate, such mountings 
shall be provided with a substantial spigot, the full thickness of the boiler plate. 


34. Bolts and nuts— Bolts and nuts shall be machined where they come in contact with the flanges, and all 
holes in saddles and pads shall be drilled. 


Note: In all cases where the boiler is lagged the joint of the mountings shall be clear of the lagging 
surface or the lagging kept clear of flange so that the joint can be inspected and, when necessary, remade. 


PART-XIV 


35. Manholes, mudholes etc.— (.) Sufficient sight and cleaning holes shall be provided to permit efficient 
inspection and cleaning. Such holes shall normally be elliptical in form and not less than 89 mm x 63 mm. 


(2) At least one manhole or sight hole shall be provided in the upper part of the cylindrical shell or in the 
shell crown, or end plate and this shall not be less than as given in the TABLE 3/8:

(4) Where cross tubes are fitted in Vertical boilers one cleaning hole shall be provided opposite at least one

(5) Cleaning holes or mud holes in Loco Tope boilers shall be provided at each bottom corner of the outer

(6) Inthe case of small boilers or where the foregoing provisions are impracticable the cleaning holes or mud 
holes shall be as near as possible in the corner of the outer firebox casing and the holes as large as 
circumstances permit. 


36. Compensating rings and frames for openings in shells — (]) Compensating rings and frames for openings 
in shells shall be of same material as that of shell. The compensation provided shall preferably be flanged frames, 
which shall be fitted in all cases where the shell plate exceeds 4 mm thick. Flanged frames shall be weld-less 
and shall be flanged or pressed to provide a flat jointing surface for the cover. 


(2) All compensating rings and frames shall be formed to bed closely to the surfaces to be connected. Any 
weld therein shall be on the transverse centre line. 


(3) The flat jointing surfaces of all flanged or pressed frames and all doors or covers shall be machined. 


37. Internal doors.— Internal doors shall be of wrought steel in accordance with Chapter-2 and constructed in 
accordance with the following:- 


(!) Doors shall be formed to fit closely to the internal joint surface and should be fitted with studs, nuts 
and crossbars; 


(2) Doors for circular opening larger than 250 mm or elliptical/rectangular openings larger than 250 mm x 
75 mm shall have two studs but for openings of 250 mm x | 70 mm or less only one stud may be fitted. 
Doors for openings not larger than !23 mm x 90 mm may have the stud forged integrally with door; 


(3) Doors studs shall be of welding quality steel having a minimum specified tensile strength of not less than 
36.7 kg/mm? and those for manholes shall be not less than 30 mm and they shall be fixed in any of the 
following way:- 


(a) screwed through the plate and fillet welded on inside; 


(0) fillet welded each side of the plate with a leg length of not less than |0 mm; 


(c) attached to the door by an intermediate plate or lugs so that the strength of the attachment is not less 
than the strength of the studs and the studs are prevented from turning; or 


(d) provided with an integrated collar and be riveted or screwed onto the door plate and be prevented from 
turning in which case the strength of the attachment shall not be less than the strength of the studs; 


(4). Door spigot when the door is in the central position shall have a clearance of approximately 05 mm 
all around and at no point shall the clearance exceed 3 mm. The spigot depth shall be sufficient to trap 
the gasket; 


(5) | The nuts shall be of appropriate material compatible with that of the bolts and be placed on the seating 
surface; 


(6) The cross-bars shall be of substantial proportions and of mild or wrought steel. 


Note: Eye bolts of suitable legs on the door plate or headed bolts engaging with slotted sections on the 
door plate may be used instead of studs. 


(7) The minimum calculated thickness of the door of the flat plate construction (i.e. unstiffened and made 
from one plate shall be not less than that determined by the following formula: -

(e) Bolts and nuts shall be machined where in contact with the flanges and the joints should be formed

dished outwards to a depth of approximately one-eighth of the internal diameter of the frames. 


(f) All frames and mouthpieces shall be close to the surfaces to which they are to be connected. All 
caulking edges shall be machined or machine gas cut. 


39. Positions of manhole in shell — Manholes and other openings in cylindrical shells shall be placed as far as 
possible from the seams, preferably towards the back end to the boiler top. Wherever practical, oval openings 
shall be arranged with the minor axis parallel to the longitudinal centre line of the boiler. In no case shall the 
circumferential length of any opening exceed twice the longitudinal width of the opening. 


40. Compensation rings to manholes— Compensation shall be provided in every case for the part cut of a 
cylindrical shell for a manhole. The strength of the net section of compensating ring and also welds securing them 
to the shell, compared with that part of the shell cut out, shall not be less than the efficiency of the longitudinal 
seam. 


4. Compensation for cutting large holes in shell type boilers—— Where holes are cut in the cylindrical shell 
for the purpose of attaching a seating of frame or door, compensation shall be provided such that the added 
sectional area, including parts of the frame within l0.6 mm of the shell shall be not less than the sectional area 
of the plate removed which shall be the product of the diameter of the opening and the calculated thickness of the 
plate as found by Equation(4/2). Where holes are cut in the cylindrical shell for the purpose of fixing seating for 
mountings and the diameter of the holes is greater than 2’ times thickness of the shell plate plus 70 mm, 
compensation shall be provided. Where a large opening is cut in a cylindrical shell to receive another part of the 
structure, the sides where cut away shall be efficiently cross-stayed or strengthened in some other effective 
manner.

CHAPTER -4 
FUSION WELDED DRUMS FOR WATER TUBE BOILERS AND SUPERHEATERS 


42. General requirements.— Where applicable the general terms of Chapter- relating to Certificates from 
Makers, Inspecting Authorities, etc., and of Chapter-3 concerning construction shall be followed. 


PART-I 


43. Materials of construction for fusion welded Boiler Drums.—(|) For plates to be used in the construction 
of fusion welded boilers drums, requirements of Chapter-2 shall apply. 


(2) Plates having thickness of more than 50 mm, before being fabricated, shall be uniformly heat treated to produce 
grain refinement and heat treatment involving quenching in a liquid medium is not permitted. 


PART-II 


44. Fusion Welded Drums.— The term 'Fusion Weld’, for the purpose of this Chapter, is applicable to all welded 
joints made by the metal arc process with covered electrodes or other electric arc process, in which the arc stream 
and the deposited weld metal are shielded from atmospheric contamination. 


45. This Chapter shall apply to the single run or heavy run welding process and that welded boiler drums 
manufactured by that process shall conform with all regulations of this Chapter, except those in which divergence 
is necessary solely because of special requirements essential for the most efficient utilisation of that process and 
all regulations governing quality of material, construction workmanship and testing (both non-destructive and 
otherwise) are applicable. 


46. Equipment of workshop.— (l) The welding plant and equipment shall be of good quality and maintained in 
an efficient working condition. 


(2) The welding apparatus shall be installed under cover and shall be arranged so that the welding work may be 
carried out in positions free from draughts and adverse weather conditions. 


(3) The procedure shall be such that there is regular and systematic supervision of the welding works, and the 
welding operators are subjected to periodic tests for quality of workmanship by the works officials. 


(4) Records of these periodic tests shall be kept and made available by works office to the Competent Person for 
scrutiny. 


47.Testing Laboratory.— 


(.) The works shall be equipped with an efficient testing laboratory which shall include apparatus suitable for 
carrying out tensile, bend and impact tests, micro-examination of specimens and x-ray examination of the actual 
joints in pressure vessels. 


(2) The works shall also be equipped with a suitable heat treating furnace having satisfactory means for 
temperature control, but as an alternative arrangement may be made whereby the drums can be heat-treated 
elsewhere. 


48. Constructional details and preparation for welding.— (|) Before starting the construction work, the 
manufacturer shall furnish to Inspecting Authority, a fully dimensioned sectional drawing reflecting therein 
complete details of construction of the drum for approval. 


(2) Fully dimensioned drawings of the proposed welds preparations of the main seams drawn to a scale, clearly 
reflecting therein all the relevant details shall be furnished. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 587 


(3) Sketches showing details of the welds preparations for the attachment of the stand pipes, branch pipes and 
seating and their locations relative to the longitudinal and circumferential seams and to other openings shall be 
furnished. 


49. Preparation of plates.— For the purpose of preparation of plates, requirements contained under regulation 
77 shall apply. 


50. Cylindrical Shell of Drums.— 
(.) Each drum shell plate shall be of cylindrical form to the extreme edges of the plate. 
(2) The bending shall be done entirely by machine and local heating or hammering is prohibited. 


(3) Where the plates are bent to an internal diameter less than 20 times of the plate thickness, they shall be 
efficiently heat-treated after bending or combined with final post weld heat treatment. 


5l. Method of making welded joints.—(.) For the purpose of requisite quality of welding, the seams may be 
welded from both sides of the plate or from one side of the plate with or without a backing strip and If a backing 
strip is used, it shall be removed and the surface so exposed shall be dressed. 


(2) Additional runs of metal shall be deposited at the surface of the welded seams so that the welded metal at 
the level of the surfaces of the plate is refined as far as possible. 


(3) Thickness of such additional welding shall not exceed values given in Table 4 below.

(4) The surfaces of the welds which are to be subsequently radiographed shall be sufficiently free from coarse 
ripples, overlap, grooves, abrupt ridges and valleys, so as to avoid stress raisers and to permit proper interpretation 


588 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


of radiographs and other Non-Destructive Testing(NDT) methods. If there is a question regarding the surface 
condition of the weld when interpreting a radiographic film, the film shall be compared to the actual weld surface 
or provide smooth contours and to be flush with the respective surfaces of the plate before radiography 
examination is done. 


(5) Undercut shall not exceed 0.8mm or !0% of wall thickness, whichever is less and undercut shall not encroach 
on design wall thickness. 

(6) When affixing standpipes, branch pipes, seating, compensating plates, doubling plates or manhole frames, not 
less than two runs of metal shall be deposited at each weld. 


(7) Each run of weld shall be thoroughly cleaned and free from slag that may adversely affect the quality of the 
succeeding runs. 


(8) Welds shall be marked permanently to facilitate their location. 


52. Type of welded joints — The longitudinal and circumferential seams shall be made with butt joints of the 
single or double U or Vee type. 


53. Number of joints.— Where, having regard to the approved design, the dimensions are such that the shell 
cannot be made from a single plate, it shall be made with the minimum number of joints and the longitudinal 
seams in successive rings shall not fall in line, except where the rings of the drum are in two halves of unequal 
thickness. 


54. Position of the tube holes —(|) Tube holes in welded seams shall be avoided as far as possible. Where the 
holes are unavoidable, they may be machined through welded seams after these seams are radiographed. 


(2) In the case of vanadium steels, in addition to radiography, the welded seams shall be stress relieved. 


(3) The efficiency of the ligament in the direction of weld shall be multiplied by a weld factor not exceeding 0.95 
except where the distance from the edge of the tube hole to the edge of the weld is greater than 3 mm. 


(4) The edge of the weld shall be considered to be the edge of the weld groove as machined in the plate prior to 
welding. 


Notwithstanding anything in this regulation, efficiency of the ligament in the direction of weld shall not 
be multiplied by a weld factor 0.95 where l00 percent radiography of weld joint is done.

located at one end only. 


(2) Where the drum shell is formed in two or more courses, the staggered longitudinal seam shall be regarded as 
a continuous longitudinal seam provided the welding be effected in one reasonably continuous operation and 
by the same operator or operators. 


(3) Where there are circumferential seams only or where the method of welding the circumferential seam differs 
from that employed for the longitudinal seams, the method of providing the test plates shall be decided by the

of test specimen, shall apply. 


(3) On completion of the test, no crack or defect on the outer surface of the specimen shall be greater 
than |.5 mm measured across the specimen, or 3 mm measured along the specimen. Premature failure at the 
comers of the specimen shall not be considered as a cause for rejection.

63. Additional tests before rejection.— (l) In case any of the test specimens taken in accordance with 
regulations [56 to 62 fail to meet the specified requirements, one retest shall be allowed for each specimen that 
fails, provided the following minimum figures have been obtained. 


(a) Reduction in area 30 per cent. 


(0) Any other test except the bend and impact tests, 90 percent of the specified requirements. 


(2) Incase, a cold bend specimen fail to meet the specified requirements, two re-tests shall be taken from 
the same test plate and these shall comply with the requirements of regulations !60 and l6]. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण
