(3) If Charpy impact test fails to meet the specified requirements, two re-tests shall be taken from the test 
plate on each side of the original specimen and separated from it by not more than 5 mm. Both re-tests 
shall show a minimum Charpy impact test value of 2.76 kgfm. 


(4) If it is found that there is insufficient metal to permit the preparation of specimen for re-test from the 
reminder of the test may be cut from the test plate relating to the opposite and of the same longitudinal 
seam. 


64. Non-Destructive test.— (l) Micro and Macro Examination— A specimen, the full thickness of the plate and 
not less than |3 mm wide may be taken from each set of test plates by the Inspecting Authority for the purpose of 


micro and macro examination. Macro-etching of a complete cross-section of the weld including the heat effected 


zone, should show satisfactory penetration, fusion and absence of significant inclusions or other defects. In case 


of a doubt as to the condition of the weld as shown by micro-etching, the area concerned shall be microscopically 


examined for defect investigation. 


(2) Radiographical examination—(a) Every portion of the longitudinal and circumferential welded joints of the 


(3 


(4 


(5 


drums shall be subjected to radiographical examination or ultrasonic examination. Where ultrasonic 
examination is used, it shall be demonstrated to the satisfaction of the Inspecting Authority that the 
equipment and the technique used are satisfactory. The manufacturer shall ensure that the operator employed 
is competent to use the equipment, apply the technique and interpret the results of the examination. NDE 
operator and evaluator shall possess qualification as per ASNT SNT-TC-IA or ISO 972 or equivalent. 


(6) The method employed in obtaining the radiographs shall be such as to show clearly defects having a 


) 


) 


~— 


magnitude equal to 2 per cent of the thickness of the welded joint. To determine whether this result is being 
obtained and indicator of approved form which includes a portion equivalent to not more than 2 per cent 
of the joint thickness, shall be placed in the vicinity of the weld so as to make a record on each radiograph. 
Each section of every weld shall be marked so that the radiographs can be easily correlated to the particular 
part of the joint represented. Radiographic or Ultrasonic testing shall be carried out as per written down 
procedure specifying technique, IQI sensitivity, density requirements and acceptance norms in line with 
established International boiler codes subject to acceptance by the Competent person. 


(c)The examination shall be made from the original films and the acceptability of the welds shall be rejected 
or dealt with under regulation !65 and be radiographed again. 


(d) PAUT or TOFD or both in lieu of Radiographic test may be used subject to establishing a procedure to 
include techniques, set ups, calibrations, operator qualification, acceptance norms in line with International 
Codes. 


Magnetic Particle Flaw Detection- Magnetic method of flaw detection shall be employed wherever possible 
for ferritic steel. 


Dye-Penetrate Flaw Detection- Dye penetrants or equivalent method of flaw detection shall be employed for 
Austenitic or other non-magnetic steel. 


All butt welded joints shall be subjected to non-destructive examination by radiographic, radioscopy or other 
approved methods such as ultrasonic testing, magnetic particle inspection or liquid dye penetrant inspection. 
When radioscopic examination is to be performed in lieu of radiography on welded components, the following 
requirements shall be met, namely: - 
(a) A written procedure shall be submitted for approval to the Inspecting Authority which shall contain 
the following: 
(i) material and the thickness range; 


(ii) equipment qualifications; 
(iii) test object scan plan; 

(iv) radioscopic parameters; 

(v) image processing parameters; 


596 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(vi) image display parameters; 

(vii) image archiving requirements; 

(vill) accept-reject criteria (Code reference); 
(ix) performance evaluation; 

(x) Operator identification. 


(0) The system shall be aided with an image processor to enhance the quality of the radioscopic images 
and system performance quality shall exhibit: 
(i) a thin section contrast sensitivity of 3%; 


(ii) a thick section contrast sensitivity of 2%; 
(iii) a spatial resolution of 3 line pairs per mm; 
(iv) IQI sensitivity - 2% of the joint thickness when wire IQI's are to be used, the wire diameter 
axis shall be oriented along the axis of the least sensitivity of the system. 
(c) Radioscopes shall be properly marked to co-relate with particular part of joint represented. 


(d) The radioscopic examination data shall be recorded and stored on videotape, magnetic disk or optical 
disk or any other electronic storage device at the maker's plant for a sufficient period after the date 
of radioscopic examination as specified by the Inspecting Authority, Efficient radioscopic 
examination record recall shall be made available at any time over the record retention period and 
shall be traceable to the test objects. 


(e) When repair has been performed as a result of radioscopic examination, the repaired areas shall be 
re-examined using the same radioscopic technique to evaluate the effectiveness of the repair. 


(f) To aid in proper interpretation of the radioscopic examination data, the details of the technique used 
shall accompany the data. As a minimum, the information shall include the approved procedure 
requirements and system performance test data. 


65. General.— (l) (a) Any repair to a weld carried out by the manufacturer shall first be agreed to by the 
Inspecting Authority. 


(b)Where defects occur in distributed positions in a seam, repairs to the extent of I5 per cent, of the total 
length of the seam shall be permitted to replace the defective welding. 


(c)Where defects are located in a single continuous length, the permissible extent of repair shall be decided 
by the Inspecting Authority. 


(2) Where the weld metal in any way fails to comply with the requirements specified, the whole of the weld metal 
may be removed and the seam re-welded provided that; 


(a) the original test plates are similarly treated, or 


(b) New test plates of the same thickness as the joint and of similar quality of material are attached to the 
end of the seam and re-welded with it. 


(c)In either case the plates shall be tested in accordance with regulations 56 to 64 and the requirement for 
heat treatment shall be in accordance with regulation 66. 


(3) With regard to the extent of permissible repair and when agreed by the Inspecting Authority, a circumferential 
seam shall be treated in the same manner as a longitudinal seam. The Inspecting Authority shall be entitled to 
call for representative tests for a re-welded circumferential seam. 


(4) Defects shall be cut out by chipping of machining or by burning out by the Air Arc Weld Process. 


(5) Where a defective part has been cut out, the Inspecting Authority shall be entitled to make an examination before 
re-welding. 


(6) Only metallic arc welding shall be used for repairs. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 597 


(7) All repaired areas shall be subjected to radiographical examination or radioscopic examination by the approved 
techniques. 


(8) The Inspecting Authority shall be entitled to call for specimen representing any welded repair, for the purpose 
of examination and test. 


(9) On completion of all welded repairs, the manufacturers shall, if requested, supply for record purposes a detailed 
diagram showing the positions, length depth and width of all such repairs. 


66. Heat treatment.—(|) (a)After completion of the welding of the seams and the welding on the stand pipes and 
including welding repairs but before the hydraulic test, each drum shall be heat treated for stress relieving; during 
this heat treatment the official test plates shall be lying inside the drum. 


(b)For heat treatment requirements refer regulation 23. 


(2) Where shell is subjected to a primary stress relieving treatment identical to the final heat treatment to be given 
to the drum, the test plates may be placed inside the shell during the primary treatment and thereafter cut up 
and tested without waiting for the final treatment of the drum. 


(3) Where the shell is not subjected to primary stress relieving treatment or is subject to a primary stress relieving 
treatment which is not identical with the final heat treatment, the test plates may be placed inside any other 
drum of comparable dimensions which is to be heat treated in accordance with this Chapter. The heat treatment 
is to take place in the furnace in which the drum relating to the test plates will eventually be given its final 
heat treatment. 


(4) Temperature charts shall be submitted to indicate that the test plates and the drum they represent have been 
subjected to identical heating soaking and cooling treatment. 


(5) (a) For the heat treatment, the drum shall be placed in a furnace sufficiently larger to accommodate the whole 
drum. 


(b) The furnace shall have proper means of temperature measurement and control and shall be capable of 
heating the whole of the drum to a uniform temperature. It shall be so designed as to prevent direct 
impingement of flame on the drum. 


(c) Thermocouples shall be attached to the drum at appropriate locations. A temperature time diagram of the 
stress-relieving process shall be provided for a welded shell or drum and a similar diagram for other welded 
pressure part shall be provided where inspecting Authority requires it. 


(6) Alternative procedure for the heat treatment of the drum may be submitted to the —_ inspecting Authority for 
approval. 


(7) In special cases it may be permissible to heat treat the test plates separately from the drum, provided the 
inspecting Authority is satisfied with the means adopted to ensure that the following factors shall be the same 
for the drum as for the test plates, namely:- 

(i) Rate of heating 

(ii) Maximum temperature 
(iii) Time held at maximum temperature 
(iv) Conditions of cooling. 


67. Hydraulic test at makers’ works.— () Boiler drum having internal diameter greater than 600 mm and other 
cylindrical component having internal diameters greater than !000 mm shall be hydraulically tested on completion 
of manufacture at the makers works in the presence of Competent Person to |/% times the maximum allowable 
working pressure without indication of weakness and defects. 


598 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(2) All components which are not reasonably accessible for inspection after assembly into the boiler or have been 
tested hydraulically prior to welding at a pressure less than that specified in sub-regulation (l) shall be tested 
hydraulically to % times the maximum allowable working pressure before assembly into the boiler. 


(3) Tubular products that have been hydraulically tested to the required pressure prior to welding or ultrasonically 
tested shall not require further hydraulic testing as components provided they were joined during assembly by 
circumferential butt joint which have been welded and non-destructively tested as per relevant provisions of these 
regulations. 


(4) Components other than tubular products shall not require hydraulic testing before assembly into the 
boiler if the completed boiler is tested hydraulically to |% times the design pressure at site. 


(5) In case of drums, headers which are to be fitted with tubes, the test may be made before drilling of tube 
holes but after attachments of nozzles and similar fittings. 


(6) The test pressure shall be raised gradually under proper control at all times so that it never exceeds by 
more than 6% of the required pressure and maintained for 30 minutes whereupon the pressure shall be reduced to 
maximum allowable working pressure and maintained for sufficient time to permit close visual inspection for 
leakages of the pressure parts. 


(7) The temperature of water used as medium of pressure testing shall not be less than 20°C and more than 
50°C. 
(8) (a) In case of drums of ‘composite’ construction and partly reverted and partly welded seams or seamless 


forged drum shell with ends attached by fusion welding. 
(b) The test pressure shall be the same as for fusion welded drums. 


(9) In case the hydraulic test reveal any defects in the welded steam, it shall not be repaired unless the 
Inspecting Authority permits to do so. 


(0) On completion of agreed repairs to a drum which has previously been stress relieved by heat treatment, 
further heat-treatment, if required by the Inspecting Authority shall be done and the drum shall again be subjected 
to hydraulic test.

and pitched longitudinally at not greater than an average pitch of four tube diameters. 


73. Intermediate boiler drum supports.— Where a boiler drum is supported at Intermediate points in its length 
at a distance greater than one internal diameter from the end of the parallel portion of the drum shell, the shell 
shall be thickened locally to the supports or so designed that when the local stress set up by the supports in the 
drum shell are added, algebraically to those caused by the internal steam pressure and supported loads, the 
maximum resultant stress does not exceed the permissible working stress at the working metal temperature.

75. General.— (|) The thickness ‘T’ specified in equation (4/0) of regulation !77 is the thickness of the end 
plate after manufacture and is applicable over the whole area of the end plate up to the point where, for ends of 
partially spherical shape, the dishing radius joins the corner radius; from this joint a gradual thinning is permissible 
up to maximum of l0 per cent of the thickness ‘T’ at the point where the corner radius joins the straight portion 
of flanged end plate. 


(2) A similar gradual thinning is permissible for end plates of semi-ellipsoidal shape. 


(3) This permissible reduction in thickness applies also to the flange for the manhole opening. In no case, however, 
when the end plate is butt welded to the drum shell, shall the thickness of the edge of the flange for connection to 
the shell be less than the thickness of an unpierced seamless shell of the same diameter and material, determined 
by equation (4/2).

(2) Welding consumables shall comply with the requirements of regulation 7 to 76.

welds) the drum shall be stress-relieved by heat treatment.

CHAPTER-5 
VALVES, GAUGES AND AUXILIARIES 
PART-I 


8l. Requisite Mountings, fittings and Auxiliaries. — () Every boiler shall be provided at least with the 
following, namely: - 


(a) Two safety valves, one of which may be a high steam and low water type safety valve and in no case 
the bore of the seat of the valve should be less than 9 mm. 


(b) Two means of indicating the water level; 
(c) A steam pressure gauge; 

(d) A steam stop valve; 

(e) A feed check valve; 


(f) One feed apparatus; 


Provided that for boilers fired by gaseous, liquid or solid fuels in suspension where heating surface 
exceeds 20 m’, shall be provided with minimum two feed apparatus which shall have a combined 
capacity of not less than the maximum continuous rating of the boiler: Provided further that for other 
boilers where residual heat is there even after fuel supply cut-off, two feed apparatus each having a 
capacity of not less than maximum continuous rating of the boiler shall be provided. (For boilers in 
battery see regulation 242); 


(g) A blow-down cock or valve; 
(h) Fusible plugs as provided under Regulation 236; 
(i) An attachment for Competent Person’s test gauge; 


(Gj) A manhole, where size and construction permit, and such mud holes or sight holes as are necessary 
for effectively cleaning the boiler. 


(2) In the case of boilers fitted with integral super heaters, an additional safety valve shall be fitted at the end 
of the super heaters outlet header. 


(3) Inthe case of boilers with no fixed steam and waterline, the fitting of such accessories that are manifestly 
not needed or used, such as water gauges, water columns and gauge cocks, may not be insisted upon. 


(4) In the case of a single boiler of the Shell type and not connected in a battery with other boilers, the heating 
surface of which does not exceed 02 m’, two independent source of power supply to the two feed 
apparatus shall not be necessary. 


(5) In the case of miniature boilers coming under Chapter-4, the Steam pressure gauge may be connected 
to the steam space or to a steam connection to the water column by a syphon tube or equivalent device 
that will keep the gauge tube filled with water and if brass or bronze composition is used, the minimum 
size of the syphon tube shall be 6 mm standard pipe size; for other materials the minimum inside diameter 
of the pipe or tube shall be 3 mm. 


(6) For Electrode boilers, see regulation 356. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 623 


(7) In case of boilers with reheaters, the reheaters shall be protected with one or more relieving devices of 
05% capacity (5% of the total capacity shall be located in the steam flow path between reheater outlet 
and first stop valve) to avoid over pressure in case of internal failures. 


82. Additional Requirements for Automatic Boilers.—(|)Every boiler which is provided with the appropriate 
water level and /or firing control, to allow for automatic working, shall comply with the following requirements: 


(a) In the event of failure of automatic control, boiler shall be capable of being brought under 
immediate manual control. 


(b) In those cases where the control and alarm devices are housed in chambers external to the boiler, 
the following shall apply, namely:- 


(i) The boiler shall have provision made for isolating the steam and water connections of the chambers 
from the boilers. Such isolating valves shall be capable of being locked in the open position and 
shall preferably be of the parallel slide type but if screw down stop valves are fitted, those on the 
water connection shall be mounted with the horizontal spindle to avoid the possibility of an air lock. 
The steam and water connections of the chambers shall be not less than 25 mm bore. In those cases 
where sequencing control water valves are fitted, the steam isolating valve may be omitted; 


(ii) The boiler shall be provided means to test operation of the control or alarm and to blow through 
separately the water connection and the chamber to prevent the accumulation of deposits. The 
means provided for flowing through shall be sequencing valves or equivalent devices so arranged 
that the water connection to the boiler cannot be shut off unless the drain connections to the chamber 
is open; 


(iii) The boiler shall have a drain system from the chambers which provides a visual indication of flow. 
Tundishes of adequate size, placed in a prominent position shall be used wherever practicable. 


(c) Where the boiler is provided with electrical equipment for water level and firing control, it shall have 
this equipment so designed that any fault in the circuits caused, both in the fuel and air supply, the boiler 
to be automatically shut off. Positive means requiring manual resetting shall be provided to cut off the 
fuel and air supplies to the boilers should there be a failure of electricity supply to water level and / or 
firing control equipment. All electrical conductors and equipment in connection with water level and 
firing controls shall be of adequate size and shall be properly insulated and protected against danger 
including adequate protection against the ingress of moisture and the effects of high temperature. 


(d) Where the evaporating capacity of the boiler is greater than 3700 Kg/h, it shall have automatic water 
level alarms and firing controls and can be tested regularly without altering the level of water in the 
boiler. The water level alarms may be incorporated in the automatic control system. With a perceptible 
water level which are arranged for automatic working and not intended for continuous supervision, shall 
be provided with an entirely independent and separately operated over-riding control in addition to the 
water level and firing control specified in sub-regulations (2) and (3). The over-riding control shall 
comply with the following requirements: 


(i) Cut off fuel supply to the burners or the fuel and air supply to solid fuel stoker and operate an 
audible alarm when the water level in the boiler falls to a pre-determined low water level; 


(ii) Be of the lock-out type and so arranged that control or its electrical circuit has to be manually reset 
before the boiler can be brought back into operation; 


624 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 
(iii) Be provided with its own entirely independent electrical control circuit. 
(e) Where mounted externally to the boiler, the over-riding control shall - 

(i) be provided with its own chamber; 
(ii) Comply with the requirements of clause (b). 

(2) Automatic water level control shall be as follows:- 
(a) float or displacer operated; or 
(b) operated by electrical probe or thermostat; or 
(c) operated by other approved principle to the satisfaction of the Inspecting Authority. 

The control equipment shall regulate the feed-water supply to the boiler in order to effectively 

maintain the level of water in the boiler between predetermined limits. 

(3) Automatic firing controls shall comply with the following requirements- 


(a) At all times they shall effectively control the supply of fuel and air to the combustion equipments. 


(b) They shall shut off the fuel supply to the burners or the fuel and air supply to the stoker under the 
following conditions:- 


(i) Flame failure or pilot flame failure in the cases of gas, oil or pulverised fuel fired boilers. 
This control shall be of the lockout type required to be manually reset; 

(ii) Failure to ignite the fuel at the burner within a pre-determined time. The control shall be 
of the lock-out type required to be manually reset; 

(iii) When the water level in a boiler falls below a pre-determined safe level. The control shall 
also cause an audible alarm. 

(iv) Failure of forced or induced draught fans or any automatic flue damper. 

(५) Increase in furnace pressure to a pre-determined value. 


Note: The above provisions shall not apply to once-through forced circulation boiler.

PART-II 


84. Castings.— (I)AlII castings shall be smooth, sound and free from flaws or other injurious defects. Variations 
in thickness at any part shall be gradual and substantial fillets shall be provided. 


(2) The body of a boiler mounting shall be connected to the boiler flange by a strong and stiff neck. In no case, 
the thickness of the neck of bronze mounting shall be less than 5 mm for sizes up to and including 9 mm 
bore or 6 mm size over |9 mm bore. 


85. Packing of Cocks.—(|)The bodies of all cocks except those for pressure gauges shall be packed with any 
non-asbestos heat resisting material and shall be of substantial design and those over 25 mm bore shall have 
special provision, other than the gland for securing the plug. 


(2) Water gauge column cocks may be any non-asbestos heat resisting material packed or solid plug type. 


86. Covers and Spindles.—(l) Valves of 38 mm bore and above directly connected to boilers, and other valves 
of 63 mm bore and over where fitted with a cover shall have such cover secured by bolts or studs and the screwed 
portion of the spindle shall be outside the stuffing box. All valves for superheated steam shall be fitted with an 
external screwed spindle. 


(2) (a) Where the covers of valves are secured by studs shall be screwed into the body with full thread for a 
length of at least one diameter. 
(b) The stud holes shall not penetrate into the pressure space of any casting. 


(3) Valves with screwed covers shall be fitted with suitable locking device to prevent rotation of the cover. 


87. Direction of Operation. —Valves shall be clearly marked to indicate the direction of flow. Valves directly 
connected to boilers shall be fitted with indicators to clearly show whether the valve is closed or open and all 
valves shall open by anti-clockwise rotation. 


88. Moving Parts.— The valves and spindles shall be efficiently guided and means shall be provided in every 
case to prevent them leaving their guides. The working parts shall have sufficient clearance to ensure freedom of 
movement under all conditions of service. 


89. Flanges.—() Flanges shall be in accordance with the tables for the appropriate pressure (Appendix-F). 
(2) Inthe case of safety valves the drilling, thickness and bolting of inlet flanges shall be in accordance with tables 
for the appropriate pressure and material and for the diameter of flange adopted. In the case of outlet flanges 


the pressure taken shall be the pressure on the outlet side of the valve. 


(3) For the purpose of determining particulars of flanges for blow down and scum pipe fittings, the design 
pressure of the fittings shall be assumed to be design pressure of the boiler. 


(4) All flanges shall be machined on the face, spot faced, or machined at the back, and the bolt holes shall be 
drilled. 


90. Valve Seatings— Where separate seats are fitted, they shall be efficiently secured and means shall be 
provided in every case to prevent the valves leaving their guides. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 627 


9. Chests and fittings in General.—(]) (a) All chests and fittings shall be smooth, sound and free from flaws, 
cracks or other injurious defects and after completion, the chests shall be hydraulically tested at minimum one and 
half times the maximum allowable working pressure of the valve for which they are intended. 

(b) Hydraulic test shall be made with water which may contain a corrosion inhibiter, with kerosene or with other 
suitable liquid provided its viscosity is not greater than that of water at a test temperature not above 52°C. 


(2) (a) (i) Valves may be fabricated from seamless steel pipes for pressures not exceeding 7.6 kg/cm?(g) and 

temperatures not exceeding 426°C.The welding shall conform to regulation 97 and valve chest shall be stress 
relieved after fabrication. 
(ii) Valves meant for use in pipe work may also be fabricated by welding from seamless steel pipes but no 
restriction as above regarding pressure and temperature shall apply to them provided the welding complies 
with all the relevant requirements of fusion welding such as stress relieving and radiographic inspection of the 
weld as prescribed in Chapter-4 of these regulations. 


(b) The maximum allowable working pressure of the chests shall be determined by equation (7/3), where the 
term ‘2 fE’ shall be substituted by the term ‘l.8 x f’. 


(3) The maximum allowable working pressure and the thickness of the bronze and cast Iron valve chests shall

PART-IV 


92. Special requirements for safety valves.— Safety valves, ordinary, high lift, and full lift, shall be so 
constructed that breakage of any part shall not obstruct the free and full discharge of steam from the boiler. 


93.ordinary Lift Safety Valve.— (.) A safety valve in which the valve head lifts automatically a distance of at 
least D/24 with an over-pressure not exceeding l0% of the set pressure. 

(2) There shall not be any mechanical stop which would prevent the valve head from being lifted a distance of at 
least D/8. D is the minimum bore of the body of seat. 


94.High Lift Safety Valve.— () A safety valve in which the valve head lifts automatically a distance of at least 
D/|2 with an over-pressure not exceeding !0% of the set pressure. 


630 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(2) There shall not be any mechanical stop which would prevent the valve head from being lifted a distance of 
at least D/8. D is the minimum bore of the body seat. 


95. Full Lift Safety Valve — () A safety valve in which the valve head lifts automatically a distance such that 
the area of discharge which limits the flow through the valve is between [00% and 80% of the minimum area at 
any section at or below the body seat. 

(2) This lift is achieved by a rapid opening within an over pressure not exceeding 5% of the set pressure.

saturated steam shall be calculated using the following equation;

(3) (a) The Total peak load evaporation of a boiler shall be calculated on the basis of evaporation not less 
than 30 kg/hr/m? of heating surface (exclusive of super heater and non-steaming economiser). 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


(0) In the case of Waste Heat Boilers, however, when the evaporation per square meter of the heating 
surface is certified by the manufacturers to be less than 30 kg. The minimum number of safety valves 
required may be calculated on the basis of the actual maximum evaporation of the boiler. 


97. Over Pressure of Safety Valves.— (|) The safety valves shall be so designed that they attain rated discharge 
capacity with the over pressure not greater than that given in regulation 93 to !95; provided that the safety valves 
which have a discharge area less than 80 per cent of the flow area, the over pressure at which the design lift is 
attained shall not exceed |0 percent of the set pressure. 

(2) For safety valves having discharge area 80 per cent of more of the flow area, the over pressure at which the 
design lift is attained shall not exceed 5 per cent of set pressure. 


98. Pressure Drop (Blow Down).— (|) The safety valves shall be reset at a pressure at least 2.5% below, but 
not more than 5% below the safety valves set pressure. 

(2) The 5% limit shall be increased to 6% for set pressures up to 25 kg/cm? and 0% for valves having a body seat 
bore less than 32 mm. 


99. Mountings of Safety Valves.—()(a)Safety valves shall be mounted without any intervening valve on pads 
or branches used for no other purpose. The axis of the valve shall be vertical. 

(b) The cross — sectional area of the bore of each pad or branch shall be at least equal to the area of the bore at the 
inlet of the safety valve, or where two or more safety valves are mounted on the same pad or branch, at least equal 
to the sum of the areas of the inlet bores of all the safety valves. 


(2) (a) Branches shall be as short as possible so as not to impair proper action of the safety valves or impose any 
undue stress on the branches at their point of attachment to the boiler. 

(b) Nothing shall obstruct free flow to the safety valve. Branches, particularly when full lift safety valves are 
mounted on them, should be radiused at the inlet. 

(c) The inlet and outlet flanges shall be drilled in accordance with the approximate table in Appendix-F for the 
diameters of flanges adopted. 


200. Openings in Shell.—() No accessories other than those integral with the Safety Valve shall obstruct the 
openings in the boiler shell. 
(2) Discharging steam shall have direct access to the safety valve without flowing through internal pipes. 


20l. Discharge Passage.—(l) (a) The safety valve discharge pipes shall comply with the requirements of sub- 
regulations (2) , (3) and (4) of this regulation. 
(b) The discharge pipe shall be as short and straight as possible and be fitted with open drain to prevent 
accumulation of water in the pipe. Suitable arrangement shall be provided in the discharge pipe system so that the 
discharge can readily be heard by the Boiler Attendant. 
(2) Where a waste steam-pipe is fitted the pipe and the passage leading to it shall have a cross-sectional area 
not less than the minimum combined area of the safety valves required by regulation 96. 


(3) For full lift valves, the area of waste steam pipe and passage leading to it shall have a cross-sectional area 
not less than twice “A”, or such area above this minimum as maybe required for valves having a higher 
approved constant, where “A”, “E” and “P” are as defined in regulation 96. 


(4) (a) The area of the discharge pipe from an economiser safety relief valve shall be at least twice the area of the 
valve seating. 
(b) Where the discharge from several economiser safety relief valves is connected to the main discharge pipe, 
the diameter of the main discharge pipe shall be designed to prevent accumulation of pressure due to the 
formation of steam under the particular conditions of temperature and pressure which may be applicable. 


202. Drainage—(|) For each enclosed safety valve chest, a means of draining shall be provided. 


632 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(2) The drain pipe shall be laid with a continuous downward gradient clear of the boiler to a place where the 
discharge is visible and cannot do injury to any person. 


203. Moving Parts.—(|) The valves and spindles shall be efficiently guided and means shall be provided in every 
case to prevent their lifting out of their guides. 

(2) The working parts shall have sufficient clearance to ensure freedom of movement under all conditions of 
service. The spindle shall not be fitted with a stuffing box. 


204. Bearings for Levers— _ () The bearings of the levers of lever valve shall be so designed as to allow free 
working of the valve under all condition of service. 

(2) Where the lever is mounted on pin bearings, the holes in the lever shall be bushed with non-corrodible metal, 
or the pins shall be of non-corrodible metal. 


205. Attachments of Weights and Springs.—(|) In a lever and weight safety valve, the weight shall be in one 
piece and attached to the lever in such a way that the safety valve cannot be over loaded. 


(2) (a) In the case of spring loaded safety valves, washers or ferrules shall be fitted under the adjusting screws so 
that the valves cannot be over loaded when under the steam. Interference with load on the spring after the 
safety valve has been adjusted shall be prevented by the fitting of a ferrule under the adjusting screw collar, 
or by using a lock nut on the adjusting screw which shall be further safe-guarded by means of a padlock or 
other suitable device. 

(b) Where springs are in tension, links or the suitable stops shall be fitted to prevent the spring being extended 
a greater amount than that corresponding to a valve lift of D/4. 


Where, D = diameter of valve seating. 


206. Easing Gear.— Safety valves shall be so arranged that they can be eased off seats when under pressure and 
the easing lever shall positively lift the valve. 


207. Lift— Safety valves shall be capable of being lifted a distance such that the area of the discharge edge 
shall not be less than the minimum aggregate area “A” in regulation 96. 


208. High and Low Water Alarms.— High and low water alarms shall be adjusted so that the alarm is sounded 
with the water level visible in the gauges. 


209. Final Settings.— Before leaving the maker’s works, each safety valve shall be adjusted to blow-off at the 
specified pressure. 


20. Adjustment of Safety Valve Set Pressure.— The set pressure of a safety valve may be adjusted using air or 
other gas as the test medium provided that the safety valve has been subjected previously to hydraulic test in 
accordance with the requirement of sub-regulation(l) of regulation 9]. 

2l.Change of Safety Valve Set Pressure.— The spring in a safety valve shall not be reset for any pressure more 
than 5% above or below that for which the valve is marked and the set pressure may be changed to the satisfaction 
of registering authority. 


22. Materials.—()(a)The springs shall be manufactured from steel made by the Acid Open Hearth or Electric 
Process and the Chemical composition shall be within the following limits:

(b) The manufacturers shall supply an analysis of each cast when required by the Inspecting Authority to do so. 
Should independent analysis be required, these shall be made at the rate of one per cent. 


(c) All springs shall be formed hot and suitably hardened and tempered. 


(d) All the springs above |6 mm bar diameter shall be formed hot and the springs below 6 mm bar diameter 
shall be formed hot or cold. The springs shall be suitably hardened and tempered. 


(2) Torsion bars shall be manufactured from steel which shall have a yield point of not less than 4 kg/mm/?. 


Note: Special steels developed by individual manufacturers may be accepted by the Chief Inspector of 


Boilers at their discretion. 


23. Dimensions.—(|) For ordinary lift valves, the compression or extension of safety valve springs required to 
load the valves to the set pressure shall not be less than one quarter of the diameter of the valve due consideration 
being given in the case of spring loaded level safety valves to the ratio of leverage. 

(2) The proportion of unloaded length to external diameter of the spring shall not exceed 4:]. 

(3) These requirements do not apply to full lift and high lift safety valves.

25. Test.—()The permanent set in the spring (defined as the difference between free height and height measured 
ten minutes after the spring has been compressed solid three additional times, after pre-setting at room 
temperature) shall not exceed 0.5% the free height. 


(2) Torsion bars shall not show a permanent distortion after being twisted to an angle fifty per cent in excess 


the working angle. 
26. Extension Springs.— Extension springs shall be made from round section wire. 


27. Number of Effective Coils — The number of effective or free coils in a compression or extension spring 
shall be determined from the following formulae:

28. Spacing of Coils —The space between the coils when the valve is lifted to /4" of its diameter, shall be not 
less than .6 mm for full lift valves and 0.8 mm for ordinary and high lift valves. 


29.Finishing of Ends.—Compression springs shall have their ends ground flat and smooth and at right angles to 
the axis of the springs over the full circumference so that when placed on end on a horizontal plane the springs 


will stand perpendicular.

PART-V 


220.Lever valves.— Where the valve is operated by means of a lever, whether hand or mechanically controlled, 
the lever shall be of ample strength and the bearings shall be so designed as to allow free working of the valve 
under all conditions of service. 


22. Steam stop valve.—(|) (a) The stop valve connecting the boiler or super heater to the steam—delivery pipe 
shall be located as near the outlet from the final superheater header as is convenient and practicable or in case of 
boilers without super-heaters as close as practicable to the drum. 

(b) Where two or more boilers are connected with a steam receiver or any other vessel, a steam stop valve shall 
be fitted between the boiler and such receiver or vessel. 


(2) (a)Steam stop valves shall be attached direct to the boiler shell or to suitable pads or stand blocks and the 
neck or the valve chest shall be reasonably short and of strong construction. 

(b) The steam stop valve may also be attached to a stand pipe, a connecting pipe or the super-heater header. 

(c) The attachment may be made by bolted flanges or butt-welded joints. Such butt- welded joints shall be suitably 
stress relieved, where necessary: 


Provided that in the case of a larger boiler in which it is proposed for the purpose of drainage or owing to 
obstruction to connect the steam—pipes to the steam stop valve at a higher level than would be obtained under this 
regulation, a vertical stand pipe not exceeding 5 diameters in height will be permitted between the stop valve and 
the boiler. Such stand pipes shall be of strong construction and of wrought iron, mild steel, or cast steel. The 
flanges of wrought or mild steel pipes shall be welded to the pipes, and there shall be no branch on the stand pipe 
for any other connection: 


Provided also that in the case of large boiler in which it is desired to fit a tee piece for the purpose of 
providing a branch connection between the stop valve and the boiler, such a tee piece may be so fitted, the tee 
piece shall be of strong construction, of wrought iron, mild steel, or cast steel and shall not exceed 22 diameters 
in height and a stop valve shall be fitted direct to each tee piece branch. 


(3) When two or more boilers are connected to a common steam main and there are no combined stop and 
isolating valves fitted to them an automatic isolating valve shall be compulsory. In the case of boilers fitted 
with welded pipes, fitting of an independent automatic isolating valve shall be compulsory. 


PART -VI 


222. Blow-down cock or valve and pipes.— (l) The blow-down cock or valve shall be of substantial construction. 
(2) The waste pipe attached to the cock or valve shall not be bound fast in arch or brick work and shall discharge 
at a point where there is no danger of injury to any person. 

(3) These pipes shall not be connected to a pipe common to another boiler. 

(4) The continuous blow-downs may, however be connected to a common header discharging freely to an 
adequately vented tank or sump. 

(5) The headers shall be of sufficiently large cross- section and the blow- off tank shall be provided with a vent 
pipe free from valves and of sufficient size to prevent accumulation of pressure. If, however, the tank is intended 
for collecting flash steam, a safety valve of adequate capacity shall be provided. 

(6) The tank shall be so located that all parts will be accessible for inspection. 


223 Blow-Down mountings.—(|) Each boiler shall be fitted with a suitable blow-down valve or cock placed at, 
or as near as practicable, to the lowest point of the boiler. 


(2) (a) For locomotive, vertical and marine type boilers, the valve or cock shall be attached direct to the boiler 
or to a suitable pad or stand pipe. 


638 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(b) For water tube boilers the valve or cock shall be outside the brick work with a substantial steel pipe 
between it and the mud box. 


(3) | For Cornish and Lancashire boilers, the cocks or valve may be attached to a cast steel elbow pipe of 
substantial section bolted to a suitable stand pipe or pad welded to the boiler. But cast iron elbow pipes shall not 
be permitted. 


224.Blow-Down Valve or Cock.—(]) Each valve or cock shall be fitted with a device which shall clearly indicate 
its open and closed positions, and any key or similar device for operating the valve or cock shall be such that it 
cannot be removed unless the valve or cock is fully closed. 

(2) The locking feather shall be secured by welding. 

(3) Cocks fitted with taper plugs shall be of the bolted cover type with separate packing glands. 


PART -VII 


225.Water Gauges.—(|)Every boiler shall have two means of indicating the water in it, out of which one shall be 
conventional gauge glass: 


Provided that in the case of boiler drums below 9[ cm diameter where there is difficulty in fitting two 
water gauges, two test cocks and a glass water gauge shall be fitted. 


(2) (a) The lowest visible part of the glass of the water gauge and lower test cocks shall be fixed at safe 
working level. 
(b) For locomotive type and vertical boilers this shall not be less than 50 mm above the highest part of the 
firebox roof plate. Minimum length of the visible portion of the gauge glasses shall be 200 mm. 
(c) The length may be increased depending upon the capacity of the boiler by the Inspecting Authority. 


(3) (a) Glass water gauges shall be so placed as to be easily seen and reached by the boiler attendant. 
(b) The fittings of glass water gauges and test cocks shall be of substantial make with large passage ways 
through them to facilitate cleaning. 
(c) The gauge cocks when open shall have their handles in a vertical direction and each handle at its junction 
with the plug shall be plainly marked with a deep line to indicate the direction of the passage way through the 
plug. 
(d) When detachable handle are provided arrangement shall be made to prevent incorrect fitting of the handles. 


226. Drains.— A drain cock or valve with a suitable discharge pipe shall be fitted to each water gauge. 


227. Protectors.—(|) Where tubular glass water gauges are fitted, substantial protectors shall be provided. 
(2) The glass shall be suitably treated to prevent splintering. 


228. Glass Size. —Tubular water gauge glasses shall be not less than 3 mm and not more than 9 mm outside 
diameter. 


229. Safety Devices.— Water gauge glass mountings shall be fitted with self-closing devices in the bottom arms 
and it is recommended that a similar device may be fitted in the top arm. 


230. Gauge Columns.—Where the gauges are mounted on a column, there shall be no connecting passage 
between the top and bottom arms of the column unless valves or cocks are fitted between the columns and the 
boiler. 


23. Isolating Cocks.— Where isolating cocks or valves connecting water gauge pipes to the boiler are fitted, 
they shall be not less than 25 mm bore and of the bolted cover type with separate packing gland.

PART - शा 


232. Pressure Gauges Dials.— () For pressure upto35 kg/cm? (g), pressure gauge dials shall be graduated in 
kg/cm?(g) from zero to twice the pressure as nearly as may be practicable. 


(2) For pressure exceeding 35 kg/cm*(g),the range of the graduation shall be from zero to one and a half times 
the maximum allowable working pressure, as nearly as may be practicable, but in no case shall the 
maximum graduation on the gauge be less than 70 kg/cm? (2). 


(3) The scale on the dial shall be clearly and permanently marked in kg/cm? (g). 
(4) The maximum allowable working pressure shall be marked in red on the dial of each pressure gauge. 


(5) (a) Where the gauge is compensated for a head of water between the gauge and the boiler connection, the 
amount of such compensation shall be marked on the dial. Pressure gauge shall be calibrated within an 
accuracy of +] percent. 

(0) Boiler pressure gauges shall not be less than 450 mm in diameter. 


(6) The travel of the pointer of the dial gauge shall not exceed 325°. 


233. Connections.— All pressure gauges shall be fitted with a syphon pipe and a cock or valve integral with, or 
adjacent to, the gauge in such manner that the gauge may be shut off and removed whilst the boiler is under steam. 


234. Gauge Cocks.— The handles of the gauge cocks shall be parallel to the pipes in which they are located when 
the cocks are open and marks shall be cut on the shank of the cock indicating open position. 


235.Test Connections- Competent Person’s Pressure Gauge Attachment.— (|)Every boiler shall be fitted with 
a valve or cock carrying in a vertical position a receiving screw for attachment of the Competent Person’s pressure 


gauge. 


(2) The receiving socket shall be tapped for M/20 x .5 metric threads and shall be fitted with an easily removable 
cap. 


PART -IX 


236. Fusible Plugs.—(l)Fusible plugs shall be of sufficient height and fitted in such a position as to give early 
protection to all parts of the boiler liable to damage by the direct application of furnace heat in the event of 
shortness of water. 


Note: For example - In Lancashire boilers the fusible plugs shall be in the crowns of the furnaces from 
305 mm to 457 mm in front of the brick work fire bridge. 


(2) (a) On boilers having wet back reversing chamber, a minimum of two fusible plugs shall be fitted; one 
on the crown of the reversing chamber and the other on one of the tube plates. On boilers not having wet back 
reversing chamber, at least one fusible plug shall be provided on the front end tube plate. 

(b) The plug shall be fitted in such a way that in the event of fusion of the plug, the pressure inside the boiler shall 
push the pellets out. 


237.Type.— (l) Fusible plugs shall consist of an outer body with a central conical passage. 


(2) The smallest part to be not greater than 3 mm for plugs suitable for pressures up to 7 kg/cm?(g) and not 
greater than 0 mm for plugs for pressures exceeding 7 kg/cm?(g). 


(3) The passage shall be closed by a plug secured by an annual lining of fusible alloy so that the plug may drop 
clear if the lining melts. 


640 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(4) The portion of the body carrying the fusible metal shall preferably be detachable from the base to allow of 
easy replacement without removing the whole fitting from the boiler. 


238. Material —(l) The non-fusible portions of the plug shall be of bronze except where the nature of the boiler 
water precludes the use of non-ferrous material. 


(2) The fusible metal shall be of an alloy melting readily at a temperature not less than 66°C in excess of the 
saturated steam temperature at the design pressure of the boiler. 


239. Attachment to Boiler.— (|) Wherever practicable, fusible plugs shall be screwed into the boiler plates from 
the water side. 


(2) The screwed portion shall have threads of Whitworth form not more than I! per 25 mm. 


PART -X 
240.Feed Valves.— (l) Feed check valves shall be of the non-return type. 


(2) Where the valve is not of screw-down non-return type, a separate screw-down valve shall be provided. 

(3) The discharge from the feed check valve or from the internal feed pipe (if provided) shall be above low 
water level and in the case of Lancashire and Cornish boilers, shall be at least [52 cm beyond the fire 
bridge: 


Provided that the aforesaid restriction regarding the position of feed discharge level shall not apply in the 
case of water tube boilers. 


24. Operating Position. — Feed check valves or regulating valves shall be so arranged as to enable them to be 
satisfactorily operated from the boiler floor. 


242. Requirements as to Feed Apparatus in certain cases.— In the case of a battery of boilers connected to a 
common feed range, the requirements ofregulation!8! in respect of the number of feed apparatus shall be 
considered to have been fulfilled provided a total supply of feed water, not less than the combined maximum 
continuous rating of all active boilers can be maintained even if any one of the sources of power supply fails.

CHAPTER -7 
PIPES AND FITTINGS 
249. Pipes.—(|)(a) Steam-pipes may be of carbon steel, cast steel, alloy steel and nickel alloys. 
(b) Pipes may be solid drawn (cold or hot finished), butt welded or electric resistance welded. 


(2) Where, material used is in conformity with the code of the country of manufacture and in accordance 
with provisions of these regulations, the permissible stress figures specified in the code at different 
temperatures may be accepted in lieu of figures computed from the data required to be furnished under 
regulation 256 in any of the following cases, namely:- 


(a) Where a certificate is furnished from the Inspecting Authority to the effect that the steel complies 
with requirements of the steel grade (to be specified by the Inspecting Authority) and that the 
permissible stress for the working condition as allowed for in the code of the country of manufacture 
falls within the permissible limits under these regulations. 


(b) Where the basis upon which these stresses have been arrived at is made available and such basis is 
not found as to give rise to stresses higher than those permissible under the regulations. 


(c) Where pipes have to be fabricated by longitudinal fusion butt electric arc welding of plates rolled to 
shape, the limits provided for butt welded pipes in Table 7/4 under regulation 255 shall not apply. 
(d) The requirements other than those relating to the minimum thickness of shell for fusion butt welding 
provided in Chapter-2 shall be applicable to such pipes. 


(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in Chapter-7, the hydraulic test for pipes in maker's premises may 
be dispensed with by the Inspecting Authority: 


Provided that these pipes have been fully tested by non-destructive examination by radiographic 
or ultrasonic techniques: 


Provided further that in the case of pipes having internal diameter | 000 mm and more, the plates 
used for the manufacture of pipes and the long seam welds of pipes are fully tested by non-destructive 
examination like ultrasonic or radiographic testing and the soundness of pipes both in the parent material 
and in the weld is established in the maker's premises; and the whole component of the pipes, after 
completion of any further fabrication and erection at site, are hydraulically tested at a pressure not less 
than .5 times the maximum allowable working pressure of the piping system: 


Provided also that in the event of detection of any defect after conducting hydraulic test of these 
pipes at site, it shall be the responsibility of the manufacturer to repair or replace the defective pipes, as 


may be deemed necessary by the Inspecting Authority.

250.Material of steel pipes.—(|) (a) The pipes shall be made from steel made by an Open Hearth or Electric 
Process or by any of the Oxygen Processes. 

(b) Hot finished seamless pipes may, however, be made of Bessemer Steel. 

(c) Bessemer Steel shall not be used for pressures exceeding 2] kg/cm? or temperatures exceeding 260°C and If 
the Bessemer process is used, the steel shall be made by a manufacturer approved by Inspecting Authority. 

(d) When pipe is used for temperatures exceeding 399°C the steel shall be of non-segregated or fully killed type. 


(2) Carbon and alloy steel pipes shall not be used for design temperatures exceeding those given in Table 
2/\ of regulation30. 


(3) For design temperature over 427°C, precaution shall be taken to ensure that the surface condition of the 
pipe is suitable for such requirements. 


(4) (a) The material from which seamless pipes are made, shall conform to appropriate specifications of 
pipes as in regulation 49 and electric resistance welded pipes are made, shall conform to the appropriate 
specification of tubes as in regulation 30. 

(b) The materials from which butt welded pipes are to be made shall conform to the requirements of 
Table 7/3 under regulation 253. 


25. Condition of pipes. —()AII pipes shall be commercially straight, free from longitudinal seaming, grooving, 
blistering or other injuries surface marks and the ends of the pipes shall be cut square.

254. Method of manufacture, heat treatment and marking.— (l) On completion of any work which involves 
heating, whether for hot bending of the pipe or for any other similar purpose, the pipe shall be carefully annealed. 


(2) (a) The cold drawn seamless carbon steel pipes and welded carbon steel pipes shall be supplied in 


normalised condition. 


(b) Hot finished seamless carbon steel pipes shall be supplied in hot finished condition or in normalised 


condition at the option of the manufacturer. 


(c) The seamless alloy steel pipe either cold finished or hot finished and welded pipes shall be supplied 


in normalised and tempered condition. 


(d) By agreement between the users and the manufacturer, the pipes may be delivered in a condition 
other than normalised and tempered condition in which case they shall be suitable for subsequent 


manipulation and the user shall be informed of the heat-treatment necessary to give required properties. 


(3) (a) (0) Pipe bending and forming (reducing or swaging) operation shall be done by any hot or cold method 
and to any radius which shall result in a surface free from cracks, buckles or other defects as determined by 
the method of inspection specified in the design. 
(ii) A post bending or post forming heat treatment for carbon steel material is required with a nominal wall 
thickness in excess of !9 mm unless the bending or forming operation are performed and completed at 
normalizing temperatures, where no further heat treatment is required. 
(iii) The heat treatment where required, shall be normalised or stress relieved, as the case may be. 


(b) A post bending or post forming heat treatment shall be required for all ferritic alloy steel material with 


nominal pipe size !00 mm and larger or with a nominal thickness (3 mm or greater. 


(c) (i) If hot bending or forming is performed the material shall receive normalize and temper or tempering 


heat-treatment as required by the design. 


(ii) For cold operation, tempering heat-treatment shall be applied. 


(4) Marking shall be carried out in accordance with regulation 329.

PART-II 


258. Flanges of carbon steel pipes—(l)The material for carbon steel flanges, where forged, cast or cut from the 
plates (excluding branches forged integral with the pipes) shall be made of steel produced by an Open Hearth or 
Electric process or any of the Oxygen processes. 


(2) Carbon steel flanges shall not be used for temperatures exceeding 454°C and such flanges shall be 
made without a weld and free from lamination or other defects secured by welding. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 655 


(3) Blank flanges shall be of mild steel or cast steel and shall be not less in thickness than the flanges to 
which they are attached. The material shall comply with the requirements specified in relevant 
regulations of chapter-2 or Chapter-4 of these regulations. 


259. Flanges of alloy steel pipes.— (l) (a) The material for alloy steel flanges where forged, cast or cut from 

plates (excluding branches forged integral with the pipes), shall be made from the steel produced by an 
Open Hearth or Electric process. 
(b)Flanges shall be made without a weld and shall be free from lamination or other defects. 

(c) The material of alloy steel flanges shall comply the provisions of regulation 30. 

(d) The material for flanges shall be similar to that of the pipes to which they are to be attached. 

(e) The flanges are to be so designed that the total stress induced in them does not exceed the maximum 
permissible stress as per criteria mentioned in regulation 70. 


(2) Blank flanges of alloy steel shall be not less in thickness that the flanges to which they are to be 
attached and the material shall be similar to that of the flanges. 


260.Non-ferrous flanges.— () The material for non-ferrous flanges shall be of bronze. 
(2) The chemical composition shall comply with the requirements of clause (iv) of sub-regulation (/) of regulation 
83. 

(3) When flanges are attached to copper pipes by brazing, they shall be secured in such additional way like forming 
a conical bore in the flange so that the resistance to withdrawal from the flange does not depend wholly on the 
brazing. 


26l. Screwed on flanges.— (l) Where flanges are secured by screwing, the screw thread on the pipes and in the 
flanges shall be arranged to end at a point just inside the back of boss of the flange and after the flange has been 
screwed on, the pipe shall be expanded into the flange by a roller expander. 

(2) Such screwed and expanded flanges may be used for steam for a maximum allowable working pressure of 
3.5 kg/cm? (g) and maximum temperature of 399 °C and for feed for a maximum allowable working pressure of 
42 kg/cm? (2). 


262. Loose flanges.— (|) (a)Loose flanges may be used where the joints are made by metal faces integral with 
ends of the pipes and alternatively these joints may be welded or seal welded. 
(b) The loose flanges shall conform to the table given in Appendix-F. 


(2) Where the joint is formed by integral flanges, after machining these shall be not less in thickness than the 
designed thickness of the pipe as calculated by Equation (7/2) 


263. Welded on flanges.— (l) Where flanges are welded on, the welding shall be done by the oxy-acetylene or 
metal arc process; the latter with covered electrodes which shall comply with regulations 7] to76.

The design conditions for each type are as follows:

(3) Type |,2,3,4 and 5 Carbon Steel types flanges welded on by the metal arc process shall 
have the welds stress relieved where the design depth of the weld recess is greater than 20 mm and all 
welds joining flanges to alloy steel pipes shall be stress relieved. 


(4) Where type | flanges are attached by oxy-acetylene welding, the welds shall be normalised in accordance 
with the following requirements: 


(a) Welds in mild steel pipes shall be normalised by heating the metal to a temperature between 
900° and 950°C, the temperature then being maintained for not less than two minutes for pipes up to and 
including !02 mm bore, and for not less than five minutes for pipes over !02 mm bore. 

(b) Welds in pipes made from the alloy steel shall be normalised by heating the metal to a 
temperature between 925° and 975°C, the temperature then being maintained for not less than two 
minutes for pipes up to and including !02 mm bore, and for not less than five minutes for pipes over l02 
mm bore. 

(c) The higher temperatures of between 950° and 975°C, shall be used for alloy steels having a 
carbon content up to and including 0.2 percent and the lower temperatures of between 925° and 950°C 
shall be used for alloy steels having a carbon content of more than 0.i2 percent. 

(d) After normalising the joint shall be covered with a suitable muff or asbestos cloth to ensure 
slow and even cooling. 

(९) The normalising of welds in pipes up to !02 mm bore may be carried out with welding 
flames the temperature being judged with the aid of a colour card, or measured by means of one or more 
thermo-couples or an optical pyrometer. 

(f) The normalising of welds in pipes over !02 mm bore shall preferably be carried out in a 
portable pipe normalising furnace or muffle, the temperature being measured by means of one or more 
thermo-couples or an optical pyrometer. 

(g) The width of the zone to be heat treated to the specified temperature shall extend at least |3 
mm on either side of the weld reinforcement. 


(5) The procedure to be observed in the stress relieving of welds shall be in accordance with regulation 23 
and stress relieving shall be carried out by any of the following methods:- 


(a) (i) Local heating using a portable muffle furnace, induction coils or other suitable appliances and 
due care shall be taken to apply heat uniformly over the area to be treated. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण

(ii) The use of procedures not providing adequate control such as manual operated gas torches are

267. Tests for Class I pipelines—(l) Where the completed pipelines are not tested by the application of 
hydraulic pressure, the welds shall be subjected to the following inspection procedure, namely: - 


(a) (i) For piping of over 02 mm bore, all butt-welds shall be subjected to non-destructive 
examination by radiographic or other approved methods. 
(ii) The entire circumference of the first five welds made by each welder shall be non- 
destructively examined and if these are found to be satisfactory and Competent Person is 
satisfied with the welding techniques, methods of control and supervision employed, 
relaxation in the extent of non-destructive examination may be considered, but this 
relaxation shall in no case permit the non-destructive examination of less than one-third of 
the circumference of each of remaining welds made by the welder concerned. 


(0) For piping of !02 mm bore and under, but not less than 38 mm bore, five percent of the 
butt-welds made by each welder with a minimum of two welds per welder, selected at 
random shall be subjected to non-destructive examination by either radiographic or other 
approved methods or may be cut out for visual examination and bend tests. 


(c) For piping of less than 38 mm bore, special tests are not normally required but two percent 
of the welds by each welder on a pipeline may be cut out from the pipe-line for visual 
examination and bend tests. 


(2) Where the completed pipelines are tested by the application of hydraulic pressure, the welds 
shall be subjected to the following inspection procedure, namely:- 


(a) For piping of over !02 mm bore, ten percent of the welds made by each welder on a pipeline 
with a minimum of two welds per welder, selected at random, shall be subjected to non- 
destructive examination by radiographic or other approved methods. 

(0) For piping of 02 mm bore and under, but not less than 38 mm bore, two per cent of the 
welds made but each welder on a pipeline with a minimum of one weld per welder, selected 
at random, shall be subjected to non-destructive examination by radiographic or other 
approved methods or may be cut out for visual examination and bend tests. 

(c) For piping of less than 38 mm bore, special tests are not normally required, but two percent 

of the welds by each welder on a pipeline may be cut from the pipeline for visual examination 


and bend tests. 


268. Tests for Class II pipelines.—(])AIl pipelines under this classification shall be subjected to 
hydraulic test on completion of erection. 


(2) (a) On completion of the first ten production welds made by each welder, one of the welds shall 
be cut out for test purposes or alternatively, the welder shall prepare a test specimen made up 
of two similar lengths of piping welded in a position as closely representative of a selected 
production weld as is practicable. 

(b) The test specimen shall be subjected to visual examination and bend tests. 


(3) Two percent of the remainder of the welds made by each welder shall be selected at random 
and cut out for test purpose, or, alternatively the welders shall prepare a test specimen made up 
of two similar lengths of piping welded in a position as closely representative of a selected 
production weld as far as practicable and the test specimen shall be subjected to visual 
examination and bend tests.

(a) For piping of over !02 mm bore, five per cent of the welds made by each welder on a

(0) For piping ०02 mm bore and under, one per cent of the welds made by each welder on a

non-destructive examination by radiographic or other approved technique. 


269. Re-tests.— (l) If any test specimen is unsatisfactory, two further weld specimen for re-test shall be 
selected from the production welds and subjected to tests. 
(2) In the events of failure of any of the re-test specimens, the production welds carried out by this welder 
subsequent to the previous tests shall be subject of special consideration. 


270. Socket weld joints.— (() Socket weld joints may be used with carbon and low alloy steel pipes not 
exceeding 60.3 mm. outside diameter. 
(2) Such welds shall not be used where fatigue, severe erosion or severe corrosion is expected to occur. 
(3) The maximum allowable working pressure of the socket weld fittings shall be determined in 
accordance with equation (7/l) (regulation 256). 
(4) The thickness of the socket weld fittings shall not be less than [4 times the nominal thickness of pipe 
and the material shall be compatible with the associated piping. 


27|. Butt welded joints— (l) Butt welded joints as applicable shall be subjected to non-destructive 
examination by radiographic, radioscopy or other approved methods such as ultrasonic testing including 
phased array ultrasonic testing, magnetic particle inspection or liquid dye penetrant inspection. 


(2) When radioscopic examination is to be performed in lieu of radiography on welded components, 
the following requirements shall be met:- 


(a) A written procedure shall be submitted for approval to the Inspecting Authority which shall contain the 
following:- 


(i) material and the thickness range; 
(ii) equipment qualifications; 
(iii) test object scan plan; 
(iv) radioscopic parameters; 
(v) image processing parameters; 
(vi) image display parameters; 
(vii) image archiving requirements; 
(viii) accept-reject criteria (code reference); 
(ix) performance evaluation; 
(x) | Operator identification. 


(b) The system shall be aided with an image processor to enhance the quality of the radioscopic images and 
system performance quality shall exhibit- 
(i) a thin section contrast sensitivity of 3%; 
(ii) a thick section contrast sensitivity of 2%; 
(iii) a spatial resolution of 3 line pairs per mm;. 
(iv) IQI sensitivity - 2% of the joint thickness when wire IQI's are to be used, the wire diameter 
axis shall be oriented along the axis of the least sensitivity of the system. 


(c) Radioscopes are to be properly marked to co-relate with particular part of joint represented. 
(d) The radioscopic examination data shall be recorded and stored on videotape, magnetic disk or optical 


disk or any other electronic storage device at the maker's plant for a sufficient period after the date of 
radioscopic examination as specified by the Inspecting Authority, Efficient radioscopic examination 


660 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


record recall shall be made available at any time over the record retention period and shall be traceable 
to the test objects. 


(e) When repair has been performed as a result of radioscopic examination, the repaired areas shall be 
re-examined using the same radioscopic technique to evaluate the effectiveness of the repair. 


(f) To aid in proper interpretation of the radioscopic examination data, the details of the technique used 
shall accompany the data. As a minimum, the information shall include the approved procedure 
requirements and system performance test data

272. Wrought Bends.— The minimum wall thickness at any point on the pipe bend shall be determined according 
to either of the following methods, namely :- 


(a) ()The minimum wall thickness at any point in the finished bend shall not be less than required by 
equation (7/2) or (7/4) given in regulation 256. 


(ii) The bend thinning allowance shall be selected based on the manufacturing process to ensure the 
minimum thickness requirements after bending. 

(iii) The bend thinning allowance thus selected is to be provided on all parts of the cross section of the 
pipe circumference without any detrimental effects on the final product.

274.Steel butt Welded fittings.— (.) (a) Branches, bosses and drain pockets welded to the pipes shall conform 
to the requirements of regulations 48 to 52. 
(b) Branches shall not be welded to any main at an angle of less than 60°.

(b) Such reinforcement may take the form of multiple radial plates of ‘horse shoe’ form or the form of 
collars or other reinforcement, approved by the Inspecting Authority or Chief Inspector as the case may 
be, applied to or around the junction between the branch and the main.

275. Blow-down pipes — () Blow-down pipes which can be subjected to full boiler pressure shall be considered 
as saturated steam-pipes at that pressure. 


(2) Blow-down pipes which cannot be subjected to full boiler pressure shall be considered as saturated 
steam-pipes at half the design pressure of the boiler. 


276. Valves chests — (|) Chests of stop-valves, isolating valves, reducing valves, steam traps, etc., forming parts 
of wrought steel main steam piping when for use with saturated steam up to a gauge pressure of llkg/cm?(g)or a 
temperature of 204°C may be made of cast iron, cast steel or wrought steel in accordance with the requirements 
of regulation 9]. 


(2) When superheated steam is used above 204°C or when pressures are above | |kg/cm? gauge, such chests 
shall be made of cast or wrought steel or other approved material in accordance with the requirements of 
regulation 9]. 

PART-VI 
277. Materials in the construction of steam receivers, separators, catch waters , accumulators and similar 
vessels.—(l)Material for plates, bars and sections used in the construction of steam receivers, separators, catch 
waters, accumulators and similar Vessels shall comply in all respects with the requirements of relevant regulations 


of Chapters-2 and 4, depending upon the mode of construction. 


(2) Branches, bosses and drain pockets may be solid forged, fabricated by fusion welding, machined 
from solid bars or made from tubes. 


(3) Materials for flanges shall comply with the appropriate provisions of regulation 258. 
(4) Forgings shall comply with the requirements of regulations 58 to 62 


(5) Steel castings for shells or pressure parts of shell shall comply with regulations 5! to 57. 


676 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


278. Construction and workmanship.—(|)Shell ends formed separately from the shell may be dished or flat or 
the ends of the shell may be forged down and closed by manhole doors or by plugs or branches welded in. 


(2) (a) G) Each dished end shall be made from one rolled plate. 
(ii) If this is impracticable, owing to the large diameter, the dished end plate may be made from two 
plates fusion butt welded together and in such cases, the line of weld shall be parallel to the horizontal 
axis of the vessels and the weld shall be radiographed after forming. 
(iii) The shape of dished end shall conform to the requirements of regulation |74. 
(iv) Dishing end peripheral flanging shall be done by machine. 
(v) Cold flanging shall not be adopted. 
(vi) All plates which have been dished, flanged or locally heated shall afterwards be efficiently heat 
treated for the purpose of relieving internal stresses, unless during the last stage of manufacture, they 
have been uniformly heated throughout to a suitable temperature. 
(vii) Care shall be taken to see that the flanges are cylindrical, of good surface and free from local 
irregularities. 


(b) Where flats are pressed in dished ends for the attachment of connections, they shall be formed 
with an ample radius at the junctions of the flat and curved surfaces and shall be free from sharp 
corners and tool marks. 


(c) Dished ends shall be attached to the cylindrical part of the shell by one of the following methods: 

(i) Welding with butt Joints of the Single or Double U or V Type; where the internal diameter of 
the shell is 60 mm or over, the joints shall in all cases, be welded from both sides of the plate. 

(ii) Where the internal diameter of the shell is less than 6]0 mm the joints may be welded from one 
side only, when efficient welding from inside is considered impracticable. 


(iii) In the construction of unfired boilers when the dished ends do not form part of the heating 
surface, cold spun dished ends conforming to IS: 2825 may be used. 


(3) (a) Flat ends shall be of forged steel or plate steel and shall be welded to the cylindrical part of the 
shell or bolted to flanges which shall be attached to the cylindrical part of the shell in accordance 
with regulation 263. 


(b) The attachment of flat ends shall be by one of the methods shown in figure7/35, 7/36, 7/37 and 7/38 
of this chapter. 


(c) When ends are attached as shown in figure7/38, welding shall be from both side of the shell plate 
wherever practicable and where welding is done from one side only, care shall be taken to ensure 
full penetration using backing strips.

279. Access to Shells.— (l) At least one manhole shall be provided to allow access for thorough cleaning and 
inspection, except that where the shell is too small to permit entry, cleaning and inspection openings of 
sufficient size and number shall be provided. 

(2) When there is an elliptical opening in the cylindrical part of the shell, the minor axis shell, wherever 
practicable be parallel to the longitudinal axis of the shell. 


678 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


280. Compensating rings to openings and doors.— The material, construction and workmanship of 
compensating rings and doors shall comply with the relevant provisions of Chapters 2, 3 and I2. 


28. Branches and other connections.—(|) (a) Connections to shell shall be made by means of branches, 
pressed plate saddles, forged pads or bosses or where the thickness of the shell is sufficient to allow suitable 
surface to be obtained, connections may be attached directly to the shell, provided that the minimum thickness 
at the hole in the shell is not less than the thickness required for the maximum allowable working pressure 
and temperature considering the shell as being unpierced and that the diameter of the hole does not exceed 
the maximum diameter of an uncompensated hole as defined in regulation 4] and 79. 

(b) Studs for securing such connections shall have a full thread holding in the shell for a length of at least one 
diameter and the stud holes shall not penetrate the whole thickness of the shell. 

(c) All holes for bolts and studs in branches, saddles and forged pads shall be drilled. 

(d) Where such connections are secured by welding alone, a minimum of two runs of metal shall be deposited 
at each weld, except for seal welds. 

(e) Each run of weld metal shall be thoroughly cleaned and free from slag before the next run is deposited. 
(f) The final finish of the welds shall be such that change of section from shell to branch is gradual and free 
from sharp notches. 

(g) Where the diameter of the shell is 60 mm and over, welding shall be from both sides of the plate. 

(h) Where the internal diameter of the shell is less than 60 mm, external and internal welds shall be applied 
unless it is considered that efficient welding from both sides is impracticable. 

(0) This does not apply to the methods of attachment shown in Fig.7/40 and 7/4] in which the welding shall 
always be from both sides.
