(2) (a) Branches of not more than 38 mm nominal bore may be screwed into the shell with a taper thread and seal 
welded, provided that the thickness of the shell is sufficient to allow for a length of thread equal to the diameter 
of the branch. 

(b) Where the thickness of the shell is not sufficient for the purpose, a boss may be welded on so that the total 
thickness of the boss and shell is at least equal to the required length of thread. 
(c) Methods of attachment of such bosses are shown in Figs. 7/65 to 7/69. 


(3) (a) Branches, pressed plate saddles, forged pads of bosses shall be secured to the shell by one of the following 
methods,- 
(i) Welding; 
(ii) Screwing and Seal Welding. 


(b) (i) Methods of attachment secured by welding are shown in Figs. 7/40 to 7/64 of this chapter. 
(ii) Branches may be provided with flanges for ordinary bolted joints. Joints of special type may also be 
used. 
(iii) Flanges for ordinary bolted joints shall be in accordance with the appropriate table of Appendix-F 
and shall be forged solid with the branches or attached in accordance with regulation 263. 
(iv) They shall be machined on the jointing and bolt bearing surfaces. 


(c) (i) Where pressed plate saddles are used, they shall be formed to bed closely to the shell and shall be 
machined on the face adjoining the connection and machined or flame cut by machine on the edges. 
(ii) The studs for the attachment of the connection, if screwed through the saddle, shall each be fitted with 
a nut on the inside. 
(iii) Where the stud holes do not penetrate through the saddle, the length of the screwed portion of the 
stud in the plate shall be not less than the diameter of the stud. 


(d 


wm 


The join faces of all pads shall be machined. 


(e 


wa 


(i) The pads shall be sufficiently thick to allow the drilling of stud holes for connections without the inner 
surface being pierced. 

(ii) The length of the screwed portion of the stud in the pad shall be not less than the diameter of the stud. 
(iii) Method of attachment of pads secured by welding are shown in Fig. 7/70 to 7/76 of this chapter but 
where pads of the type shown in Fig. 7/70 are used, they shall be formed to bed closely to the shell.

(i) Tapped bosses of not more than 38 mm standard pipe welded to the shell, may be used for maximum 
allowable working pressure not exceeding 4 kg/cm? (9) and design temperatures not exceeding 343°C. 
(ii) Such bosses shall have taper threads. 

(iii) Methods of attachment of bosses secured by welding are shown in Fig. 7/65, 7/69 of this chapter 


(i) All welded attachments other than flange connections shall be by the metal arc process and the 
electrodes used shall comply with the requirements of regulations 7 to 76. 

(ii) Where tack welds are used, they shall be sound and unless cut out, shall be carefully fused into the 
main runs. 


All parts secured by welding shall be effectively heat treated after completion of all welding and before 
hydraulic test. 


282. Shell joints .— (l)Fusion Welded Shells shall be classified as follows: 


(a) Class I—No limit to scantlings. 
(b) Class I] - When none of the following limits exceeds:— 


(i) maximum allowable working pressure- 35 kg/cm? (g) 

(ii) product of maximum allowable working pressure and internal diameter in centimeters — 
3750. 

(iii) design temperature — 343°C. 


(c) Class III — When none of the following limits exceeds:— 


(i) maximum allowable working pressure -7.4 kg/cm? (g) 

(ii) product of maximum allowable working pressure and internal diameter in centimeters — 
940. 

(iii) design temperature — 7°C. 


(2) Fusion welds, preparation of seams, the method of formation of cylindrical shells including heat treatment 


after bending, method of making welded seams, types of welded joints, test plates and circularity of 
shells, all shall conform to the requirements of Chapter -4, except for the following, namely;- 


(a) (0) Whenever practicable, seams shall be welded from both sides of the plate. Additional runs of metal 
shall be deposited at both surfaces of the welded seams to build up to a thickness I0 per cent greater than 


thickness of the plate. 


(ii) The surfaces of welds wherever carried out on both sides shall be ground smooth and flush with the 


respective surfaces of the plates. 


(iii) Where the seam is welded from one side only, these provisions shall apply to the exposed of the surface 


weld. 


(b) Tests for Class I fusion welded seams shall comply with the requirements of the relevant regulations 
of Chapter -4. 


(c) Tests for Class If fusion welded seams shall comply with the requirements of those of Chapter-!2, 
except that an additional provision for one micro and macro examination shall be made. 


(9) Tests for Class III fusion welded seams shall comply with the requirements of Chapter -2. 


(९) Class I and Class II shells shall be effectively stress-relieved by heat treatment when the wall thickness 
exceeds 20 mm or the carbon content exceeds 0.25% or the pipes are made of alloy steel. 


688 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


283. Determination of maximum allowable working pressure.—(|) (a) The maximum allowable working 
pressure of shells shall be determined as per the following formula: - 


2f E (T - 0.75) 
PS 42222202 
D + (T-—0.75) 
Where, 
T is thickness in mm, 
D is maximum internal diameter in mm, 
P is maximum allowable working pressure in kg/cm? (g), 
f is maximum permissible working stress as prescribed in 
regulation !70 or 256 whichever is applicable in kg/cm? at the working metal 
temperature, 
E is Efficiency factor for fusion welded shells as given in table below, 
is |.00 for seamless shells or shells made from seamless tubes, 
is Efficiency of ligaments between holes or openings in shell expressed as a 
fraction.

286. Bronze screwed and socketed joints and mountings and fittings of bronze.— 
(.) Mountings and fittings of bronze up to 76 mm diameter may be attached directly to steel pipes by screwing, 
when the pressures and temperatures do not exceed 8.5 kg/cm? (g) and 225°C respectively; where tapered threads 
are employed, such joints may be used for pressures not exceeding 7.6 kg/cm? (2). 
(2) Bronze fittings above 76 mm diameter shall be of flanged construction. 


287. Reducing valve.— Where a reducing valve is installed in a pipe line, the pipe line and accessories on the low 
pressure side of the reducing valve shall be protected by a suitable safety valve or valves so adjusted as to permit 
the steam to escape as soon as the maximum allowable working pressure is exceeded or by a suitable appliance 
for cutting off automatically the supply of steam as soon as the maximum allowable working pressure is exceeded. 


288. Flexibility.—()The pipe shall be arranged so that the system is sufficiently flexible to absorb the whole of 
their expansion and the imposed movement of the connected equipment without the actual expansion stress (SE) 
exceeding the allowable stress range (SA) determined as per the following equation,—

3. The sum of the longitudinal stress due to pressure, weight and other sustained load including 
bending stresses caused by external loads shall not exceed the allowable stress in the hot conditions

be added to the term 0.25 SH, in the above formula for determining the allowable stress range SA.

(2) Where practicable, the requisite flexibility shall be provided in the layout of the pipes without having 
recourse to special expansion bends or expansion joint except for the safety valves discharge piping. 
Where lack of space or other considerations prohibits the use of this method, expansion fittings like 
expansion joints or the bellows type of corrugated pipes may be used provided that the limitations 
imposed by maximum shall be given to the design of anchors, guides and ties to ensure that they 
adequately protect the expansion fitting and accommodate the additional loads due to pressure.

(b) the piping system can be adjudged adequately by comparison with previously analysed system.

289. Pipe work supports.— () All pipe work shall be adequately supported in order to permit free movement for 
expansion and contraction, and the amount of such movement shall be proportioned throughout the whole of any 
main by the provision of anchors at suitable points. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 695 


(2) Where pipes may be subject to vertical movement, spring supports designed to carry the load under all 
conditions shall be provided. 

(3) Points of supports shall, as far as practicable, be arranged adjacent to the pipe joints. 

(4) Slings are in general preferable to roller supports and the latter shall be used only where necessary. 

(5) All pipe supports shall as far as practicable, be of mild steel and pipe anchors either of mild steel or cast steel. 


290. Drainage.— (|) (a) In the case of steam mains, attention shall be paid to the adequate provision of drainage 
points in the form of drain pockets. 

(b) Drainage points connected to stream-traps, shall be provided wherever water can collect under working 
conditions. 

(c) Hand drains shall be provided at all points at which water can collect in any portion of the steam main, by 
valve leakage or other means, when shut down, or when warning up prior to use. 


(2) Wherever practicable, a suitable gradient shall be provided in the pipe work to ensure the passage of 
condensed water in the direction of flow of steam towards the drainage points. 


(3) Itis recommended that a bypass shall be fitted at each steam trap. 


(4) Where the volume of water deposited is likely to be of serious proportions, separator shall be installed. 
(5) Each separator shall be furnished with a steam trap which shall be connected to it by means of a three-way 
cock, one end of which is connected to a manually operated drain. 


29.Freedom from rust and other foreign matter.— All pipes, valves and fittings shall be thoroughly cleaned 
as far as possible of rust and other foreign matter before erection and pipe lines shall be blown through with steam 
or air before being put into service. 


292. Test Pressures.—(l) Each completed pipe and fitting shall be tested by hydraulic pressure as per Chapter-2. 


(2) (a) Pipes and fittings with flanges for steam pressures exceeding 7 kg/cm? (g) shall be tested with blank flanges 
bolted or clamped on. 
(b) All other pipes, if straight, may be tested between the heads of an ordinary hydraulic pipes testing machine. 


(3) (a) The piping system shall, after erection, be subjected to a hydrostatic test pressure. 
(b) The hydrostatic test pressure at any point in the piping system shall not be less than |.5 times the design 
pressure but shall not exceed the maximum allowable test pressure of any non-isolated components such as 
vessels, pumps or valves. 
(c) At no time during the hydrostatic tests, any part of the piping system shall be subjected to a stress greater 
than 90 per cent of its yield strength (0.2 per cent off set) at test temperature. 


Notwithstanding anything contained in this sub-section, for boiler external piping and non-boiler external 
piping which are open to atmosphere such as vent and drain pipes, the hydraulic test for the portions of such 
pipes located beyond the last isolation valve may be dispensed with provided the weld joints in the pipe under 
reference are tested !00% by approved non-destructive examination and found satisfactory. 


(4) Special arrangement shall be made, according to circumstances, for testing bends and other fittings which are 
not flanged. 


(5) Hydraulic testing of butt welded and socket welded joints shall be conducted either at makers work or at user’s 
premises on completion of fabrication of pipes by the Inspecting Authority. 


(6) (a) Hydrostatic testing of fabricated pipes having attachments of flanges, fittings, butt joints, branch joints and 
weldolets shall be done at manufacturer’s works or alternatively at site at .5 times the maximum allowable 
working pressure. 

(b) Where hydraulic testing of fabricated pipe joints is not carried out at manufacturer’s works, dye-penetrant 
test shall be carried out on the welded joints along with five per cent radiography of such joints.

(2) The boiler components shall be erected at site based on the final inspection report as per Form-VIII approved 
by Competent Person and there is no need for any ground inspection or submission of any other document like 
manufacturing drawings, design calculations.

295. Preparations of Inspection.— (.)(a)(i) At every boiler examination or grant of renewal of a certificate, the 
boiler shall be empty and all its parts shall be thoroughly cleaned. Except as provided for in sub-regulation (6), 
all doors of manholes, hand holes and sight holes and cleaning plugs and all caps in the headers and mud drums 
of water tube boilers, all fire bars, bearers, front plates, bridge plates, fire bridges brick arches, oil fuel burners 
and mechanical stoker fitting shall be removed. 

(ii) All valves and cocks comprising the boiler mounting shall be opened up and taken apart and the valves or 


| 
| 
| 
2 
2 
2 
2 
24 


cocks grounded, when necessary, before the Competent Person’s visit. 


(b) The removal of fire bars, bearers, front plates, bridge plates, fire bridges, brick arches, oil fuel burners and 
mechanical stoker fitting is not required at the time of registration for boilers for which boiler pressure part 
assembly is completed and hydraulic test has been carried out at manufacturer works by Competent Person. 


(2) (a) In case of requirement for inspection by the Competent Person, provision shall be made for removal of 
lagging or brick-work or other concealing part for drilling of plates, and for verifying the pressure gauge and 
safety valve dimensions and weights. 

(b) The removal of lagging or brick-work or other concealing part shall not be required at the time of 
registration of boilers for which boiler pressure part assembly is completed and hydraulic test carried out at 
manufacturer works by Competent Person. 


(3) All smoke tubes, exterior of water tubes, smoke boxes, and external flues shall be swept clean. 


(4) Provision shall be made for effective disconnection of all steam and hot water communication with another 
boiler under steam as required in Chapter-9. 


(5) No blank flange or plug shall be inserted between a safety valve chest and the boiler generally and where it is 
permitted by the Competent Person, the blank flange or plug shall be removed in his presence. 


(6) At alternative annual inspections and subject to a minimum of three bottom rows or all tubes subject to the 
first pass of heat being opened up for inspection, the Competent Person may at his discretion relax the 
preparation for inspection specified under sub-regulation (() above in favour of boilers having an evaporative 
capacity of 90 tons per hour and over, and using treated feed water to the satisfaction of the Competent Person. 


698 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(7) For boilers used for electric power generation, the inspection shall be carried out as per the provisions of 
Appendix-H. 


(8) (a) For Waste Heat Boilers (Fired and Unfired) used exclusively in continuous process plants, the inspection 
shall be carried out as per the provisions of Appendix-l. 
(b) The boilers used in corrosive environment such as sulphuric acid plants shall not be covered under the 
provisions of Appendix-I. 


(9) In the case of forced flow and forced circulation types of boilers, proper circulation in every section of the 
circuit shall be ensured by the flow of water. 


296. Hydraulic test of boilers.— (4) Every boiler shall be hydraulically tested in the presence of an Inspector. 


(2) Boiler working at a pressure of 50 kg/cm? (g) or more, and used exclusively for electric power generation 
need not be hydraulically tested for issue of certificate every year, provided the inspection of such boiler is 
carried out as per the provisions of sub-regulation (7) of regulation 295. 


(3) Waste Heat Boilers (Fired and Unfired) used exclusively in continuous process plants need not be 
hydraulically tested for issue of certificate every year, provided the inspection of such boilers is carried out 
as per the provisions of sub-regulation (8) of regulation 295. 


297. Preparation for hydraulic tests.— (l) The chest of all mountings subject to steam pressure shall be in place 
and shut tight or blank flanged. 


(2) The safety valves shall be invariably removed and the chest opening blank flanged. 
(3) The attachment for the Competent Person’s pressure gauge shall be in order. 


(4) (a) All doors shall be properly jointed and tightened up. 
(b) The boiler shall be completely filled with water with care being taken to allow all air to escape and, 
if possible, a preliminary test not exceeding the design pressure of the boiler shall be taken before the 
Competent Person’s visit, to test the tightness of the joints. 


(5) When a boiler is hydraulically tested for the first time, it shall be entirely cleared of lagging or brick work; 
at subsequent tests the lagging or brick work, or portions thereof, shall be removed, if required by the 
Competent Person, provided the Competent Person may, at his discretion, allow the lagging and brick 
work to remain in situ, in case of boilers where the covered parts have been fabricated and tested before 
erection in position. 


298. Procedure of hydraulic tests.— () (a) Subject to the provisions of sub-regulation (I)of regulation300, every 
sub-critical boiler shall be hydraulically tested after erection at site in presence of the Competent Person to 4.25 
times the design pressure as certified by the Inspecting Authority in Form-I(Part-B) or Form-I(Part-C) as the case 
may be, to be stamped on the boiler, as free from any indication of weakness or defects and every Super critical 
boiler, with no fixed steam and waterline, having pressure parts designed for different pressure levels along the 
path of water-steam flow, shall be hydraulically tested after erection at site in presence of the Competent Person 
to a pressure of not less than |.5 times the design pressure at the super heater outlet but not less than .25 times 
the design pressure of any part of the boiler as certified by the Inspecting Authority in Form-I(Part-B) or Form- 
I(Part-C) as the case may be, to be stamped on the boiler, as free from any indication of weakness or defects. 


(b) If all components of the boiler in the manufacturer’s premises have not been tested hydraulically as per 
regulation 67, the test, on completion, shall be taken to |.5 times the design pressure. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 699 


(c) The temperature of the water used as medium of pressure testing shall not be less than 20°C and greater 
than 50°C. 


(d) The test pressure shall be raised gradually under proper control at all times so that it never exceeds by 
more than 6% of the required pressure and maintained for 30 minutes whereupon the pressure shall be 
reduced to maximum allowable working pressure and maintained for sufficient time to permit close visual 
inspection for leakage of pressure parts. 
(e) The hydraulic test at site for the components meant for renovation or retrofit or spares shall be carried 
out at .25 times of the design pressure and these components need not be hydraulically tested at 
manufacturer’s premises. 


(2) The boiler shall satisfactorily withstand such pressure without appreciable leakage or undue deflection 
or distortion of its parts for at least ten consecutive minutes. If the test if not satisfactory, the design 
pressure allowable by calculation shall be suitably reduced, unless the owner desires to make such 
alterations as will enable the boiler to withstand the hydraulic test satisfactorily, in which case the boiler 
shall again be examined after the alterations have been made, the pressure recalculated, if necessary and 
the boiler tested to satisfaction of the Competent Person. 


(3) At the first hydraulic test of a boiler prior to the issue of an original certificate, deflection measurements 
shall be made before, during and after test of each furnace length, fire-box and flat end or other plates. 


(4) After application of the hydraulic test, the Competent Person shall carefully examine the boiler inside and 
outside and satisfy himself that it has satisfactorily withstood the test. 


(5) (a) In case any part of the boiler show undue deflection or indication of permanent set during the progress 
of the test, the pressure shall be released immediately such indications are observed. 
(b) The maximum allowable working pressure for the part shall be 40 per cent of the test pressure applied 
when the point of permanent set was reached. This procedure shall apply to any boiler at any test. 


(6) Hydraulic tests of boilers at subsequent examination shall be at 4.25 times the design pressure of the boiler. 


(7) When the internal construction or size of a boiler does not permit the Competent Person to get inside it for 
examining all its parts closely, he shall see it tested by hydraulic pressure to |.5 times the design pressure 
at each inspection or the grant or renewal of a certificate. 


(8) Water tube locomotive type boiler and all tubular boilers shall be hydraulically tested at each inspection 
for the grant or renewal of a certificate, unless such test is waived under the orders of the Chief Inspector. 


(9) The Competent Person may if he considers it necessary, apply a hydraulic test to any boiler at any 
inspection. 


(0) Except in the case of vertical boilers having heating surface of less than 8.5m’portable and vehicular 
boilers, which do not require re-erection or building in brick work, the hydraulic tests of all boilers shall 
be conducted only after the erection of the boiler in situ and all boilers shall after re-erection in a position 
different from that in which were last examined by hydraulically tested. 


(.l) A hydraulic test shall also be taken granting an increased pressure certificate and after repairing a boiler. 
However, in the case of minor repairs to the water tube boilers where non-destructive testing(/(NDT) has 
been carried out, hydraulic testing may be dispensed with provided non-destructive testing is carried out 
by an approved method. 


700 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


({2) When carrying out hydraulic test, Competent Person shall ensure that the pressure gauges have valid 
calibration. 


299. Steam tests.— (l) Every boiler before registration and every boiler of which the design pressure has been 
altered shall, before the issue of an original or renewal certificate for such boiler, be tested under steam to the 
satisfaction of the Inspector. Inspector shall send notice to the owner for the date fixed for the steam test and 
on completion of the test the Inspector shall enter all relevant details in the memorandum of inspection books. 


(2) At the time of test, the safety valves shall be left free and capable of being adjusted to the approved design 
pressure. 


(3) After adjustment of the valves to the correct blowing pressure, the boiler shall be tried under full steam and 
firing with the feed water shut off and the stop-valve closed, and the Inspector shall note the accumulation of 
pressure and other details of the test as accumulation of pressure and other details of the test as well as the 
loading and adjustment of the safety valves. 


(a) In the case of sub-critical water tube boiler or boilers fitted with super heater, the feed water 
connection and stop valve need not be shut off and if the total valve area is lifted and found to be 
adequate by calculations, the requirement of the accumulation test may be assumed to have been 
satisfied if the valves are or have been found so adjusted that at least one safety valve on boiler shall 
be set at or below design pressure and remaining safety valves can be set up to three per-cent above 
the design pressure: 


Provided that all valves shall be lifted so that all steam which can be generated by the boiler 
can be discharged with a pressure rise not exceeding ten per-cent of the design pressure; 


(b) In the case of super critical boiler or boilers, with no fixed steam and waterline, having pressure 
parts designed for different pressure levels along with the path of water-steam flow, safety valves 
shall be set up to ten per-cent above the maximum allowable working pressure: 


Provided that all the valves shall be lifted so that all steam which can be generated by the boiler 
can be discharged with a pressure rise not exceeding thirteen percent of the individual component 
maximum allowable working pressure, provided the boiler is having automatic burner management 
system and Master Fuel Trip (MFT) on main steam pressure. High lifting of safety valves can be 
tested by hydraulically actuated methods. 


(4) Before the safety valve test, the Inspector shall satisfy himself that the water gauges are in working order 
and that the feed apparatus is capable of supplying the boiler with sufficient water. 


(5) Where as per rules, a person-in-charge of a boiler holding certificate of competency is not required, the 
Inspector may, when he thinks fit, satisfy himself by questioning or by practical test, whether the person- 
in-charge of the boiler understands the use and purpose of the water gauges, the pressure gauge, the 
safety valves, the feed water-supply and blow down. 


(6) When witnessing safety valves test, Inspector shall ensure that the pressure gauges have valid calibration. 
(7) No steam gauge shall be used without a syphon filled with water between it and the boiler. 
(8) When the accumulation of pressure at a steam test exceeds ten per cent of the design pressure the area of 


the safety valves shall be considered insufficient, and a certificate shall be refused until the safety valve 
area is increased. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 704 


(9) An Inspector may, when visiting a factory for any purpose, verify the correctness of the safety valve and 
pressure gauge of any boiler under steam by comparison with his standard pressure gauge. 


*Note: A steam test is primarily intended for ascertaining that the safety valves are sufficient to relieve boilers 
effectively of excess steam and operate at the time when the maximum allowable working pressure is reached. 


300. Procedure for Registration.— () On receipt of an application for registration under sub-section (l) of 
Section 2 of the Act, along with certificates and drawings as provided in regulation-8, the Inspector shall, when 
the boiler has been properly prepared for examination proceed to inspect it with a view to satisfy himself that the 
boiler has not suffered any damage during its transit from the place of manufacture to the site of erection and if 
he is satisfied with the correctness of the maker’s certificate and other particulars relating to the material and 
construction as mentioned under clause (c) of sub-section (.) of section l9 of the Act and regulation 7, take due 
account of the workmanship and details of the construction of each part; 


(2) Subject to any discretionary power exercised by the Chief Inspector, he may accept the permissible working 
pressure of the boiler as certified by the Inspecting Authority in Form-I(Part-B) or Form-I(Part-C) as the 
case may be and Form-IV(Part-A) and after inspecting the boiler, the Inspector shall conduct hydraulic test 
as per requirements of regulations 298 and a provisional order under section !4 in Form-X shall be issued 
after the hydraulic test. 


(3) If the requirements of provisional order under sub-regulation (2) are not fulfilled, fresh provisional orders 
shall be issued for a maximum of another six months but not exceeding twelve months from the date of issue 
of first provisional order, without any subsequent inspection and payment of fees. 


(4) The Inspector shall enter the above particulars and dimensions of the boiler, together with details of the 
hydraulic test, in Form-XI (Memorandum of Inspection Book) provided under regulation 306 and with all 
the makers’ papers for the boiler, shall be submitted to the Chief Inspector with the Inspector’s report after 
issue of registry number, the Inspector shall conduct steam test as per regulation 299 and enter the details of 
steam test in Form-XI.

302. Measurement of Heating Surface. — (.) For the purpose of regulating the area of the safety valves and the 
amount of registration and inspection fees, the heating surface of a boiler shall be the total surface of all plates 


and 


tubes exposed to heat on one side and in contact with water on the other measured on the water side or the 


fire side, whichever is larger. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 703 


(2) (a) For Lancashire and Cornish boilers, the total heating surface shall include the wetted surface of the 
furnaces between the end plates, the fire surface of cross tubes where fitted, and the part of the external shell 
below the side flue covers. In estimating the areas, furnaces shall be considered as plain cylinders and the area 
of their wetted surface shall be taken as their mean external circumference X the length of the boiler between 
end plates. For the shell, the width of that part of the circumference below the flue covers shall be taken as = 
2D, and this width multiplied by the length between end plates, shall be taken as the area of shell heating surface. 

(b) The part of the surface of the back end plate exposed to heat shall be omitted from the calculation. 


Example — The formula for the total heating surface of a Lancashire boiler having plain furnaces without 
cross tubes is as follows: - 


Heating Surface in square meter = 2 L (3.!4d+D). “L” is the length of the boiler between end plates in 
meter, “d” is the mean external diameter of the furnaces in meter and “D” is the internal diameter of the 
largest belt of shell in meter. 


(3) (a) For steam and water drums of water tube boilers, the heating surface of the drum shall be taken as 
half the external mean circumference multiplied by the clear length of drum between the outer brick walls or 
centers of cross boxes, as the case may be. 

(b) The heating surface of the tubes shall be taken as the external surface of the tubes between the tube plates 

or heaters. 

(c) The heating surface of the heater shall be omitted from the calculation. 


(4) (a) For marine boilers of the fire-tube type, the heating surface shall include the wetted surface of the 
furnaces between the tube plates (considered in the same way as for Lancashire boilers), the wetted surface of 
the combustion chambers (less the area of the tube holes) and the wetted surface of the tubes between tube 
plates. 

(b) The parts of the front tube plate exposed to heat shall be omitted from the calculation. 


(5) (a) For locomotive type boilers, the heating surface shall include the wetted surface of the fire-box above 
the foundation ring (less the area of the tube holes and the fire hole and ring) and the wetted surface of the tubes 
between the tube plates. 

(b) The smoke box tube plate shall be omitted from the calculation. 


(6) For vertical boilers of ordinary type; the heating surface shall include the wetted surface of the fire-box 
above the foundation ring (less the area of fire hole and ring and tube holes if any) and the surface of any cross 
or other tubes and uptake below the lowest water level shown in the gauge glass. 


(7) For Electrode boilers, the heating surface shall be calculated as per the following formulae,-

design pressure with the feed water temperature of I5°C. 


(8) No deduction shall be made for stays, in calculating the heating surface. 


(9) For any other heating surface not provided for in the foregoing instructions, the same general procedure 
shall be observed.

3. Procedure for inspection of installed boilers.— () (a)It is essential to have every part of the boiler that is 
accessible, open and properly prepared for examination, internally and externally. 

(b)AIl boilers have openings through which an examination may be made and for which operation are closed; all 
such parts shall be opened whether for access to water surfaces, or heater surfaces. 

(c)In cooling a boiler down for inspection or repairs, the water should not be withdrawn until the setting is 
sufficiently cooled to avoid damage to the boiler and when possible allowed to cool down naturally. 

(d)It is not necessary, in order to comply with ordinary prudence, to remove insulation material, masonry, or fixed 
parts of the boiler, unless defects or deterioration peculiar to certain types of in accessible parts of boilers are 
suspected and where there is moisture or vapour showing through the covering should be removed at once and a 
complete investigation made. 

(e)Particular attention shall be paid to the external parts of boilers in the way of seating blocks, especially when 
the situation is damp. Saddle tanks and engine fittings of locomotive type boilers shall be removed to facilitate 
the inspection of the parts underneath at the first inspection, and at any reasonable period afterwards, if the 
Competent Person cannot otherwise satisfy himself as to the condition of those parts. 

(f)Upon sufficient visible evidence or suspicion due to age or other causes, every effort shall be made to discover 
the true condition, even to the removal of insulating material, masonry or fixed parts of a boiler. Sometimes 
drilling or cutting away of parts is justifiable and necessary to positively determine this condition. 


(2) The Competent Person shall, whenever the size permits, go inside it and make a thorough inspection of all its 
internal parts. Before doing so, he shall, satisfy himself that proper provision has been made for disconnecting 
the boiler from any other boiler under steam. In case he find that proper provision for disconnection has not 
been made or that the boiler has not been properly cleaned, or scaled, or that is unreasonably hot, he shall 
decline to proceed with the inspection and shall report the facts to the Inspecting Authority or Chief Inspector 
as the case may be, for orders. When a boiler is of such a size or its construction is such that the Competent 
Person cannot go inside it, there should be sufficient sight holes or hand holes provided to enable him to see 
the principal internal parts; if any important part of a boiler is so constructed that the Competent Person cannot 
examine it, he should report the facts to the Inspecting Authority or Chief Inspector as the case may be, for 
orders. 


(3) In the case of forced circulation and forced flow boilers which are not accessible to close visual inspection, 
the Competent Person shall, besides thorough examination, ensure by the flow of water that proper circulation 
is maintained through all sections of the water circuits. 


(4) (a)Upon entering a boiler, the Competent Person shall examine all surfaces of the exposed metal to observe 
the action caused by the use of water, oil scale solvents, or other substances which may have intentionally or 
unintentionally gone in with the feed water. Any evidence of oil is dangerous and immediate steps shall be 
taken to prevent any further entrance of oil into the boiler. 

(b)Oil or scale in the tubes of water-tube boilers or on plates over the fire of any boiler is particularly bad, 
often causing them to rupture. 


(5) A given amount of corrosion along or immediately adjacent to a seam is more serious than a similar amount 
of corrosion in the solid plate away from the seams. Grooving along longitudinal seams is especially 
significant as grooving or cracks are likely to occur when the material is highly stressed. Severe corrosion is 
likely to occur at points where the circulation of the water is poor and such places shall be examined most 
carefully for evidences of corrosive action. 


(6) If the Competent Person decides that a boiler in one or more of its parts is no longer fit for the pressure 
approved for it, he shall without delay report his proposal for reducing the pressure to the Chief Inspector and 
at the same time submit his calculation for the wasted parts for check and approval of pressure. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 709 


(7) With regard to the pitting and wasting of shell plates, the Competent Person shall bear in mind that thickness 
of shell plates may reduce to an appreciable extent and still be stronger than longitudinal seams. 


(8) (a)All flanging shall be thoroughly inspected and particularly the flanges of circular and plates that are not 
stayed. 
(b)Internal grooving in the fillet of such heads and external grooving in the outer surfaces of heads concave 
to pressure is very common since there is slight movement in the heads of this character which produces this 
kind of defect. Some types of boilers have what is known as the OG or reversed flange construction in some 
of their parts that may be inaccessible to the eye, but the condition shall be determined by the insertion of a 
mirror which at a proper angle will reflect back to the eye the condition of such a place, or any other feasible 
manner. 


(9 


Ne 


(a)All stays, whether diagonal or through, shall be examined to note that they are in even tension. 

(b) All fastened ends shall be examined to note whether cracks exist where the stays are punched or drilled 
or rivets or bolts and, if not found in proper tension, the Competent Person shall recommend their proper 
adjustment. 

(I0) (a)The manhole and other reinforcing plates, as well as nozzles or other connection flanged or screwed into 
a boiler, shall be examined internally as well as externally to see that they are not cracked or deformed, and 
wherever possible observation shall be made for the inside of the boiler, as to the thoroughness with which 
its pipe connections are made to the boiler. 

(b)AIl openings to external attachments, such as water column connections, openings in dry pipes and opening 
to safety valves, shall be noted to see that they are free from obstructions. 


(() (a)Particular attention shall be given to the plate or tube surface exposed to the fire. The Competent Person 
shall observe whether any part of the boiler has become deformed during, operation by bulging or blistering; 
bulging is a distortion of the entire thickness of the plate or tube where it takes place, while the blistering is 
a lamination or separation of the plate due to foreign material being embedded in the ingot before the plate is 
rolled. 

(b)If bulges or blisters are of such size as would seriously weaken the plate or tube and especially when the 
leakage is noted coming from those defects, the boiler shall be discontinued from service until the defective 
part or parts have received proper repairs. 

(c) Careful observation shall be made to detect leakage from any portion of the boiler structures, particularly 
in the vicinity of seams and tube ends. 

(d) Fire tubes sometimes blister but rarely collapse, the Competent Person shall look through the tubes for 
such defects and if they are found with a sufficient degree of distortion they shall be removed. 


((2) (a) Lap joint boilers are apt to crack where the plates lap in the longitudinal or straight seam; if there is any 
evidence of leakage or other distress at this point, it shall be thoroughly investigated and, if necessary rivets 
removed or the plate slotted in order to determine whether cracks exist in the seam. Any cracks noted in shell 
plates are usually dangerous except fire cracks that run from the edge of the plate into the rivet holes of girth 
seams. 

(b) A limited number of such fire cracks is not usually a very serious matter. 


({3) The Competent Person shall test stay bolts by tapping one end of each bolt with a hammer and when 
practicable a hammer or other heavy tool shall be held on the opposite end to make the test more effective. 


((4) (a) G)Tubes in horizontal fire tube boilers deteriorate more rapidly at the ends toward the fire, and they shall 
be carefully tapped with a light hammer on their outer surface to ascertain whether there has been serious 
reduction in thickness. 

(ii)The tubes of vertical tubular boilers are more susceptible to deterioration at the upper open ends when 
exposed to the products of combustion without water protection. 
(iii)They shall be reached as far as possible either through the hand holes if any, or inspected at the ends. 


70 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(b) (i)The surfaces shall be carefully examined to detect bulges or cracks, or any evidences or 
defective welds. 

(ii)Where there is a strong draft, the tubes may become thinned by corrosion produced by the 

impingement or particles of fuel and ash, or the improper use of soot blowers. 

(iii)A leak from a tube frequently causes serious corrosive action on a number of tubes in its immediate 

vicinity. 


(c) (i)Where short tubes or nipples are employed in joining drums or headers, there is a tendency 
for waste products of the furnace to lodge in the junction points and such deposits are likely to cause 
corrosion if moisture is present. 

(ii)All such places shall be thoroughly cleaned and examined. 


(.5) G)The ligaments between tube holes in the heads of all types of fire-tube boilers and in shells of water-tube 
boilers shall be examined. 
(ii)If leakage is noted, it may denote a broken ligament. 


(6) Steam pockets on surfaces are sometimes found in new or replacement work, and wherever, this is possible 
or likely, the Competent Person shall make observation and, if any are found, recommend the necessary 
changes. 


(.7) (a)() The steam and water pipes, including connections to the water column, shall be examined for leaks, and 
if any are found, it shall be determined whether they are the result of excessive strains due to expansion and 
contraction, or other causes. 

(ii)The general arrangement of the piping in regard to the provisions, for expansion and drainage, as well as 
adequate support at the proper points, shall be carefully noted. 

(iii)The location of the various stop valves shall be observed to see that water will not be pocketed when the 
valves are closed and thereby establish cause for water-hammer action. 


(b)The arrangement of connections between individual boilers and the main steam pipes shall be especially 
noted to see that any change of position of the boiler due to setting or other causes, will not produce an undue 
strain on the piping. 


(c) It shall be ascertained whether all pipe connections to the boiler possess the proper strength in their 
fastenings, whether tapped into the boiler, a fitting, or flange riveted to the boiler. 


(d) (i)The Competent Person shall determine whether there is provision for the expansion and contraction of 
such piping, and that there is no undue vibration tending to crystalize the parts subjected to it. 

(ii)This includes all steam and water pipe and special attention shall be given to the blow off pipes with their 
connections and fittings, because the expansion and contraction due to rapid change in temperature and 
water-hammer action create a great strain upon the entire blow off system, which is more pronounced when 
a number of blow off pipes are joined in one common discharge. 

(iii)The freedom of the blow off connection on each boiler shall be tested whenever possible by opening the 
valve for a few seconds, at which time it can be determined whether there is excessive vibration. Blow off 
pipes should be free from external dampness to prevent corrosion. 


((8) (a)(i)The piping to the water column shall be carefully noted to see that there is no chance of water being 
pocketed in the piping forming the steam connection to the water column. The steam-pipe shall preferably 
drain towards to the water column. 

(ii)The water pipe connection to the water column must drain towards the boiler. 


(b) G)The relative position of the water column to the fire surfaces of the boiler shall be observed to determine 
whether the column is placed in accordance with the regulations. The attachments shall be examined to 
determine their operating condition. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


((9) (a)In Water-Tube boilers, it shall be noted, as far as possible, whether or not the proper baffling is in place. 
(b) In many types of boilers, the absence of baffling often causes high temperatures on portions of the boiler 
structure which are not intended to be exposed to such temperatures, from which a dangerous condition may 
result. The location of combustion arches with respect to tube surfaces shall be carefully noted. These are 
sometimes arranged so as to cause the flame to impinge on a particular part of a boiler and produces 
overheating of the material and consequent danger of the rupture of the part. 


(20) Localisation of heat brought about by improper or defective burner or stoker installation or operation creating 
a blow pipe effect upon the boiler, shall be condemned. 


(2) Where boilers are suspended, the supports and setting shall be carefully examined specially at points where 
the boiler structure comes near the setting walls or floor. Often accumulation of ash and soot will bind the 
boiler structure at such points and produce excessive strains on the structure owing to the expansion of the 
parts under operating conditions. 


(22) (a) As the safety valves are the most important attachments on the boiler, they shall be inspected with the 
utmost caution. There shall be no accumulations of rust, scale, or other foreign substances located in the 
casings so as to interfere with the free operation of valves. The setting and freedom of the safety valves shall 
be tested preferably by raising the steam pressure to the blow-in-off point, or if this cannot be done, the valves 
shall be tested by means of the try levers to ascertain if they are free. Where the steam discharged from a 
safety valve is led through a pipe the Competent Person shall determine at the time the valve is operating 
whether or not the drain, opening in the discharge pipe is free and in accordance with the Regulations. 


(b)If the Competent Person deems it necessary, in order to determine the freedom of discharge from a 
safety valve, the discharge connections shall be removed. Under no circumstances a stop valve shall be 
permitted between a boiler and its safety valve. 


(23) The steam gauges on all boilers shall be removed and the Competent Person shall test them and compare their 
readings with a standard test gauge. The readings of the steam gauges shall be observed and compared when 
making an inspection with steam on the boiler, where several boilers are in service connected to a common 
steam main. The location of the steam gauges shall be noted to see whether or not it is exposed to high 
temperature either externally, as would be the case if placed close to the smoke flue or other high heated part 
of the boiler or setting, or exposed to heat internally due to lack of protection of the gauge spring with a 
proper syphon or trap to prevent steam from coming in contact with the spring. The Competent Person shall 
see that the provisions are made for blowing out the pipe leading to the steam gauge. 


32. Calculation of wasted shell.—(])When any part is wasted and the Competent Person is doubtful of its fitness 
for the pressure, he shall cause one or more small holes to be bored and from them ascertain the average thickness 
of the parts from which he can satisfy himself by calculation, in accordance with the formula applicable to the 
part. He shall enter such gauging and calculations in the Memorandum of Inspection Book. 


(2) In making calculations for a wasted part of a boiler shell, e.g., along the line of seating blocks of a 
Lancashire boiler, the Competent Person shall use the following formula:

(3) (a)Shell type Waste Heat Boilers(un-fired), on completion of a life of twenty-five years, shall be non-

(b) Pressure parts, such as shell, end- plates, stand pipes etc., of such boilers, shall be inspected

Boilers Board. Such agency shall work in close coordination with the office of the Chief 
inspector or Director of Boilers as the case may be.

36. Repairs to boiler and steam pipes.—(l) Major repairs or replacements such as tubes, coils, headers, drums, 
fusion welded patches to shells, fireboxes and end plates of boilers and extensive building up of wasted parts of boilers 
permitted under these regulations, the renewal of furnaces and end plates, parts of shell, fireboxes, girders and steam- 
pipes, etc., shall only be entrusted to a firm who is recognised as a repairer under these regulations. 


(2) Any firm seeking recognition shall apply in ‘Form-XII’ to the Chief Inspector of Boilers of the State in which 
the recognition is sought along with the fee specified in table 8/9. 


(3) A firm seeking recognition as a repairer shall meet the following requirements depending upon the class of boilers, 
namely: — 


(a) For Class I boiler repairer, the owner of the firm himself shall have a degree in mechanical or Production 
or Power Plant or Metallurgical engineering or the firm shall have on its rolls a permanently employed 
engineer having a degree in mechanical or Production or Power Plant or Metallurgical engineering and 
the said owner or the permanently employed engineer shall also have an experience of at least five years 
in an organisation engaged in fabrication, erection, repair or maintenance and quality control of boilers; 
and the firm shall also have qualified and permanently employed welders as per the provisions of these 
regulations; 


(b) For Class II boiler repairer, the owner of the firm himself shall have a diploma in mechanical engineering 
or the firm shall have on its rolls a permanently employed engineer having a diploma in mechanical 
engineering and the said owner or the permanently employed engineer shall also have an experience of 
at least three years in an organisation engaged in fabrication, erection, repair or maintenance and quality 
control of boilers; and the firm shall also have qualified and permanently employed welders as per the 
provisions of these regulations; 


(c) For Class III boiler repairer, the owner of the firm himself or a person permanently employed with the 
firm shall have a minimum three years’ experience in repair, maintenance, operation, erection or 
inspection of boiler and the firm shall also have qualified and permanently employed welders as per the 
provisions of these regulations; 


(d) For Special class boiler repairer, the owner of the firm himself shall have a degree in mechanical or 
welding engineering along with specialised experience in welding technology for a minimum period of 
three years or the firm shall have on its rolls a permanently employed engineer having a degree in 
mechanical or welding engineering along with specialised experience in welding technology for a 
minimum period of three years, and have permanently employed welders as per the provisions of these 
regulations who should also have valid certificate for carrying out Tungsten Inert Gas welding; 


(e)(i) Where the power stations, fertilizer plants, chemical and petrochemical plants or refineries apply for 
repair of their own boilers, they shall have all the facilities in-house and may apply to the Chief Inspector of 
Boilers of the State for permission to repair their own boilers in accordance with these regulations; 


(ii) On receipt of the application for permission to repair to a boiler, the Chief Inspector of Boilers of 
the State shall reply to the request within a period of two days of the receipt of the application. 


(4) The Chief Inspector shall scrutinise and evaluate the application along with the replies to the questionnaire 
and after satisfying himself that the following requirements are fulfilled, shall recognise the firm as a repairer 
within a period of thirty days, in the category applied for, namely: — 


(a) that the firm possesses rectifier or generator, grinder, general tools and tackles, dye-penetrant kit, 
expander and measuring instruments; 


7i8 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(b) that the electric arc or oxy-acetylene welding sets and all other tools and plant in his possession for 
carrying out repairs are suitable for the work undertaken; 


(c) that the quality of material used conforms to the specifications prescribed in these regulations; 


(d) that the supervisory and operational staff employed by the firm possesses the necessary training and 
experience for the work undertaken; 


(e) that all welders employed by the firm possess certificates issued as required under Chapter-3 of 
these regulations; 


(f) Standard of work should be of high order and comply with all the requirements and test that may be 
specified by the Chief Inspector. 


(5) The recognition of the firm as a repairer shall be for a period of two years and thereafter it shall apply for 
renewal of its recognition at least two months before the expiry of said period. 


(6) A repairer recognised in one State shall be eligible to work in any other State by getting his recognition 
endorsed from the Chief Inspector or Director of Boilers of the concerned State on making payment of fee as 
prescribed in this regulation. 


(7) In case the repairer is found indulging in violating the provisions of the Act or regulations, the firm shall be 
blacklisted under intimation to Chief Inspector or Director of Boilers of all the States and Union territories 
and Secretary, Central Boilers Board, and renewal shall not be done in any case.

37. Procedure for repairs.—(|)The repair work shall be carried out under the supervision of Inspector or Competent 
Person and when the fireboxes and smoke tubes of locomotive tube boilers are withdrawn, the internal parts, which 
are otherwise inaccessible to close inspection, shall be inspected by the Inspector or Competent Person, as the case 
may be. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 79 


(2) Repair to boilers shells shall be carried out by patching or by removing a strip of worn or damaged plate and 
inserting the new strip with covering straps over the longitudinal butt ends, the strength of the riveted joints shall 
be not less than that of the longitudinal joints of the shell. 

(3) (a) Patches for fire exposed plates shall be fitted metal to metal without joint of any description; 


(b) The affected part shall be cut out, leaving the corners of the hole well-rounded. 


(c) Patches shall be secured, wherever possible, properly spaced rivets with a width of plate at least equal to the 
diameter of rivet between the edge of the rivet hole and the edge of the plate. 


(d) Where riveting is impracticable, the plate shall be secured by welt fitting countersunk headed screw pins. 
(4) The thickness of a patch plate shall not be less than the original thickness of the plate which it is used to patch. 


(5) Bulged or distorted furnaces or circular section may, if the bulge or distortion is not too great, be pressed back 
to shape. 


(6) Circular furnaces of horizontal boilers that have become distorted may be suitably reinforced. 

(7) (a) Anti-collapse rings shall be substantial section either of single or double angles bolted back to back with 
screw stays not less than 22 mm in diameter and about 78 mm in pitch passed though flat of angle and screwed 
into the furnace, the ends being rounded over on the fire side and fitted with nuts at the other. 

(b) The stay bolts shall be fitted with ferrules not less than 25 mm in depth between furnace and angle ring. 
(8) Welding shall not be accepted for the repair of any part of a boiler for which welding is forbidden for a new 
boiler under these regulations and boiler shells shall not be repaired by welding beyond the filling up of a small 


isolated corroded or pitted part or the making up of wasted edges of openings. 


(9) Cracks or grooving in dished or flat end plates of cylindrical shells or in the bends of furnace flanges in a 
circumferential direction may be weed out and welded. 


(.0) Wasted parts of circular furnaces and fireboxes and fire exposed flat plates as in rectangular fireboxes and 
combustion chambers may be cut out and be replaced by new pieces welded in or they may be built-up by 


welding. 


(.]) Longitudinal cracks in circular furnaces and fireboxes and cracks in rectangular fireboxes and combustion 
chambers may be welded. 


(.2) No stay bar shall be welded. 


(3) Smoke tubes may be butt-welded either by fusion welding, flush welding or oxy-acetylene welding, and these 
may be tested hydraulically at the discretion of the Inspecting Authority. 


720 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


38. Procedure for welding during repairs. The repairer shall satisfy the inspecting Authority :- 


() That the electric arc or oxy-acetylene welding sets and all other tools and plant in his possession 
for carrying out repairs are suitable for the work undertaken. 


(2) That the quality of material used conforms to the specification that are prescribed. 


(3) That the supervisory and operational staff employed by him possess the necessary training and 
experience for the work under taken. 


(4) That all welders employed by him possess certificates issued as required under Chapter-3 of 
these Regulations. 

(5) Standard of work shall be of high order and comply with all the requirements and test that may 
be prescribed by the Chief Inspector. 


39. Riveting and other repairs.— The repairer shall satisfy the Chief Inspector:- 


(!) That he possesses the necessary equipment and tools and engages trained and experienced workmen 
and staff for the work underwork taken. 


(2) Standard of work shall be of a high order and comply with all the requirements and test that may be 
prescribed by the Chief Inspector, and all material used shall be boiler quality. 


320. Miscellaneous provisions for repairs.— () (a)The repairs shall be supervised, so far as his other duties permit 


by the Competent Person. 
(b) When the fire boxes and smoke tubes of locomotive tube boilers are withdrawn, the opportunity shall be 
taken to inspect the internal parts which are otherwise inaccessible to close inspection. 


(2) Repairs to boiler shells shall be effected either by patching or by removing a strips of worn or damaged plate 
and inserting the new strip with covering straps over the longitudinal butt ends, the strength of the riveted 
joints shall be not less than that of the longitudinal joints of the shell. 


(3) (a) Patches for fire exposed plates shall be fitted metal to metal without joint of any description. The 
affected part shall be cut out, leaving the corners of the hole rounded. 
(b)Patches shall be secured, wherever possible, properly spaced rivets with a width of plate at least equal 
to the diameter or rivet between the edge of the rivet hole and the edge of the plate. 
(c)Where riveting is impracticable, the plate shall be secured by welt fitting countersunk headed screw pins. 


(4) The thickness of a patch plate shall not be less than the original thickness of the plate which it is used to 
patch. 


(5) Bulged or distorted furnaces of circular section may, if the bulge of distortion is not too great, be pressed 


back to shape. 
(6) Circular furnaces horizontal boilers that have become distorted may be suitably reinforced. 


(7) Anti-collapse rings shall be of substantial section either of single or double angles bolted back to back with 


screw stays not less than 22 mm in diameter and about 78 mm in pitch passes through flat of angle and 


wm 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 72व 


screwed into the furnace, the ends being rounded over on the fire side and fitted with nuts at the other. The 
stay bolts shall be fitted with ferrules not less than 25 mm in depth between furnace and angle ring. 


(8) Welding shall not be accepted for the repairs of any part of a boiler for which welding is forbidden for a new 
boiler under these Regulations. Boiler shells shall not be repaired by welding beyond the filling up of a small 
isolated corroded or pitted or the making up of wasted edges of openings. 


(9) Cracks or grooving in dished or flat end plate of cylindrical shells or in the bends of furnace flanges in 
circumferential direction may be weed out and welded. 


((0) Wasted parts of circular furnaces and fire boxes and fire exposed flat plates as in rectangular fire boxes and 
combustion chambers may be cut out and be replaced by new pieces welded in or they may be built up by 
welding. Longitudinal cracks in circular furnaces and fire-boxes and cracks in rectangular fire-boxes and 
combustion chambers may be welded. 


(.l) No Stay bar shall be welded. 


((2) For the purposes of these Regulations renewed part shall be deemed to be parts of a new boiler intended for 
use at the pressure at which the boiler under renewal is used. 


((3) For Butt Welding of Smoke Tubes, Smoke tubes may be butt welded either by fusion welding, flush welding 
or oxy-acetylene welding, and these should be tested hydraulically at the discretion of the Chief Inspector. 


32.Submission of manufacturing drawings and the particulars of boilers in advance.— (|) In the case of land 
boilers and boiler components including spares made in India for use in the States, the manufacturing drawings and 
the particulars of materials, design and construction of boilers shall be submitted by the makers of the boilers or boiler 
components or spares, as the case may be to the Inspecting Authority of the State, where the principal parts of the 
boilers will be manufactured, for examination and approval before commencement of the manufacture of boilers. 


(2) In the case of boilers and boiler components including spares made outside India for use in the State, the 
manufacturing drawings and particulars of the material, design and construction, of boilers shall be submitted 
initially to the Inspecting Authority in the country of manufacture for examination and approval. 


(3) The manufacturing drawings and the particulars of materials, design and construction in the case of fired boilers 
of steam generating capacity !00 Tons/hour and above and that of Waste heat boiler of 20 Tons/hour and above 
including boiler components and spares thereof shall then be submitted to the Technical Adviser (Boilers) for 
selection of latest materials with high strengths and use in high temperature and pressure, for the safety. 
Thereafter, the manufacturing drawings and the particulars of materials, design and construction approved by 
the Inspecting Authority shall be sent to the Chief Inspector of Boilers of the State where the boiler will be 
installed and used, for final examination and approval before commencement of manufacture so as to avoid 
questions arising at the time of erection and registration of the boiler. 


(4) The manufacturing drawings and the particulars of materials, design and construction in the case of fired boilers 
of steam generating capacity less than 00 Tons/hour and that of Waste heat boiler of less than 20 Tons/hour 
including boiler components and spares thereof approved by the Inspecting Authority shall be submitted to the 
Chief Inspector of Boilers of the State where the boiler will be installed and used, for final examination and 
approval before commencement of manufacture so as to avoid question arising at the time of erection and 
registration of the boiler.

therein. When the manufacturing drawings and the particulars of boilers have been approved, the Inspector or

(8) If the detailed manufacturing drawings are got approved by the Inspecting Authority of the State where parts will

322. Inspection of pipes.— (|) Pipes shall be inspected and hydraulically tested before use in place, in test 
pressure to be that prescribed in the standard conditions for steam pipes. A certificate from the Inspecting Authority 
in Form-IV(Part-B), stating that this has been done by him may be accepted. If the Competent Person is satisfied with 
the test, the pipes may be erected in position. The Chief Inspector shall intimate his approval to the owner regarding 
the suitability of the pipe line for use at the pressure and temperature to be specified. 


(2) At subsequent inspection of the boiler or at any other time, the Competent Person may make an external inspection 
of the steam-pipes and for this purpose may require a part of the lagging at the flanges to be removed, and the pipe 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 723 


made bare. If as a result of this inspection the Competent Person is of opinion that the pipes or any positions of 
then are in an unsatisfactory condition he shall report the matter to the Chief Inspector, who may require the whole 
of the lagging to be removed and may require any pipe or pipes to be hydraulically tested. The test pressure at 
such hydraulic test shall be not less than one and half times, the design pressure of the boiler or the maximum 
allowable working pressure of pipe as the case may be. 


(3)(a) A memorandum of Inspection Book shall be prepared in respect of steam pipe and fittings in Form-XIV. In 
this book, the Inspector shall enter in ink, all particulars and dimensions of the steam pipe and fitting with 
calculations for the various parts in detail, particulars of hydraulic test and his inspection notes. 


(b) At subsequent inspection, the Competent Person shall enter the date of the inspection and hydraulic test 
together with notes thereon. 


(c) The Competent Person shall also enter in the Memorandum of Inspection Book remarks regarding the general 
condition of the steam pipes and fittings, and repairs, replacements of alterations, if any, and the extent to 
which the steam pipes have been cleaned of lagging and covering so that the book provides a useful record 
of the steam-pipes and fittings for the information and guidance of Competent Person at subsequent 
inspection.

CHAPTER-9 
SAFETY OF PERSONS INSIDE BOILERS 


333.Safety of persons working inside boilers.— () The owner or person in charge shall not compel or 
allow any person to go inside a steam boiler for any purpose whatsoever unless the boiler is 
effectively disconnected from any steam or hot water communication with any other boiler, in the 
manner provided in this regulation. 


(2) (a) Effective disconnection shall be made either by the removal of the boiler stop valve or of a 
length of piping from all steam and hot water connection with any other boiler, vessel or pipe 
containing steam or hot water by the insertion of substantial blank flanges between the boiler stop 
valves and piping. 

(b) The shutting of a stop valve, stop cock or automatic isolating valve shall not be deemed to 
compliance with this regulation. 

(c) In the case of welded pipe work, however, if a vent pipe of not less than 50 mm internal 
diameter (bore) is fitted between the main stop valve and the intermediate stop valve on the steam 
main and between the feed check valve and intermediate check valve on the feed line, this 
regulation shall be considered to have been complied with, provided such vent pipes are fitted with 
bolted-on blank flanges and the flanges are removed so as to effectively discharge any leakage 
steam or water to the atmosphere which the valves on either side of it have been closed. 


(3) The owner of a boiler to which this regulation is applicable shall obtain the approval of the Chief 
Inspector in writing to the method of disconnection which he proposes to use and shall be 
responsible for ensuring that the method so approved is followed in practice. 


(4) When electric light is used for work inside a boiler shell or drum or any confined space within a 
boiler, the voltage shall not exceed 24 volts and the owner of the boiler shall provide a hand lamp 
with lamp-guard, keyless socket, insulated handle and extension cord of approved type. 


(5) Where power is used for working any equipment inside a boiler the metallic portion of the 
equipment shall be effectively earthed.

CHAPTER-0 
ELECTRODE BOILERS 
PART-I 


334. Application.— This Chapter applies to electrode steam boilers for all voltages for any working pressure and for 
temperatures not exceeding 343°C and electrode boilers shall only be of the following construction: 


(a) Fusion welded steel boilers; 
(b) Seamless shell steel boilers. 


335. General requirements.— Wherever applicable, the provisions of Chapter- relating to certificates from makers, 
Inspecting Authorities etc., and of Chapter-3 relating to construction shall be followed. 


336. Materials — The material specifications for structural parts of electrode boilers shall comply with Chapter-2, as 
regards the process of manufacture, chemical composition, mode of manufacture and test, and the certificates for the 
steel plates, provided that the ultimate tensile stress and elongation of materials shall be between the following limits: - 


(a) For fusion welded construction, as mentioned in Chapter-2. 


(b) For seamless construction as mentioned in regulation 250 and for seamless carbon steel pipes as mentioned in 


Table 7/3 of regulation 253. 


PART-2

the provision made in chapter-4 for fusion welded drums subject to the following conditions, namely:- 


(a) Class I boilers shall comply with the requirement of chapter-4;

(c) Class II boilers shall comply with the following requirements;

340. Bend Test.— () (a) Two bend tests shall be made for welded seams. 


(b) One specimen shall be tested with the outer surface or the weld in tension, and the other with the inner surface in

full thickness of the test plate. 


(b) Where the plate thickness exceeds 32 mm, the thickness of the specimen shall be at least 32 mm. 


(c) The specimen to be tested with the outer surface of the weld in tension shall be prepared by cutting to 
waste the metal local to the inner surface of the weld, so that the desired specimen thickness is obtained. 


(3) (a) The specimen to be tested with the inner surface in tension shall be prepared by cutting to waste the 
metal local to the outer surface of the weld so that the desired metal thickness is obtained. 


(b) Where the thickness of the plate permits, both specimen being located in the plate one above the other. 


(c) Each specimen shall be mounted with the weld midway between the support, set apart at a distance of not 
more than 5.2 times the thickness of the specimen and pushed through the supports with a former having a diameter 
equal to three times the thickness of the specimen (see Fig. 4/6 of regulation 60 of chapter 4). 


(4) (a) On completion of the test, no crack or defect at the outer surface of the specimen shall be greater than 
.5 mm, measured across the specimen or 3 mm measured along the length of the specimen. 


(b) Premature failure at corners of the specimen shall not be considered cause for rejection (see Fig. 4/6, 
specimen A). 


34. Nick Break Test — (a) The specimen shall be rectangular in section and cut transversely to the well so as to have 
a width not less than one-half times its thickness. 


(b) The slot shall be cut in one side of the specimen through the center of the weld and perpendicular to the outer face 
of the vessel. 


(c) The specimen shall then be broken in the weld and the fracture shall reveal a sound homogeneous-weld, 
substantially free from slag inclusions, porosity and coarse crystallinity. 


342. Retests.— In case any of the tests fail, two retests shall be made on specimens cut from the same plate and both 
retests shall meet the specified requirements. 


343. Specimens after Tests.— If required by the inspecting Authority, the specimens after test shall be forwarded for 
examination. 


344. Heat Treatment.— All fusion welded electrode boilers shall be stress relieved by heat treatment and the heat 
heat-treatment shall be in accordance with regulation 23. 


345. Hydraulic Test.— Hydraulic Test shall comply with regulation 67.

CHAPTER -I 


STANDARD CONDITIONS FOR THE DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION OF ECONOMISERS, FEED PIPES, 
FEED HEATERS AND OTHER SIMILAR VESSELS 


PART-I 


ECONOMISERS 
357. Application of standard condition and exceptions thereto.— (l) An economiser shall not be registered under 
sub-section (5) of section |2 of the Act and a certificate shall not be issued under sub-section (6) of that section with 
reference to an economiser unless the standard conditions in respect of material design and construction, which are 
specified in this chapter are satisfied in respect of such economiser. 


(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub regulation (.), the chief Inspector may, subject to the provisions 
of regulation 359, register an economiser and order the issue of a certificate authorising the use thereof, although the 
standard conditions are not fully satisfied in respect of such economiser. 


358. General requirements.— (l) All cast iron and steel headers and parts used in the assembly of an economiser 
shall conform to the requirements of this Chapter in respect of material specification and test workmanship and 
structural requirements. 


(2) Alleconomisers shall be constructed under the supervision of an Inspecting Authority and shall be so certified 
by that authority. 


(3) A certificate from the Inspection Authority in Form--XV certifying that material was tested and the 
economizers built under their supervision shall be furnished to the chief inspector before or with the first 
application for registration. 


(4) In advance or along with application for registration, the following shall be furnished: - 

(a) A certificate of manufacture and test in Form-XVI signed by the maker or by a responsible representative 
of the Maker, containing the description of the economiser, particulars of the materials used in its 
construction and the dimensions of the several parts with the declaration that the limits of tensile breaking 
strength and tests comply with the standard conditions. 

(0) A certificate from the maker of the material stating the tensile breaking strength and the elongation provided 
that if the maker and manufacturer be the same, the manufacturer’s precise statements showing the above 
information shall be accepted. 

(5) To suit owners’ convenience, wherever possible it is recommended that economiser be installed in two or 
more sections. 


359. Modification of formula.— Where no certificate is produced, the maximum allowable working pressure as found 
by formula will be reduced by 0%. However, when the workmanship is doubtful in any way and the chief Inspector 
is not satisfied that any of the foregoing conditions would be sufficient to meet the circumstances, he may at his 
discretion reduce the maximum allowable working pressure by such percentage as he deems fit. 


360. Maker’s certificate for steel economisers.— The maker shall furnish a certificate to the Competent Person in 
the following form: 


We hereby certify that the material described below has been made by the Open Hearth or an Electric process 
acid/basic and has been satisfactorily tested in the presence of the Competent Person in accordance with the 
standard Tests. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 743

(3) Maximum allowable working pressure shall be the highest pressure at which the economiser relief valves 
are to be set. 


(4) The above test pressure shall be held for a minimum period of ten minutes. 


362. Workmanship and manufacture.— All materials used in the construction of pressure parts shall be tested and 
shall conform to the following requirements:- 


(i) The workmanship shall be of highest standard. All castings shall be well finished, free from defects, porous 
places and blow holes, and true to dimensions without warping. Where chaplets are used, there shall be 
satisfactory fusion with the metal and chaplets shall be properly tinned with metal free from lead. 


(ii) The screw threads of all bolts shall be of whitworth forms. 


(iii) Wherever necessary, all component parts shall be manufactured to limit gauges to secure interchangeability 
throughout.

368. Joint bolts and studs for cast iron economisers.— (|) The maximum allowable working pressure for the bolts

(2) The use of studs tapped into cast iron shall be permissible where;
