temperature of the economiser shall be at least 22°C below the saturated steam temperature in the boiler drum: 


Provided that this requirement shall not apply to economizers used on low pressure water heating system 
working at pressure less than 36.5 m head of water. 


PART-4 


CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENTS FORSTEEL ECONOMISERS WITH OR WITHOUT CAST IRON 
SLEEVES ON THE TUBES 


370. Construction of Tubes.— (l) The tubes shall be manufactured as per regulation 22. 
(2) Suitable provision shall be made for supporting horizontal tubes at one or more interval in their length to relieve 
bending stresses and these supports as well as the end connections shall permit free expansion. 


37. Maximum allowable working pressure of tubes.— The maximum allowable working pressure of the tubes shall 
be calculated as per sub-regulation (.) of regulation 244, but the working metal temperature shall be taken as the 
maximum water temperature for which the part of the elements is designed plus I°C. 


372.Construction of headers.—(|)The headers shall be constructed in accordance with regulation !25. 
(2) Branches shall be secured by one of the following methods, namely: - 


(a) Expanded, belled and welded. 

(b) Strength welded with additional securing means. 

(c) Full depth strength weld. 

(d) Branches less than 3 mm bore may be screwed and seal welded. 


(3) Open ends of forged seamless steel tube headers may be closed by forging, or the ends may be secured by 
bolting, screwing, or welding in an approved manner. 


373. Maximum allowable working pressure of headers.—(l)The maximum allowable working pressure of 
rectangular headers shall be calculated as per regulation 246. 


(2) The maximum allowable working pressure of cylindrical headers shall be calculated as per regulations 69 
and 70. 


374. Attachment of tubes to headers.—(l)Tubes shall be connected to the tube plates by one of the following 
methods, namely:- 


(a) Expanding with bell mounting or seal welding. 
(0) Strength welding. 


(c) Mechanical bolted joint. 


748 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(2) Roller expanded tubes shall project through the neck or bearing part in the holes by at least 6 mm and shall 
be secured from drawing out by being bell mouthed to the extent of 0.8 mm for each 25 mm in diameter plus 
.6 mm. 


(3) (a) Tubes expanded into headers may be seal-welded inside or outside the header. 
(b) Where a seal weld is provided inside the header, the tube end projection and bell mouthed specified in 
sub-regulation (2) is not required. 


(4) In the case of roller expanded tubes the tube holes in the headers shall be formed in such a way that the tubes 
can be effectively tightened in them, there shall be a neck or belt of parallel seating of at least 3 mm. 


(5) Where the tubes are strength welded direct to the headers, the technique followed shall be approved by the 
Inspecting Authority and all welds shall be suitably heat treated. 


(6) Bolted joints shall be designed as per regulation 375. 
(7) Tubes spacers supporting clips and lugs may be welded to the tubes. 


(8) The tubes shall be so arranged that they are accessible for cleaning internally and externally.

PART-6 


376. Valves and mountings.— (l) All economisers shall be provided with thermometers for measuring water 
temperature adjacent to the inlet and outlet connections. 


(2) (a)A valve which shall prevent increase of pressure beyond a predetermined limit shall be fitted to every 
economiser and the design shall provide against unauthorized interference with the loading. Economisers with 
pressure parts of cast iron and arranged in groups of tiers connected by circulating piping shall have a relief valve 
fixed on each group or tier. Relief valves shall have a minimum orifice diameter of 9 mm. 

(b)The relief valve capacity shall be calculated on the basis of economiser thermal capacity. 

(3) Pressure gauge for indicating the pressure in the economiser shall be constructed as per regulation 232. 


(4) Air release valves shall be provided for the release of air at all points where air accumulation may occur. 


(5) Blow off drain valves shall be provided for complete drainage of water in the economiser. 


750 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(6) Economiser provided with means for heating the incoming feed by mixing it with hot water from the economiser 
outlet, shall have a non-return valve in the hot water return line. 


(7) In every case, a reserve flue shall be provided for by passing the flue gases when no water is being fed to the boiler 
through the economiser where it is not integral with boiler. 


(8) To relieve the economisers of excessive pressure accumulation due to internal explosion doors preferably of 
horizontally hinged ‘self-sealing’ type shall be fitted. 


(9) All valves and mountings shall satisfactorily withstand a hydraulic test to the same pressure as will be applied to 
the economiser during its registration. 


(0) Alternative means of feeding the boiler other than through the economiser shall be provided. 


(.l) A non-return valve shall be provided in the hot feed line between the economiser and the boiler to prevent the 
discharge of steam or water from the boiler into the economiser. 


PART-7 
FEED PIPES 


377.Maximum allowable working pressure for feed piping .—The maximum allowable working pressure shall be 
the maximum pressure generated in overcoming friction and other losses in the feed piping under ordinary working 
conditions, or the maximum pressure which can be generated by the boiler feed pumps unless special provision is 
made to prevent that pressure being communicated to the pipe line. 


Note: For boilers operating at design pressure 00 kg/cm? (g) and above feed water discharge piping for feed water 
system without economizer inlet isolating valve can be designed based on boiler design pressure with 
provision of mechanical relief device or a three way valve for bypassing H.P Heater, to prevent Boiler Feed 
Pump (BFP) shut off pressure being communicated to the piping system and with such a feed water system, 
boiler shall be hydro tested up to the last isolation valve in the feed water line. 


378. Steel feed pipes.— Steel feed pipes shall be in accordance with chapter -7. 


379. Feed Heaters and similar vessels fitted to feed pipes.— ()(a) If welded construction, such vessels shall comply 
with the requirements of Chapter-l2, provided that radiographic examination of welds may be waived for pressure 
not exceeding !7.5 kg/cm?(g). 


(b) For parts of vessels of composite construction, the requirements of the appropriate regulations of the above 
Chapters shall be complied with as may be applicable to each such part. 


(2) Maximum allowable working pressure of all parts shall be determined as per appropriate formulae given in these 
regulations and due consideration shall be given to the following additional points while calculating the stresses, 
namely. — 


The stresses due to self-weight of vessels and its contents, any super-imposed vessel or other equipments, 
pipes and other similar parts attached to the vessels, insulation and stresses due to static head, if any. 


(3) Every such vessel shall be protected with a relieving device of sufficient capacity to avoid over pressure in case 
of internal failure. 


(4) Inspection during construction, stamping and testing shall comply with the appropriate regulation of chapter-|.

PART-8 
REGISTRATION AND INSPECTION OF ECONOMISER AND FEED PIPES 


380. Preparation for inspection.— (l) (a) At each inspection, the economiser shall be emptied and thoroughly cleaned 
internally and externally and in the flues. 


(b) All mountings shall be opened up and all caps, doors and blank flanges removed to permit adequate inspection. 


(2)The owner of an economiser to which this regulation is applicable shall obtain the approval of the chief inspector 
in writing to the method of disconnection which he proposes to use and shall be responsible for ensuring that the 
method so approved is followed in practice. 


38. Procedure for registration.— () On receipt of an application for registration, the Inspector after the economiser 
has been prepared for examination, shall take full particulars of the design and ascertain the maximum allowable 
working pressure allowed by the regulations. 


(2) The fitness of the economiser parts shall be determined as per the following formulae:

regulations, the Chief Inspector shall at his discretion determine the fitness of the part. 


After inspecting the economiser and ascertaining, the maximum working pressure to which it may be worked, 
the Inspector shall witness the hydraulic test as per regulation 383 and may issue a provisional order in Form- 
XVI. 


(6) If the requirements of provisional order under sub-regulation (5) are not fulfilled, fresh provisional orders 


shall be issued subject to a maximum period of twenty four months from the date of issue of first provisional 
order, without any subsequent inspection and payment of fee. 


382. Procedure at subsequent Inspection.— (/) (a)After economiser has been cleaned, the Competent Person shall 


make a thorough examination so far as its construction permits. 


(b) The external condition of the tubes shall be carefully noted for wasting especially at the feed inlet end and all 


accessible tubes shall be calibered. 


(c) The internal surfaces of cast iron tubes shall be closely observed for graphitic wasting as far as it is possible and 
in the event of any tube failure, these shall be broken up for scrutiny so that the general internal condition of the other 


tubes may be estimated. 


(2) Where tubes or other parts are wasted, the strength shall be re-calculated. 


(3) The scraper gear shall be examined to note if any parts are missing, if the length of travel is adequate and if 


the scrapers are correctly adjusted. 


(4) All cap bolts shall be inspected and also the condition and position of the dampers and baffles. 
(5) The record of each inspection and calculations shall be entered in the Memorandum of Inspection Book. 


383. Procedure for Hydraulic Test.—(l)Every economiser for registration shall be hydraulically tested in the 
presence of Inspector to %2 times the maximum allowable working pressure. Hydraulic tests of economisers at 
subsequent examination when required by the Competent Person, shall be made after the inspection. 


754 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(2) The test pressure to be applied to economisers at subsequent examinations shall be from |.25 to |.5 times the 
maximum allowable working pressure of the economisers. During the test, all parts externally and in the flues shall 
be noted for leakage. 


384. Memorandum of Inspection Book — (l) A Memorandum of Inspection Book shall be prepared for each 
economiser in Form-X VIII and the Inspector shall enter all particulars in ink and dimensions of the economisers with 
the particulars of hydraulic test and his inspection notes in this book; 


(2) At subsequent inspection, Competent Person shall enter the dates of the Inspections, hydraulic tests when 
such are made with their notes pertaining to the condition of the various parts; 


(3) the Inspector or Competent Person, as the case may be, shall also enter in the Memorandum of Inspection 
Book, the general condition of the economiser and of repairs; 


(4) (a) On submission of the Memorandum Book to the Chief Inspector, he will in the case of newly registered 
economisers, check all particulars and calculations and approve the design pressure that is to be permitted. 
(b) In the case of old economisers, the Chief Inspector shall examine the Inspector’s notes of inspection and 
proposals made for repairs. 
(c) A pressure once approved for the economiser shall not be altered without the written authority of the Chief 
Inspector. 
(d)The Memorandum of Inspection Book shall be kept clean and up-to-date and the Inspection Book except 
when actually required by the Competent Person, shall be kept in the office of the Chief Inspector. 


385. Registration book.— (l) A registration book or copy of memorandum of inspection book for economiser 
containing all the particulars required for registration shall be maintained in the office of the Chief Inspector in Form- 
XVIII and any orders passed by him regarding the economiser shall be entered in the registration book under his 
initials. 

(2) The Chief Inspector shall also see that the note of subsequent inspections entered in the Memorandum of 


Inspection Book are copied in the Registration book. 


386.Transfer of memorandum of inspection book and registration book - On transfer of an economiser from one 
state to another, the memorandum of inspection and registration book shall, on the request of the Chief Inspector of 
the State to which the economiser has been transferred, be forwarded to that Officer who shall take over their custody 
and maintain them as prescribed. 


387. Grant of certificate. A certificate for the use of an economiser shall be granted in Form-XIX. 


388. Casual visits.— () The Inspector shall note that the economiser is working satisfactorily, the relief valves are 
correctly adjusted, the scraper gear is operating and the external brick work is free from cracks. 


(2) He shall also ascertain that the maker’s instructions for working are being strictly followed by the owner. 


Note: It is recommended that the feed inlet temperature to the economiser shall not be less than 38°C, to 
prevent sweating and consequent external corrosion of the tube and bottom headers. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 755 


389. Economiser rating.— The rating shall be equivalent to the area of the heating surface in square meters which 
shall be computed from the tubes and the headers. 


390. Registration fee.— An application for registration of Economiser shall be accompanied by appropriate fee as 
specified in regulation 304. 


३9], Fee for renewal of certificate An application for renewal of certificate of registration of economiser shall be 
accompanied by appropriate fee as specified in regulation 305. 


392. Engraving of registry number.—(|)(a) Every economiser shall have a plate with its registry number engraved, 
secured in a conspicuous place and wherever practicable stamped for identification with that number in a prominent 
place. 

(b) The engraving shall be done within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of the registry number. 


(2) A letter “E” shall be prefixed to the registry number in the denominator of the appropriate device as shown in 
regulation 30]. 


Example: UP 
E-53 


(3) The engraving shall be completed and ready for verification within thirty days from the date of receipt of the 
engraving slip from the Chief Inspector of the State. 


(4) (a) Economisers having registry devices different from those prescribed in sub-regulations (.) and (2) shall have 
such devices crossed out or erased and engraved a new registry number in conformity with those prescribed in the 
aforesaid sub-regulations. 

(b) The original numbers of such economisers shall be retained in the new device, provided that in the case of 
economisers operating in an area which consequent upon the reorganization of State forms part of another State, 
new numbers shall be given by the Chief Inspectors of the State. 

(c) A number once allotted shall not be used again in another economiser. 


393. Inspection of feed pipes.—() (a)Feed pipes shall be inspected and hydraulically tested before erection in place, 
and the hydraulic test pressure shall be not less than twice the maximum allowable working pressure of the economiser. 
(b) A certificate from the recognized maker or Inspecting Authority certifying that this has been done may be accepted. 
(c)If the Inspector or Competent Person, as the case may be, is satisfied with the test, the pipes may be erected. 

(d) Neither separate certificate for feed pipes shall be issued, nor separate fee shall be charged for their inspection. 
(e) The engraving shall be done within a period of two months from the date of receipt of the registry number. 


(2) At subsequent inspection or at any other time, the Competent Person may make an external inspection of 
feed pipes and if found in an unsatisfactory condition, he shall report the matter to the Chief Inspector who may require 
the pipes to be hydraulically tested. 


394. Submission of plans of feed pipes.— (l)The fees for the scrutiny of plans and particulars of the material, design 
and construction of feed pipes, before commencement of manufacture of the feed pipes, shall be at the rate of Rs. 200 
for 30 metres of piping or part thereof. 


(2) The fees for scrutiny of plans and particulars of the material, design and construction of any such fittings like 
feed water heater shall be charged at Rs. 2500 per fitting.

CHAPTER-2 
SHELL TYPE BOILERS OF WELDED CONSTRUCTION 
PART-I 
395. Application.— () These regulations shall apply to all boilers of fusion welded construction other than Water 
Tube boilers and Electrode boilers referred to in Chapters-4 and [0 respectively. 


(2) Where the design of the boiler is of composite construction viz. combination of Fire tube and Water Tube, it 
shall comply with the relevant regulations governing that particular type of construction. 


396. General requirements. — Wherever applicable, the general requirements of Chapter-| relating to certificates 
from Makers, Inspecting Authorities, and the like and of Chapter-3 concerning construction, shall be followed. 


397. Equipment of workshop. — (l) The welding plant and equipment shall be of good quality and maintained in an 
efficient working condition. The welding apparatus shall be installed under cover and arranged so that welding work 
may be carried out in positions free from draughts and adverse weather conditions. The procedure shall be such that 
there is regular and systematic supervision of the welding works, and the welding operators shall be subjected to 
periodic tests for quality of workmanship by the works officials. Records of these tests shall be kept and shall be made 
available to the Competent Person for scrutiny. 


(2) The works shall be equipped with welding plant equipment and quality control personnel. However, the 
equipment for destructive, non-destructive testing and heat treatment are not necessary. The manufacturer can tie-up 
for these facilities outside and a letter from the party with whom he makes a tie-up shall be made available to the Chief 
Inspector of Boilers or the Inspecting Authority or his representative and shall be allowed to inspect the material of 
the party in the laboratory during the test. 


398.Materials of construction. — Plates, sections and bars used in the construction of these boilers shall comply with 
the requirements of Chapter-2in all respects. However, where the tensile strength exceeds 49.6 kg/mm/, the full details 
of the welding technique including pre-heating and post-heating, and the plate preparation to be used, shall be 
submitted to Inspecting Authority for approval before commencement of manufacture. 


399. Welding consumables. — Where welding consumables are used , they shall comply with the requirements of 
regulations 7! to 76, save in the case of the weld metal as deposited, where the tensile strength shall not be less than 
the lower limit specified for the plate. 


400. Plain and Stay Tubes. — (|) Tubes shall comply with the provisions of regulations 30,47 and 48. 
(2) Seamless steel cross-tubes and uptake tubes shall come with regulations 99 and l00respectively. 


40i. Construction and workmanship.— The manufacturer shall provide Inspecting Authority with a fully 
dimensioned sectional drawing showing the construction of the boiler in full detail for approval before putting the 
work in hand. Full details including dimensions of plates preparation for the longitudinal and circumferential seams 
shall also be shown on the drawing. Fully dimensioned sketches showing in details the attachment for stand-pipes, 
branch pipes and seatings, the position of these attachments relative to the longitudinal and circumferential seams and 
other opening shall also be given in the drawing. 


402. Preparation of plates. — For preparation of plates, requirements of regulation 77 shall apply. When plates of 
different thickness are aligned, the welding shall be matched to the lower thickness plate and tolerance as required for 
thinner plate. (refer Figure 2/). 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 757 


403. Stress relieving. — Requirements of regulation 78 shall apply. 
404. Cylindrical shells. — Requirements of regulation 80 shall apply. 


405. Circularity. — (l) The difference between the maximum and minimum internal diameters of the shell measured 
at any one cross section shall not exceed one per cent of the nominal internal diameter. 


(2) The profile as measured on the outside of the boiler by means of a gauge of the designed form of the 
exterior of the boiler, having a length equal to one quarter of the internal diameter, shall not depart from the designed 


form by more than the percentage given in Table 2/I.

(3) There shall be no flats at the welded seams and any local departure from circularity shall be gradual. 


406. End plates, crown plates and tube plates.— (|) End plate of welded Lancashire and Cornish boilers shall be 
flanged for attachment to shell plates. 


(2) For requirements of end plates of boilers, sub-regulation (l) of regulation 86 shall apply. 
(3) For requirements of hemispherical crowns, regulation 89 shall apply. 
(4) For requirements of flanging, sub-regulation (2) of regulation 86 shall apply. 


(5) In the construction of unfired boilers when the dished ends do not form a part of the heating surface, cold spun 
dished ends conforming to IS: 2825 may be used. 


(6) Where flats are pressed in dished end plates, for the attachment of mountings they shall be formed with an ample 
radius at the junction of the flat and curved surfaces, and shall be free from sharp corners or tool marks. The plate 
shall not be unduly thinned. 


(7) (a) Plates which are flanged in accordance with sub-regulation (4), shall be welded to the parts to which they are 
to be connected as follows:

(iv) to combustion chamber or firebox wrapper plates as shown in Figure ।2/9.

(i) to shells as shown in Figure 2/2 or 2/(3.

(ii) to internal flue tubes or uptakes as shown in Figure 2/7. 
(iii) to combustion chamber or firebox wrapper plates as shown in Figures 2/20, 2/2 or 2/22. 


(c) Where dished ends or crowns are used, they shall be flanged for connection to the shell or the cylindrical 
portion of the firebox. Flat shell and firebox crown plates of vertical boilers shall also be flanged for connection to the 
cylindrical portions of the shell or firebox. 


(d)The opening in the firebox crown plate of a vertical boiler for the uptake shall be flanged and the connection 
to the uptake made by means of a circumferential butt-weld. (see Figures 2/3, 2/4, 2/5, 2/6). 


407. Internal flues.— () Sections of internal flues shall each be made from one plate, which shall be rolled while 
cold to circular form. The longitudinal seam shall be fusion butt-welded by the metal arc process. 


(2) The maximum permissible variation in diameter of any cross-section shall not exceed 6 mm or half of the 
thickness of the plate, whichever is greater. 


(3) The longitudinal welds shall be placed at lower part of the furnace and shall break joint in successive sections 
at least by 50 mm. This requirement shall not be applicable if successive sections are separated by tube plate 
or end plate or bowling hoops. 


(4) Where flue sections are flanged for circumferential joints, the flanging shall be carried out at one heat by 
suitable machinery. 


(5) Edges of all flue flanges shall be machined or flame-cut by machine (see regulation 402). 


(6) Flanged circumferential seams shall be so arranged that they do not fall in line with those of the adjacent flue 
or with circumferential seams of the shell. 


(7) The minimum mean internal diameter of furnaces shall not be less than those given in Figure [2/23 depending 
on the net heat input. 


(8) Where furnace flue is made up of plain or corrugated sections or both, they may be connected to each other 
by fusion butt welded circumferential seams. 


(9) (a) Plain furnaces shall not exceed 3 meter in length except in the case of reverse flame boilers, which are 
considered to be inherently flexible or as provided in clause (d). In all other cases flexibility shall be provided 
in the furnace by means of corrugations or blowing hoops or stepping of a minimum of 50 mm in the diameter 
of the furnace. (see figures ]2/24 to 2/28. 


(b)If corrugations are used to provide flexibility, at least one-third of the furnace length shall be corrugated. 
(c)Breathing spaces as per regulation 483 shall be provided for boilers made as per this clause. 


(d) Notwithstanding the provisions of clauses (a) and (b), plain furnaces longer than 3 meter are allowed to 
be used in a boiler when the length between boiler end plates do not exceed 6.5 meters provided that 
breathing spaces used in this case are in accordance with regulation 484 . 


(0) Where a complete flue is constructed of short plain sections, the ends of each adjoining section shall either 
be swaged out to a radius to provide an adequate point of support and longitudinal flexibility and butt-welded 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 759 


together or be butt-welded to each side of a bowling hoop. The dimensions shall comply with Figures |2/3], 
2/32 or 2/33. 


(.) Stress relieving by heat-treatment shall be carried out when the construction of a flue involves the use of a 
circumferential weld such stress relieving being carried out on the completion of all welding in accordance 
with regulation 453. 


(2) The forms of flue connections to end plates shall be as shown in Figures 2/4, 2/I5, 2/6, l2/I7 and 2/8 
or be in any other form of welding groove subject to the approval of the Inspecting Authority. 


408. Uptakes.— (l) The uptakes shall be formed from seamless or electric resistance welded or fusion butt-welded 
pipes by electric arc process. The tolerances on these pipes shall comply with the requirements of regulation 25[. The 
uptakes shall be fusion butt welded to the upward flange of the opening of the furnace crown plate in accordance with 
Figures 2/3 and 2/4. The depth of the flange of the firebox crown plate opening from the commencement of the 
curvature of flange shall be not less than twice the plate thickness with a minimum of 25 mm. Unless the whole boiler 
is to be subsequently stress relieved, the uptake and firebox crown plate shall be effectively stress relieved after 
welding. Where the firebox crown plate is also fusion welded to the body of the firebox as in Figure 2/6, the firebox 
complete with uptake shall be effectively stress relieved by heat treatment on completion of all welding. 


(2) The uptake may be attached to the shell crown as indicated on Figure 2/7 before the boiler is finally 
stress relieved by heat treatment. 


(3) Where the vertical seam of the uptake is fusion welded, the welding shall comply with regulation 
432 and the weld shall be so arranged that it is welded externally and internally (see Figure 2/42) 
(4) It is desirable that the uptake shall be fitted with an internal cast iron liner extending below the low 


water level. 
409.Cross-tubes.—Requirements of regulation 99 shall apply. 


PART-2 
Fireboxes and Combustion chambers 


40.Furnace of vertical boilers— (.) The furnaces of vertical boilers may be constructed in one or more lengthwise 
sections, each section being rolled from one plate to a full circle. In such cases, the component sections may be jointed 
circumferentially by electric butt-welding. The welding shall be stress relieved in accordance with regulation 432. 


(2) In the case of vertical boilers where tube plates form part of the firebox, the tube plate portion may be 
constructed in two vertical sections and the welding of the vertical seams when welded shall be stress relieved. 


(3) The maximum permissible variation in diameter, at any cross-section shall not exceed 6 mm for fireboxes up 
to 900 mm in diameter, or !0 mm for fireboxes over 900 mm in diameter, or half the thickness of the plate whichever 
is the greater. 


(4) Circular fireboxes shall preferably be tapered. A taper of 38 mm in diameter per 300 mm of height is 
recommended. The water space at the bottom between the firebox and the shell shall be not less than 50 mm for boilers 
up to and including 760 mm in diameter and shall be not less than 63 mm for boilers over 760 mm in diameter. 


(5) The method of welding shall be in accordance with regulation 432. 


(6) Flats formed in the firebox for the insertion of water tubes shall have an ample radius at the junction of the 
flat and the curved surfaces and shall be free from sharp corners or tool marks. The plate shall not be unduly thinned. 


760 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(7) Ogee flanging whether integral with the firebox or made as separate ring shall preferably be formed in one 
heat by suitable machinery and shall be allowed to cool gradually to avoid internal stresses. 


(8) Rings of fire holes mouthpieces or foundation rings shall be made of mild steel. ‘Z’ sections shall not be used 
for foundations rings. 


(9) Attachment of fireboxes to cylindrical shells shall be in accordance with Figures !2/34, 2/35, 2/36 or 2/37.

PART-3 
44. Bar stays and firebox stays.— (l) Each bar stay or firebox stay shall be made from a solid rolled bar without 
weld in its length, except where it is attached to the plate it supports. 


(2) Bar stays which have been worked in the fire shall be subsequently annealed. 


(3) Itis preferred that when the stay is in position in the boiler, its axis shall be normal to the plate it supports, 
but where this cannot be so arranged, then, if the stay is fitted with nuts, bevelled washers shall be provided 
between the nuts and the plate.

to 48. 


45.Bar stays.— ()Plain bars, passing through clearing holes in the plates and welded thereto (see Figure |2/50). 


(2) Plain bars passing through clearing holes in the plates and fitted with washers on the outside, the stay and 
washers being welded to the plates in accordance with any one of the methods shown in Figures 2/52, 2/53, |2/54, 
2/55, 2/56, 2/57, 2/58, 2/59. 


Note: Clearing hole for the purpose of this regulation mean a machined cylindrical hole having a 
diameter not exceeding that of bar stay by more than 2%. 


46.Firebox Stays.— (.) (a) Screwed stays, screwed through the plates and riveted over at each end to form substantial 
heads, or fitted with nuts, or the projecting ends fillet-welded as indicated in Figures | 2/47 and 2/48. 


(b) It is recommended that where the stays are screwed, this shall be with a fine thread and the stays and holes 
shall be screwed with a continuous thread. 


(c)The stays shall be screwed with fine threads of not less than |] threads per 25 mm. 


(d)The screw threads on the stays shall be clean, free from checks or imperfections, of full depth, or a correct 
standard form and a good fit in the holes. The middle portion shall preferably be turned down to the bottom of 
the thread. 


(2) Plain stays shall be strength welded to the plates (see Figure 2/49 and 2/50). 
NOTE: This form of attachment is also suitable for plain bar stays. 
(3) All screwed stays less than 350 mm long shall preferably be drilled with a tell-tale hole of5 mm diameter to a 
depth of !3 mm beyond the inner face of the plate. Stays which are obscure on one side shall preferably be 


made from hollow stay bar. 


47. Girder stays for firebox and combustion chamber crowns.— (l) Where girder stays are attached with stay 
bolts and nuts, they shall be bedded to the corners or ends of side plates. 


(2) The attachment of girder stays welded directly to the crown plates shall comply with Figures 2/60, 2/6], 
2/62, 2/63 or 2/64. Such girders shall be welded to the crown plate prior to stress-relieving. 


(3) Each girder shall be of sufficient strength to support its due proportion of the load on the crown 
plate independently of the crown plate, and the bolts or weld attachments shall have sufficient cross-sectional area to 


carry the applied load. 


(4) The waterways between the underside of the girder and the crown plate shall be as large as 
practicable, but in no case less than 38 mm deep. 


48. Gusset Stays.— Requirements of sub-regulation(l) of regulation 2 shall apply.

420. Manhole frames, mouthpieces and doors.— (|) Manhole frames, mouth-pieces, doors or cover plates shall be

where of the flanged type shall be bedded closely to the shell. 


(2) Wherever practicable, the frame shall be attached to the inside of the shell with the shorter axis parallel to 
the longitudinal centre line of the boiler. In all cases where the shell thickness exceeds |4 mm, oval frames 
or circular mouth-pieces shall be fitted. 


(3) Oval frames and externally raised circular mouthpieces shall be either: 
(a) Formed in one piece without weld, or 


(b) Formed from a suitable rolled section and forge-welded, or fabricated by fusion welding, provided they are 
stress-relieved by heat-treatment after welding and before attaching to the boiler unless the whole boiler is to 
be subjected to heat-treatment on completion. 


(4) Welds shall be positioned so that they are located on the transverse centre line of the boiler (see regulation 
430). 


(5) The joining flanges of mouthpieces and covers shall be machined on the face and edges and on the bearing 
surface for the bolts. Bolts and nuts shall be machined where in contact with the flanges and the joints shall

423. Stand Pipes.— Where stand pipes are used, the flanges shall be machined or flame-cut by machine on the edges. 
The bolting flanges shall be machined on the jointing and bolting surfaces. 


424. Saddles.— Where saddles are used, the edges of the flanges shall be machined or flame-cut by machine. The 
joining surfaces shall be machined. The studs for the attachment of the mountings, if screwed through the saddle, shall 
be fitted on the inside with nuts of full thickness. Where the stud holes do not penetrate through the saddles the length 
of the screwed portion of the stud in the plate shall be not less than the diameter of the stud. 


425. Pads.— Where pads are used, the joining surfaces shall be machined. The pads shall have sufficient thickness to 
allow drilling of the stud holes for mountings without inner surface being pierced and the length of the screwed portion 


of the stud in the pad shall be not less than the diameter of the stud. 


426.Attachment of standpipes.—(|)The following constructions as to standpipes attached to shells and end plates 
shall be permissible:- 


(i) When the internal diameter of the standpipe does not exceed 25 mm the standpipe may be screwed into the 
plate with a nut on the waterside. 


(ii) Where the internal diameter of the standpipe exceeds 25 mm but does not exceed 50 mm, it may be screwed 
in and seal welded. 


(iii) Where the diameter of the standpipe exceeds 50 mm, it may be welded to the end plate. 


(2) The provisions in sub-regulation (() as to the standpipe attachment shall be regulated by the following 
conditions- 


(i) When standpipes are screwed, the screwing shall be of standard pipe thread. 
(ii) Standpipes shall be attached by one of the methods shown in Figures 2/04, 2/05, 2/06,2/07,

the Inspecting Authority.

(iii) Where the standpipes are fabricated by fusion-welding, they shall be stress relieved by heat-

completion. 

(iv) Where the bore of the standpipe does not exceed !27 mm or the diameter of the opening in the shell 


does not exceed 27 mm plus twice the thickness of the plate to which it is attached, the standpipe 
may be welded to the plate without subsequent heat-treatment of the welds made. If these limits are

427.Attachment of pads.—(|) Pads welded to the shell or end plate shall be welded internally and externally.

seating does not exceed 27 mm or the diameter of the opening in the shell does not exceed 27 mm plus twice the 
thickness of the plate to which it is attached, the pad may be welded to the plate without subsequent heat-treatment of 
the welds so made. If these limits are exceeded the whole plate to which the pad is attached shall be stress relieved by 
heat-treatment on completion of welding. 


428.Attachment of water and pressure gauges.— Water gauges and pressure gauge siphons may be attached direct 
to the front end plate without the intervention of a pad or standpipe, provided they are flanged and secured by studs. 
If the studs are screwed through the plate, nuts of full thickness shall be fitted on the inside of the plate. 


429.Bolts and Nuts.— All holes for bolts and studs shall be drilled and bolts and nuts shall be machined where in 
contact with the flanges. 


PART-6 
430. Compensating plates — Compensating plates shall be of same material as that of shell and before attachment, 
shall bed closely to the plates to which they are to be connected. Any weld therein shall be on the transverse centre 
line. 


43. Definition of the term ‘fusion weld’ — () For the purpose of this chapter, the term ‘fusion weld’ is applicable 
to all welded seams made by the metal arc process with covered electrodes or by any other electric arc process in 
which the arc stream and the deposited weld metal are shielded from atmospheric contamination. 


(2) The relevant provisions of this chapter shall also apply to the single run or heavy run welding process and 
that welded boilers manufactured by that process shall comply with all regulations of this chapter excepting those in 
which divergence is necessary solely because of special requirements essential for the most efficient utilisation of that 
process. Thus all regulation governing quality of material construction workmanship, and testing (both non-destructive 
and otherwise) are applicable. 


(3) Where welded shells conforming to the regulations of this chapter are made by single or heavy run process, 
it shall be understood that regulations 43 |,432 and 433 do not apply in their entirety. The method of making the 
welds shall be approved by the Inspecting Authority. 


432. Methods of welding.— (|) The seams shall be fusion welded from both sides of the plates. The main welding 
may be on either side of the plate, whichever it is most convenient to the manufacturer. Before the second side of the 
plate is welded, the weld metal at the bottom of the first side shall be removed by grinding, chipping, machining or 
other approved method. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 765 


(2) Provided the requisite quality of welding is achieved, the seams may be welded from both sides of the 
plate or from one side of the plate. Before the second side of the plate is welded, the metal at the bottom of the first 
side shall be removed by grinding, chipping, machining or other approved method. 


(3) Additional runs of metal shall be deposited at both surfaces of the welded seams to ensure that the weld 
metal at the level of the surfaces of the plate is refined as far as possible. 


(4) Thickness of such additional welding shall not exceed values given in following table.

(5) The surfaces of the welds which are to be subsequently radiographed shall be sufficiently free from coarse 
ripples, overlap, grooves, abrupt ridges and valleys, so as to avoid stress raisers and to permit proper 
interpretation of radiographs and other Non-Destructive Test (NDT) methods. If there is a question 
regarding the surface condition of the weld when interpreting a radiographic film, the film shall be 
compared to the actual weld surface or provide smooth contours and to be flush with the respective 
surfaces of the plate before radiography examination is done. 


(6) In the case of circumferential shell seams welded by submerged arc or any other approved automatic 
process producing a similar surface finish, such circumferential welds, need not be flush dressed, subject 
to their surface finish and shape being acceptable to the Inspecting Authority. 


(7) Undercut shall not exceed 0.8mm or 0% of wall thickness, whichever is less and undercut shall not 
encroach on design wall thickness. 


(8) The positions of the welds shall be marked, compensation plates, doubling plates or manhole frames, not 
less than two runs or metal shall be deposited at each weld. 


(9) When affixing standpipes, branch pipes, seatings, compensation plates, doubling plates or manhole 
frames, not less than two runs or metal shall be deposited at each weld. 


(0) Each run of weld metal shall be thoroughly cleaned and freed from slag before the next run is deposited. 


433. Types of welded shell seams.— The longitudinal and intermediate circumferential seams shall be made with butt 
joints of the single or double U or V type (see Figures !2/3, 2/4, 2/5, and 2/6) or of any other type approved by the 
Inspecting Authority. End circumferential seams shall be in accordance with Figures 2/7, 2/8, 2/9, [2//0, 2/l or 
2/i2 or with any other form approved by the Inspecting Authority.

434. Repairs to welded seams.— () Any repair to a weld carried out by the manufacturer shall first be agreed to by 
the Competent person. 


(2) (a)Where defects are distributed over the whole length of the seam, the total length of the portions which 
may be cut from any one longitudinal or circumferential seam to remove all defects shall not exceed I5 
percent of the total length of the seam. 


(b) When, however, the defects are all located in a single continuous length which may be cut out to 
remove all defects shall not exceed l0 percent of the total length of the seam. 


(3) Defect shall be cut out by chipping, machining or other approved methods. 
(4) In the case of Class I boilers, all repaired areas shall be subjected to radiographic examination. 


435.Tests on welded seams of shell.—() Test plates to represent all welded seams shall be attached at each end of 
each longitudinal seam. These shall be of a size sufficient for the preparation of the test pieces specified. In the case 
of shell plates, the test plate may be located at one end only (see Figure 2/58). Where the shell is formed in two or 
more rings, the staggered longitudinal seam shall be regarded as a continuous longitudinal seam provided the welding 
be effected in one reasonably continuous operation and by the same operator or operators. The material for the test 
plates shall be cut from the respective plate or plates forming the appropriate seam. 


(2) In the case of insufficient material being available on the shell plate to permit the cutting of test pieces, these shall 
be acceptable if they are made from another plate, provided it is made from the same cast. The test plates shall be 
stamped by the Inspecting Authority before being cut. 


(3) The weld groove in the test plates shall be similar to that adopted for the corresponding edges of the 
longitudinal seam, and the respective fusion faces shall be in continuous alignment. The test plates may be reinforced 
or supported during welding so that any relative displacement due to warping during welding does not exceed 5°. The 
weld metal in the test plates and the seam shall be deposited continuously at the same operation. 


(4) The weld in any test plate shall not be repaired. If any defects are revealed in the weld metal of a test plate 
the position of this shall be clearly marked on the plate and the test pieces shall be selected from such parts of the test 
plates as may be decided by the Competent Person. 


(5) Test plates warped during welding by not more than 5° may be straightened before heat-treatment. For the 
heat-treatment of the test plates (see regulation 453). 


(6) Where there are circumferential seams only or where the method of welding the circumferential seams differ 
from that employed for the longitudinal seams, the test plates shall be provided.

436.Test of Class I boilers —() Specimens for the following tests shall be selected from the test plate or plates and 
stamped by the Competent Person for identification (see Figures 2/7] and 2/72). 


(i) One tensile test specimen for the welded seam. 
(ii) One all weld metal tensile test specimen. 
(iii) Two bend test specimens. 


(iv) Two impact test specimens. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 767 


(५) One specimen from each test plate for macro examination. 


(2) The dimensions of the specimens shall be in accordance with the sketches in Figures 2/73, 2/74, 2/76,2/77 and 
2/78. The remainder of the test plates shall be retained for re-tests, if required. Any specimen for re-test shall be cut 
from the same test plate as the original specimen. Specimens representing welded seams shall, if necessary, be 
straightened cold before the commencement of machining. Tensile and bend specimens shall, if practicable, be of the 
full plate thickness. Surfaces of tensile, bend and Charpy specimens corresponding with the outside or inside of the 
boiler shall be lightly dressed only so that the rolled surface of the parent metal is not wholly removed. Where the rolled 
surfaces of the abutting plates are not level with one another one plate may be machined at each face of the weld so long 
as the depth of the metal removed does not exceed 0.8 mm. 


437. Tensile tests— (|) Welded joint; the dimensions of the reduced tensile section shall be as shown in Figure |2/73. 
The width of the reduced section shall be at least 25 mm. 


(2) If the thickness of the plate does not exceed 30 mm, the thickness of the specimen shall be equal to the plate thickness 
and the plate surface of the specimen shall be machined to take away the surface irregularities of the plate and the 
weld. 


(3) If the plate thickness exceeds 30 mm, the tensile test shall be carried out on several reduced section specimens, each 
having a thickness of at least 30 mm and width at the effective cross-section of at least 25 mm. These specimens shall 
be taken out of the test piece in such a way that the tensile test covers the whole thickness of the weld joints as shown 
in Figure |2/74. The tensile strength shall not be less than the lower limit specified for the plate. 


(4) The dimensions of the all weld metal tensile test specimen shall be those given in Figure |2/77. The diameter shall be 
the maximum possible consistent with the cross section of the weld but in no case more than 20 mm, the gauge length 
shall be equal to five times the diameter. The tensile strength shall not be less than the lower limit specified for the 
plate. The elongation shall not be less than 20% on a gauge length of five times the diameter of the specimen or 5.65 
times the square root of the cross-sectional area of the specimen, and the reduction in area not less than 35 percent. 


438.Cold bend tests — () Two bend tests shall be made as given in this regulation. 

(2) One specimen shall be tested with the outer surface of the weld in tension and the other with the inner surface in 
tension. The specimen shall be rectangular in section and shall be cut out transversely to the weld so as to have a width 
not less than one-and-a half times the thickness of the plates. The sharp corners of the specimens shall be rounded to 
a radius not exceeding 0% of the thickness of the specimen. 

(3) Where the plate thickness does not exceed 32 mm, the thickness of the specimen shall be equal to the full thickness 
of the test plate. Where the plate thickness exceeds 32 mm, the specimen shall in all cases have a thickness of at least 
32 mm. The specimen to be tested with the outer surface of the weld in tension shall be prepared by cutting to waste 
the metal local to the inner surface of the weld, so that the desired specimen thickness is obtained (see A, Figure 
2/78). 

(4) The specimen to be tested with the inner surface in tension shall be prepared by cutting to waste the metal local to 
the outer surface of the weld so that the desired specimen thickness is obtained (See B, Figure 2/78). Where the 
thickness of the plate permits, both specimens may be cut from the same piece of plate, the specimens being located 
in the plate one above the other (see C, Figure |2/78). Each specimen shall be mounted with the weld midway between 
the supports set apart at a distance of not more than 5.2 times the thickness of the specimen and pushed through the 
supports with a former having a diameter equal to three times the thickness of the specimen. 

(5) On completion of the test, no crack or defect at the outer surface of the specimen shall be greater than |.5 mm measured 
across the specimen or 3 mm measured along the length of the specimen. Premature failure at corners or the specimen 
shall not be considered cause for rejection. 


439. Impact tests.— Impact tests shall be as per regulation 62.

440.Macro and micro examinations.—(l) A specimen of the full thickness of the plate and not less than 3 mm wide 
shall be provided from each set of test plates for the purpose of macro and micro examinations. 


(2) Micro-etching of a complete cross-section of the weld including the heat affected zone shall show satisfactory 
penetration, fusion and absence of significant inclusions or other defects. In case there is any doubt as to the condition of 
the weld as shown by macro-etching, the area concerned is to be microscopically examined for defect investigation.

443. Radiographic examinations.— (l) Every portion of the longitudinal and circumferential butt-welded seams of the 


shell of the boiler shall be subjected to radiographic or ultrasonic examination. Each Longitudinal and circumferential 
butt welded seams of Furnace, Reversal chamber, Access tube and drop pipes shall be subjected to 0% radiographic 
examination. The percentage of welds to be examined shall include each intersection of longitudinal and 
circumferential seams. Where ultrasonic examination is used, it shall be demonstrated to the satisfaction of the 
Inspecting Authority that the equipment and the technique used are satisfactory. The manufacturer shall ensure that 
the operator employed is competent to use the equipment, apply the technique and interpret the results of the 
examination. 


(2) The methods employed in obtaining the radiographs shall be such as to show clearly differences equal to 2% of the 


(3) 


thickness at the welded joints. To determine whether this result is being attained, an indicator of approved form which 
includes a portion equivalent to not more than2% of the joint thickness shall be placed in the vicinity of the weld so 
as to make a record on each radiograph. Each section of every weld shall be marked so that the radiographs can be 
easily correlated to the particular part of the seam represented. 


The examination shall be made from the original films and the acceptability of the welds shall be decided by the 
Inspecting Authority. The welds deemed unsatisfactory shall be rejected or dealt with under the condition of regulation 
434 and can be radiographed again. The films shall be retained by the manufacturer for minimum three years for 
reference.

repaired areas shall be re-examined using the same radioscopic technique to 
evaluate the effectiveness of the repair. 


To aid in proper interpretation of the radioscopic examination data, the details 
of the technique used shall accompany the data. As a minimum, the 


770 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


information shall include the approved procedure requirements and system 
performance test data.

444. Test for class II boilers.— (l) Test pieces shall be selected from each longitudinal seam for the following 
tests and stamped by the Competent Person for identification. 


(i) From the test plate or plates: 

(ii) One tensile test specimen for welded seam. 
(iii) One bend test specimen. 

(iv) One reverse bend test specimen. 

(v) One nick-break test specimen. 


(2) The disposition of the specimen shall be in accordance with the sketches in Figure |2/79. 
The remainder of each test plate shall be retained for retests, if required. 


445.Tensile test— The dimensions of the test specimen shall be in accordance with the sketch in Figure 
2/73:SpecimenlA, and the specimen shall be cut out transversely to the welded seam. When the capacity of the 
available testing machine does not allow full specimen to be tested, two narrower tensile specimens shall be 
substituted. These specimens shall be the full thickness of the plate at the welded joint and their breadth shall be 
as great as the testing machine will reasonably allow, provided the effective cross sectional area of the test piece 
is not less than 968 mm? (see Figure [2/74: specimen B). The tensile strength of the welded joint specimen shall 
not be less than the lower limit specified for the plate. 


446.Cold bend tests — () Two bend tests shall be made as given in this regulation. 


(2) One specimen shall be tested with outer surface of the weld in tension, and the other with the inner surface 
in tension. The specimens shall be rectangular in section and shall be cut out transversely to the weld so as 
to have a width not less than one-and-a-half times the thickness of the plate. The sharp corners of the 
specimens shall be rounded to a radius not exceeding l0 percent of the thickness of the specimen. 


(3) The specimen to be tested with the outer surface of the weld in tension shall be prepared by cutting to waste 
the metal local to the inner surface of the weld, so that the desired specimen thickness is obtained (see A, Figure 
2/78). The specimen to be tested with inner surface in tension shall be prepared by cutting to waste the metal 
local to the outer surface of the weld so that the desired specimen thickness is obtained (see B, Figure |2/78). 
Where the thickness of the plate permits, both specimens may be cut from the same piece of plate, the 
specimens being located in the plate one above the other (See C, Figure |2/78). 


(4) Each specimen shall be mounted with the weld midway between the supports set apart at a distance of not 
more than 5.2 times the thickness of the specimen and pushed through the supports with a former having a diameter 
equal to three times the thickness of the specimen. 


(5) On completion of the test, no crack or defect at the outer surface of the specimen shall be greater than .6 
mm measured across the specimen, or 3 mm measured along the length of the specimen. Premature failure at 
corners of the specimen shall not be considered cause for rejection.

-Nick-break specimen .— (|) This specimen shall have a width not less than one and a half times its thickness and 
the slot shall be cut in each side of the specimen through the centre of the weld and perpendicular to the outer face 
of the boiler. 

(2) The specimen shall then be broken in the weld and the fracture shall reveal a sound homogenous weld 
substantially free from slag inclusions, porosity and coarse crystallinity. 


Additional tests before rejection.— In case any of the test specimens fails, two retests shall be made and both 
shall meet the specified requirements. 


Specimen after tests.— If required, specimens after tests shall be at the disposal of the Inspecting Authority for 
examination.

(including shell to end plate) shall be subjected to spot radiographic or ultrasonic examination.

482. Breathing space.— Breathing spaces as provided in regulations 483,484 or 485shall be provided depending on 
the design of the boiler with special attention to the provision of sub-regulation (9) of regulation 407 regarding 
furnaces. 


483.For boilers as per clause (a)of sub-regulation (9) of regulation 407.— 


(.) Stays shall be arranged to give sufficient breathing space around the furnace connections and tube 
nests (see figure 2/9! and 2/93), and shall divide the unstayed areas equally. 


(2) (a) In case of multi-tubular boilers, for both front and rear attachment of furnaces, the breathing 
spaces between furnace and tube nests or between furnace and shell shall be minimum of 50 mm 
or 5% of the shell inside diameter, whichever is larger, with a maximum requirement of !00 mm. 


(b) Clearances between the furnace and wet-back wrapper plates shall not require consideration as 
breathing spaces. 

(c)In the case of reverse flame boilers, the breathing space at the front end between furnace and the tube 
nests shall be not less than 50 mm and the breathing space formed by the outer-annular area of the 
furnace rear plate shall be not less than 50 mm or 5% of the shell inside diameter, whichever is 
larger, with a maximum of !00 mm. 


(d) Breathing spaces between gusset or link stays and tube ends shall be not less than !00 mm. 
Clearances between the tubes and wet-back wrapper plates shall not require consideration as 
breathing spaces. 


(e ) Breathing spaces between tubes and shell shall not be less than 40 mm. 


(f) Breathing spaces between gusset or link stays and furnaces shall be not less than 200 mm except 
that for shell outside diameters exceeding 800 mm and furnace length exceeding 6000 mm they

(g) All other breathing spaces shall be a minimum of 50 mm or 3% of the shell inside diameter, 
whichever is larger, with a maximum requirement of !00 mm.

503.Hydraulic test.— () (a) Each Class I Boiler shall, on completion of all welding and/or repairs and after heat- 
treatment, be subjected to a hydraulic test of l.5 times the design pressure without any indication of weakness or 
defect. 

(0) Each Class II and Class II Boiler shall be tested to a pressure twice the design pressure. 


(2) (a) The test shall be witnessed by the Inspecting Authority or Competent Person. 


(b) The test pressure shall be maintained for a period not less than 30 minutes. 
(c) In the interest of safety, it is important that the boiler be properly vented, so as to prevent the formation 


of air pockets, before the test pressure as applied. 


Notes: 

l. Itis recommended that the temperature of the water shall not be less than 7°C during the hydraulic test. 

2. Itis further recommended that before the boiler is approached for close examination, the pressure shall 
be reduced to not less than |.! times the design pressure and not more than 0.9 times the hydraulic test 
pressure. 

3. Oncompletion of hydraulic test, release of pressure shall be gradual. 
Deflection of different pressure parts shall be examined carefully and there shall not be any permanent 
set after release of pressure. 


(3) If any repairs are found to be necessary during or subsequent to the hydraulic pressure test, the boiler shall 
again be subjected to the pressure test specified above after completion of the repairs and after any heat 
treatment provided repaired weld joint requires heat treatment as per regulation 453. 


Note: Observations and remarks of Competent Person/ Inspecting Authority shall be recorded for filing with 
maker’s papers. 


504.Safety valves.— Boiler shall be provided safety valves complying with regulations 92 to 29, with following 
changes:- 


(i) The safety valves shall be reset at a pressure at least 2.5% below, but not more than 5% below the safety valve set 
pressure. 


(ii) The 5% limit is increased to l0% for valves having a body seat bore less than 32 mm and or having a set pressure 
of 24 bar gauge or less.

836 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


CHAPTER-3 


QUALIFICATION TESTS FOR WELDERS AND WELDING OPERATORS ENGAGED IN WELDING 
AND REPAIR OF BOILERS AND BOILER COMPONENTS, PIPES, HEAT EXCHANGER AND HEAT 
EXCHANGER COMPONENTS UNDER CONSTRUCTION, ERECTION AND FABRICATION AT SITE. 


505. Application.— (|) These regulations shall apply to testing of welders and welding operators engaged in welding 
and repair of boilers and boiler components, steam-pipes, heat exchanger and heat exchanger components of ferrous 
and nonferrous material under construction, erection and fabrication at site. 


PART-I 
Definitions 


506. Welder.— Welder means a person who performs manual or semi-automatic welding. 
507.Welding operator — Welding operator means a person who operates machine or automatic welding equipment. 


508. Reasonable continuity of service— The continuity of service of the welder or welding operator shall be 
considered as continuity of service if he retains the initial skill level though not engaged in welding for a period of 
upto six months. 

509. U-Number.—(l) U Number grouping of electrodes and welding consumables in table 3/5 of regulation 520 is 
based essentially on their usability characteristics, which determine the ability of welders to make satisfactory welds 
with a given welding consumables. 

(2) This grouping is intended to reduce the number of welding performance qualifications. 


PART-2 
Welding Positions 
50.Plate groove welding.— The welding positions as mentioned in Figure |3/] of this chapter shall be as following, 
namely:- 
(i)Flat position 3/LGF; Plate in a horizontal plane with the weld metal deposited from above. 
(ii) Horizontal Position 3/LGH; Plate in a vertical plane with the axis of the weld horizontal. 
(iii) Vertical Position 3/LGV; Plate in a vertical plan with the axis of the weld vertical. 


(iv) | Overhead Position 3/LGO; Plate in a horizontal plane with the weld metal deposited from underneath. 


5]. Plate fillet welding — The welding positions as mentioned in Figure |3/2 of this chapter shall be as following, 
namely:- 

(i) Flat Position 3/LFF; Plates so placed that the weld is deposited with its axis horizontal and its throat 
vertical 

(ii) Horizontal Position 3/LFH; Plates so placed that the weld is deposited with its axis horizontal on 
the upper side of the horizontal surface and against the vertical surface. 

(iii) Vertical Position 3/LFV; Plates so placed that weld is deposited with its axis vertical. 

(iv) Overhead Position 3/LFO; Plates so placed that the weld is deposited with its axis horizontal on 


the underside of the horizontal surface and against the vertical surface. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 837 


52. Pipe groove welding.— The welding position of pipe groove welding as mentioned in Figure 3/3 of this chapter 
shall be as following, namely:- 

(i) Horizontal Rolled 3/PGR; Pipe with its axis horizontal and rolled during welding so that the weld 
metal is deposited from above with the axis of the weld horizontal. 

(ii) Vertical Fixed 3/PGV; One test of groove welded joint with the axis of the pipe in a vertical position 
and the seam welded circumferentially in a horizontal position. 

(iii) Horizontal Fixed 3/PGH; One test of groove welded joint with the axis of the pipe in a horizontal 
position and the seam welded without rotating the pipe. 

(iv) Pipe Inclined 3/PGI; One test of groove welded joint with the axis of the pipe inclined 45 degree 


to the horizontal axis and the seam welded without rotating the pipe.

PART-3 
53. Engagement of certified welders or welding operators.— (|)No welder or welding operator shall be engaged 
for welding on boilers or steam-pipes under construction, erection or fabrication at site or in the repair of boilers or 
steam-pipes, unless he possesses a certificate as required under the regulations and attains the age not less than eighteen 
years. 


(2) He shall have undergone a regular apprenticeship of two years from a recognised Industrial training institute or 
have at least one year regular on the job industrial experience as a welder or welding operator. 

(3) The holder of such certificate shall be bound to produce it when called upon to do so by the Inspecting Authority 
or Competent Person. 

(4) In case of engaging experienced welders or welding operators, reasonable continuity of service shall be ensured 
by the employer before engaging them by maintaining proper records of test conducted by the employing 
organisation. 


54. Initial qualification test and issue of certificate — (l) Every welder or welding operator shall meet the 
qualification requirement to the satisfaction of the Competent Authority who shall assess his performance for 
qualifying for the certificate. 


(2) The Competent Authority may, thereafter, issue a certificate in the Form-II indicating the class and type of welding 
in which he has qualified. 


55. Issue of duplicate certificate.— () In case of loss of a certificate issued to a welder or welding operator in Form- 
XXI, a duplicate certificate may be issued by the Competent Authority who issued the original certificate provided 
that the Competent Authority is satisfied with the genuineness of the case. 


(2) Fee for issue of duplicate certificate shall be as per regulation 33[, 


56. Validity of certificate —(l) The certificate issued to a welder or welding operator under these regulations shall 
remain valid for a maximum period of twenty-four months from the date of issue, provided that the holder thereof has, 
subsequent to the test, been employed with reasonable continuity on the class and type of work for which he is 
qualified. 


57. Revalidation or renewal of certificate —(l) The certificate may be renewed after the validity of 24 months 
from the date of qualification from time to time, for a period not exceeding twenty-four months at a time, in case the 
welder or welding operator is continuously engaged in qualified process and certified by the organisation for which 
he is working. 


(2) The details of welding continuity shall be filled up in the Form-XX duly signed by the organisation and preserved 
along with the original certificate and put up to Competent Authority for renewal. 


(3) In case of non-fulfilment of continuity criteria the welder or welding operator shall appear for the re-qualification 
test to the satisfaction of the Competent Authority. 


58. Revoking of qualification.— () The performance qualification of a welder or welding operator can be revoked 
by the Competent Authority if there is a specific reason to question his ability to make welds that meet the 
specification. 


(2) The qualification that support the welding that he is doing shall be revoked. 


842 


THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4]

plate and subsequently, allowed to appear for qualification testing in alloy steel plate, carbon steel or alloy steel pipe 
and tube qualification. or, a welder or welding operator may be tested for higher grades, pipe and tube directly. 


(b) The range of qualification covered by testing of a particular grade of material or product form shall be as shown 


in Table 3/I. 


(2) The qualification certificate of such a welder or welding operator who has successfully completed qualification 


test, may be extended as per regulation 5]7.

520.Essential variables for welder or welding operator requalification. — A welder or welding operator shall 


require requalification whenever a change is made in one of the following essential variables, namely:-. 


(i) 


(ii) 


(iii) 


(iv) 


(v) 


(vi) 


(vii) 


An omission of backing- A welder or welding operator needs requalification when the backing is 
removed and double-welded groove welds are considered welding with backing. 

An addition of the backing in gas welding - A welder or welding operator shall require 
requalification when the backing is introduced in gas welding process. 

A change in U number of electrode - A welder shall require requalification when the consumable 
group designation is changed from one U number to other U number (refer Table 3/5 & Table 3/6 
of this regulation). 

A change in the base metal (M number) to be welded - A welder shall require requalification when 
the base metal is changed (refer Table 2/ in Chapter-2 and Tablel3/7 in this Chapter). However, a 
welder who is qualified in a higher grade of steel shall be permitted to weld a lower grade of steel. 

A change from one welding process to any other process - A welder shall require requalification 
when the welding process is changed. 

A change from direct current to alternating current, and vice versa - A welder shall require 
requalification when the current type is changed from ‘dc’ to ‘ac’ and vice versa. 

A change in welding position —(a) A welder shall require requalification when the position in which 


he is qualified is changed.

PART-4 


52]. Tests for initial qualification of a welder or welding operator.— For qualification of a welder, the welder or 


welding operator has to appear for the tests as given in regulations 522 to 526. 


522. Theoretical examination — A welder or welding operator shall be required to answer questions on the following 


subjects, orally or otherwise- 


(i) Weld preparation 
(ii) Elementary knowledge of the working of welding equipment. 
(ili) Elementary knowledge of properties of material to be welded — cold and hot working, thermal 


conductivity, fusion point, oxidation (for welders engaged in alloy steel welding). 
(iv) Elementary knowledge of electro-technical principles, - kinds of current, striking arc voltage, welding — 


arc voltage (for arc welders). 
(५) Kinds of welds, welding defects and their prevention, welding technique (forward and backward), 
influence of electrical parameters like amperage (for electric arc welders), preheating of base material 


and subsequent heat treatment. 


(vi) Electrodes and filler metals for different types of welds and steels and joints in different positions. 


523.Practical tests—() The welder or welding operator shall be required to undergo and pass the tests as given in 


regulations 524 to 526. 


(2) The material of plates, tubes, pipes and electrodes used for these tests shall conform to the requirements of 


appropriate regulations as may be applicable in each case. 


524.Plate Welding.— (/)One groove welded joint of two pieces of plates with single V, double V or double U grooves 
on boiler quality plates in the required positions (see Fig. 3/] of regulation 52). 


846 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(2) One fillet welded joint over a length of 38! mm using plates of not less than 6 mm thick in the required positions 
(see Fig. 3/2). 


525.Pipe and tube Welding.— () A butt welded joint of two pieces of pipes with the axis in a horizontal position. 
(see Fig. |3/PGH) with a pipe diameter |27.5 x !2.5 mm thickness (minimum). 
(2) A butt welded joint of two pieces of boiler tubes of diameter 76.l mm x 7.! mm thickness (maximum) with 
the axis in a vertical position and tubes of same size fixed in adjoining positions at a pitch distance of 300 
mm (see figure |3/PGV). 
(3) A weld between a branch tubes of diameter 88.9 mm (minimum) to a pipe (see Fig. 3/7). The branch tube 
shall not be of size less than 89 mm diameter x 6 mm thick. 


526. Cladding.—(l) This test is required only for welders or welding operators doing corrosion resistant/hard facing 
overlay. 
(2) The qualification test coupon shall be of minimum size of !50 mm x I50 mm x T (thickness of base metal). 
(3) The weld overlay cladding shall be of 38 mm wide (minimum) and 5 mm thick (minimum two layers). 
(4) The weld overlay shall consist of a minimum of three weld beads in the first layer. (See Table 3/9 of chapter 
3 for qualification limits.) 


Note - Every welded test piece for the examination of welders shall be stamped with an identification mark on either 
side of the weld. 


527. Tests for requalification of a welder / welding operator.— (|)The material of plates, tubes, pipes and electrodes 
used for practical tests shall conform to the requirements of appropriate regulations as may be applicable in each case. 


(2) For requalification, the welder or welding operator need not be examined in theoretical subjects. He shall be 
required to qualify in the following practical tests, namely: - 
(i) Plate Welding; a groove welded joint shall be made in a position originally qualified. 
(ii) Pipe and Tube welding; as mentioned in regulation 525. 
(iii) | Cladding; as mentioned in regulation 526. 
(3) When a welder is continuously engaged on production weld, test on the actual production joints to the 
satisfaction of the Competent Authority may be accepted as an alternative to the tests prescribed as above 


under clauses (0), (ii) and (iii) of sub-regulation (2).

529.Fillet welded plate specimens.— (|) (a) The preparation of the fillet-weld test specimen shall conform to Fig. 
3/5 of chapter 3. 


(b)The test specimen shall not contain any visible cracks. It shall be cut transversely to provide a centre section (254 
mm) long and two end sections each approximately (25 mm) long. 


(2) (a) The centre section shall be loaded laterally in such a way that the root of the weld is in tension. 


(b) The load shall be steadily increased until the specimen fractures or bends flat upon itself. 


848 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(3) The cut end of one of the end sections shall be polished and etched with a suitable reagent to give a clear definition 
of the structure of the weld. 


(4) The test shall be deemed to have been satisfactory when the requirements as specified in sub-regulation (5) are 
met. 


(5) (a)The bend specimen shall not fracture during loading and if the specimen fractures, then the fractured surface 
shall show no evidence of cracks or incomplete root penetration, and the sum of the lengths of inclusions and gas 
pockets visible on the fractured surface shall not exceed (5 mm). 


(b) Visual examination of the cross-section of the weld shall show the following: 
(i) Complete fusion at the root and freedom from cracks. 
(ii)Convexity or concavity of the weld profile not more than |.6 mm 


(iii) The length of two legs of the fillet within |.6 mm difference.

53.Welded Tube Joints.— ()A test length approximately 203 mm long shall be cut from the tube with the welded 
joint disposed approximately at the centre. After visual examination, one test piece not exceeding !3 mm, for tubes 6 
mm in thickness and below and thrice the thickness of the tube for thickness of over 6 mm shall be cut longitudinally. 


(2) (a) The test piece shall not be less than 76 mm in length on either side of the weld. 
(b) The slight excess of internal bead may be filed until it is not more than 0.8 mm proud of the general surface. 


(c) The test piece shall then be bent back with the root in tension through 90° round a former of diameter equal to 
three times the thickness of the tubes. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 854 


(d) With regard to alloy steel pipes and tubes, the bend test specimen shall be bent without being straightened, but 
after removal of the weld reinforcement down to the level of but not below the surface, round a former of diameter 4t 
and through an angle of 90°. 


(e) The bending may be carried out by blows or by pressure. Care shall be taken to ensure that the former is so 
positioned that the weld is maintained at the crown of the bend. 


(f) The test specimen shall be capable of being bent through 90° without signs of failure, although slight premature 
failure at the edges of a specimen need not be considered a cause for rejection. 


(g) The opening out of a slight defect due to incomplete root penetration or lack of root fusion need not be considered 
a cause for rejection; provided the defect has sound metal at the back and on either side of it.

(2) The corrosion resistant test coupon shall be sectioned to make four side-bend (Bl, B2, B3, B4) test specimens 
perpendicular to the direction of the welding as per regulations 60 and l6l. Test specimens shall be removed at

PART-7 
540. Awarding of marks.— () (a) Marks shall be awarded as per the Form-XXI. 


(b) Candidates obtaining marks not less than 60 per cent in the oral or written examination and not less than 75 per 
cent in the practical tests, shall be deemed to have qualified for a certificate provided that the bend tests are found to 
be satisfactory and in case a candidate fail in the oral or written examination but passes in the practical test, he may 
be re-examined in oral or written examination within a period of twelve weeks from the date of examination of

practical test, and if he obtains not less than 60 per cent marks in the re-examination, he shall be deemed to have

(2) The Form shall be attested by the Competent Authority. 


54. Award of Certificate — (!) On successful completion of theoretical tests mentioned in regulation 522 and 
practical tests mentioned in regulations 523 to 526, the welder may be awarded a certificate in Form-II to the extent 
of the tests passed by him. 


(2) (a) Welder or welding operator who pass the tests for groove welds in plates shall be considered as having 
qualified for making fillet welds in plates. 


(b) Welders or welding operators who pass the tests for fillet welds, shall be qualified to make fillet welds 
only. 


(c) Any certificate issued for any purpose under any rules made by the State Government in this behalf shall 
be deemed to have been issued for that purpose under this Chapter and any action taken under the said rules, shall be 
deemed to have been taken under this Chapter. 


542. Maintenance of records.— (|) Every manufacturer or repairer of boilers and steam-pipes shall maintain a record 
of all welding personnel engaged on welding and repairing of boilers and steam-pipes, particulars of each welder and 
welding operator and the work handled by him. Such record shall be produced to the Inspecting Authority or 
Competent Person on demand. 


(2) In the case of welders or welding operators who undertake welding under their own responsibility, the 
record as aforesaid shall be maintained by themselves. 


543. Fees for examination of Welders or Welding operators.— Fees for examination of Welders or Welding 
operators shall be as per regulation 33|. 


544. Penalty.— Penalty shall be as per regulation 332.
