CHAPTER -4 
SMALL INDUSTRIAL BOILERS 


PART-I 
GENERAL 


545. Scope— =‘ This Chapter shall apply to the design, construction, inspection, registration, operation and 


maintenance of small industrial boilers. 


546.For the purpose of this chapter, “small industrial boiler” shall include;- 


(a) 


(b) 


A shell type boiler generating steam for use external to itself under pressure up to 7 kg/cm? (g) and having a 
volumetric capacity exceeding 25 litres (such capacity being measured from the feed check valve to the main 
steam stop valves), but not exceeding 500 litres including the volumetric capacity of all pressure parts being 
heated from the same heating source and connected to the boiler; or 


A coil type or a once through boiler or a water tube boiler having the conditions specified in clause (a) above 
except - 


(i) The limitation of pressure shall be 2 kg/cm? (g), and 


(ii) The capacity shall not be exceeding 50 litres; 


Provided that in case of boilers having combined features of clauses (a) and (b), the design pressure shall be 


restricted to 7 kg/cm? (g) and the volumetric capacity of particular pressure parts shall not exceed the limits specified 
in the respective clauses above subject to an aggregate of 500 litres.

(b) The steel maker certificate provided in Part A of Form V is not required for steel plates of IS: 2062 from 
the steel maker provided all other certification requirements as specified in applicable regulations are 
complied with. 


(a) Heads of parts of boilers when not exposed to direct impact of flame may be made of cast iron or malleable

(b) The allowable stress on cast iron or malleable iron shall be based on the tensile strength of material with

(c) The safety valve shall be connected to the boiler independently of any other steam connections, without 
any unnecessary intervening pipe or fitting. Such intervening pipe or fitting if unavoidable shall not be

(l0) No valve of any description shall be placed between safety valve and the boiler not on the discharge pipe 
from the safety valve to the atmosphere.

CHAPTER-5 
FEED WATER FOR BOILER 


556. Scope.— This chapter lays down specifications for feed water and boiler water for— 
(a) Low and medium pressure boilers (boilers operation up to 60 kg/cm? (g). 
(b) For boilers operating at pressures higher than 60 kg/cm? (g), better quality of water to IS: 0496 shall be 
adopted. 


557. Requirements.— The water shall comply with the requirements given in Table 5/] of this chapter when tested 
by the methods provided in Columns 6 and 7 of the table. 


558. Sampling.— Sampling shall be done by following general directions mentioned in Part-2 of IS: 3025 issued by 
Bureau of Indian Standards and in particular, the following points shall be observed, namely:- 


(a) A stainless steel or monel metal coil shall be fitted on the sampling cock so that the temperature of the water 
sample shall be well below the boiling point at atmospheric pressure and there is no risk of aeration and 
concentration due to flashing into steam; and 


(b) Samples of feed water shall be collected from the delivery of the boiler feed pump, samples of boiler water 
from the top drum, and samples of condensate from the delivery of the condensate extraction pump. 


559. Test methods.— Tests shall be carried out as provided in the appropriate clauses of IS: 3025 and IS: 3550 and 
indicated against the characteristics in Table |5/! of this chapter.

CHAPTER -6 
HEAT EXCHANGERS AND PRESSURE VESSELS 


PART-I 


560. Application.—_(l) This chapters hall apply to steam accumulators, steam coil air preheaters, high 
pressure(HP) heaters, deaerators and blow down tanks operating above 3.5 kg/cm?(g). 

(2) Any steam consuming equipment where steam is condensed or open to atmosphere shall not be covered under 
this chapter. 


56l. Construction and workmanship.— The construction and workmanship shall conform to the requirements 
of relevant regulations for the particular type of construction. 


562. Materials.— Materials used in the construction of these vessels shall comply with the applicable regulations 
of Chapter-2. 


563. Welding consumables.— Welding consumables shall comply with the relevant provisions of Chapter-2. 
564. Tubes and pipes.— The tubes and pipes shall comply with the relevant provisions of Chapter-2. 


565. Heat treatment.— All fusion welded vessels shall be heat treated for stress relief as per regulation 23. 


PART-2 
Determination of working pressure of vessels of welded construction 


566. Shells — The working pressure shall be calculated as per Equation (4/l) mentioned under regulation 69 
of chapter 4. 


567.Dished end plates.— The maximum working pressure of dished end plates subject to pressure on the 
concave side shall be determined as per Equation (4/0) of regulation [77 of chapter 4. 


568.F lat end plates.— The maximum working pressure of flat end plates shall be determined as per appropriate 
regulations in Chapter -3 


569. Girth flange—() Non-standard bolted flange connections when used shall satisfy the requirements of 
these regulations . 

(2) The design and construction of a flange shall involve the selection of the gasket (material, type, and 
dimensions), flange facing, bolting, hub proportions, flange width, and flange thickness. 

(3) Flange dimensions shall be such that the calculated stresses in the flange, does not exceed the allowable 
flange stresses. 


570. Standard flanges.— Standard flanges used in heat exchanger shall conform to the Codes or Standards like 
British Standards (BS), European Standards (EN), American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Boiler 
and Pressure Vessel Code and Tubular Exchanger Manufacturers Association (TEMA), commonly used in 
industrially advanced countries.

577. U-Tubes.—(|) U-tubes used in heat exchangers shall not have ovality more than 0% after forming. 
(2) Carbon and alloy steel U-Tubes up to mean radius R = 5D (where D = Tube outside diameter) shall be 
stress relieved with minimum soaking time of l5 minutes. 


578. Tube bundle assemblies. — Tube bundle assemblies shall be checked for free entry by using a ring 
gauge having inside diameter of baffle equal to Outside Diameter(OD) of tube + .5 mm. 


579. Initial qualification of tube to tube sheet joints —()The method of joining tubes to tube sheet shall be 
any one of the following, namely:- 


(i)Strength expansion only (without welding); 
(ii) Strength welding & light expansion, or 
(iii) Strength expansion & seal welding. 


(2) All the above three process shall be carried out with procedure qualified by the manufacturer. 


(3) (a) The boiler or boiler component manufacturer shall prepare written procedures for joints that are 
expanded (whether welded and expanded or expanded only) for joint strength. 

(b) The boiler or boiler component manufacturer shall establish the variables that affect joint repeatability in 
these procedures. 

(c) The procedures shall provide detailed descriptions or sketches of enhancements, such as grooves, serrations, 
threads, and coarse machining profiles. 


(4) (a) For strength welded joints, minimum eight mock up welds are required to qualify each procedure. 
(b) The mock up assembly shall essentially duplicate the tube hole configuration and tube-to-tubesheet joint 
design. 


(5) The materials group (M No. wise), tube hole size, tube size and tube fit up with tube sheet shall 
simulate production. 


(6) Test block arrangement shall be as given under,— 


Minimum number of holes = 3-2-3 for triangular pitch. 
= 3-3-3 for Square pitch 
Thickness = Tube sheet thickness or 50 mm whichever is less. 


(7) (a) The test block simulating the tube-sheet may be circular, square or rectangular in shape, 
essentially in general conformity with the tube pitch geometry. 

(b) The test assembly shall consist of an array of tubes such that the tube to be tested is in the geometric center 
of the array and surrounded by at least one row of adjacent tubes. 

(c) The test block shall extend a distance of at least one tube-sheet ligament beyond the edge of the peripheral 
tubes in the assembly. 


(8) All tubes in the test block array shall be from the same grade of material and shall be installed using 
identical procedures. 


(9) (a) The length of the tube used for testing the tube joint need only be sufficient to suit the test apparatus. 
(b) The length of the tubes adjacent to the tube joint to be tested shall not be less than the thickness of the test 
block to be qualified. 


864 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


580. Procedure for testing the test block.—(|) The mock-up welds shall be subjected to the tests given in 
regulations 58 to 583sequentially and shall meet the applicable acceptance criteria. 


58l. Acceptance criteria for visual examination.— (l) The accessible surfaces of the welds shall be examined 
visually with no magnification required. 

(2) The welds shall show complete fusion and no evidence of burning through the tube wall, and shall be free 
from cracking or porosity. 


582. Acceptance criteria with liquid penetrant.— Procedure and performance tests examined by liquid 
penetrant techniques shall be judged unacceptable when the examination exhibits any indication in excess of 
the limits specified as the following;- 

(i) relevant linear indications; 
(ii) relevant rounded indications greater than 5 mm; 
(iii) four or more relevant rounded indications in a line separated by |.5 mm or less (edge-to-edge). 


583. Acceptance criteria for macro-examination.— (l) The mock up welds shall be sectioned through the 
center of the tube for macro-examination. 
(2) The four exposed surfaces shall be smoothed and etched with a suitable etchant to give a clear definition of 
the weld and heat-affected zone. 
(3) Using a magnification of 0X to 20X, the exposed cross sections of the weld shall conform to as under;- 
(i) minimum leak path dimension required by the design; 
(ii) no cracking; 
(iii) complete fusion of the weld deposit into the tube-sheet and tube wall face; 
(iv) complete penetration of the weld deposit to within 0.4 mm of the root of the joint; and 
(v) porosity shall not reduce the weld throat below the required minimum leak path thickness. 


584. Tube thinning calculations.— () Tube thinning calculations shall be using the equation given below, based 
on the measured values. 
(2) The thinning shall be within 5% to 8%.

[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 865 


CHAPTER- 7 
SMALL SOLAR BOILERS 


585. Scope.—This chapter shall apply to the design, construction, inspection, registration, operation and 
maintenance of small solar boilers. 


PART-I 
Definitions 


586. Solar receivers.— Solar receivers are the devices that receive solar radiation heat from the sun to generate steam. 


587. Small solar boiler .— () A small solar boiler shall be a solar steam generating system producing steam for use 
external to itself having area concentration ratio of solar radiation capturing aperture area to receiver area less than 
300 and having a volumetric capacity more than 25 litres. 


(2) A natural or forced circulation type boiler wherein the receiver is the solar heat receiving device generating steam 
at pressure up to 2 kg/cm?(g) 


588. Heating surface area.— The heating surface area of a small solar boiler shall be the area of receivers exposed 
to the receiving radiation. 


589. Volumetric capacity.— Volumetric capacity of a small solar boiler shall be the total volume from feed check 
valve to the main steam stop valve at the outlet of steam header. 


PART-2 
Extent to which Variation from the standard conditions laid down in the preceding chapters is 
permissible 


590.Variations from standards.— The variations from the standard conditions provided in the preceding 
chapters of these regulations shall be permitted for small solar boilers as provided in regulations 59 to 594. 


59. Materials.— (l) The materials used in the construction of small solar boilers shall conform to the 
provisions made in these regulations. 


(2) (a) Plates used in the construction of the boilers shall be either of IS: 2062 or equivalent or as per Chapter-2. 
(b) The plate for shell and heads shall be not less than 6 mm in thickness and the heads as tube sheets for tubes 
rolled in shall be at least 8 mm in thickness. 


(3) The tubes and pipes shall be made of carbon steel, alloy steel, stainless steel or copper. 


(4) Corrosion allowance of 0.75 mm shall be provided for parts of the boiler directly exposed to atmosphere and solar 
radiation. 
(5) No corrosion allowance is required for stainless steel parts of the boiler. 


(6) Materials need not be certified with Indian Boiler Regulations forms from the maker provided all other certification 
requirements as mentioned in applicable regulations are complied with. 


866 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


592. Design, construction, workmanship and the method of computing the maximum allowable working 
pressure.— (|) The construction except where otherwise specified shall be the same as those provided in the 
relevant provisions of the preceding chapters of these regulations. 


(2) In the case of Fusion welded small solar boilers, radiography or stress relieving of the weld joints shall not 
be mandatory. 


593. Inspection and testing.— (|) The small solar boilers shall be subjected to inspection during construction 
and after completion of construction by an Inspecting Authority. 
(2) The inspection of small solar boilers shall be made at the following stages, namely:- 


(i) Material identification and inspection. 


(ii) Hydraulic test; every completed boiler wholly or partly welded construction, the hydraulic test 
pressure shall be equal to two times the design pressure of the boiler. 


594. Certificates and maker’s stamps.— (l) The certificate and maker's stamp shall be in conformity with the 
provisions of Chapter-lof these regulations. 


(2) Where all information cannot be visibly stamped on the boiler plate due to its small size, maker's certificate 
accompanying the boiler shall contain the necessary details, but in all cases name, works number and the year 
of make shall be stamped or exhibited on the boiler. 


PART-3 


595. Valves, gauges, fittings and feed supply.— () Small solar boiler shall be fitted with the following, namely:— 
(i) wash plugs for cleaning; 
(ii) suitable provision to indicate the water level; 
(iii) one water feeding device; 
(iv)one feed pipe shall be provided with a check valve and a stop valve of a size not less than that of the 
pipe; 
(v) suitable provision to drain the boiler water; 
(vi) one steam pressure gauge having minimum 00 mm dial size; and 
(vii) one safety valve for relieving the steam pressure. 


(2) Safety valves shall be certified under Indian Boiler Regulations and all other fittings may be certified by the 
manufacturers of such fittings. 


596. Registration, operation and maintenance.—()The fees required to accompany an application under sub- 
section (2) of Section l2 of the Act shall be such as provided in regulation 304. 

(2) The inspection fee for renewal of certificate after every four years shall be as provided in regulation 
305. 

(3) The certificate of manufacture and test for small solar boilers shall be issued in Form-XXIII. 


(4) Operator for these boilers shall possess minimum educational qualification of matriculation or 
equivalent.

(a) onthe expiry of the period for which it was granted; or 
(b) when any accident occurs to the boiler; or 


(c) when the boiler is moved the boiler, except a vertical boiler, the heating surface of which is less than 


two hundred square feet, or a portable or vehicular boiler; or 


(d) save as provided in section 47 of the Act, when any structural alteration, addition or renewal is made 


in or to the boiler; or 


(e) if the Chief Inspector in any particular case so directs when any structural alteration, addition or 


renewal is made in or to any steam-pipe attached to the boiler; or 


(f) on the communication to the owner of the boiler of an order of the Chief Inspector or Inspector 
prohibiting its use on the ground that it or any boiler component attached thereto is in a dangerous 


condition. 


Under Section i5 of the Act, when the period of a certificate relating to a boiler has expired, the 
owner shall, provided that he has applied before the expiry of that period for a renewal of the certificate 
be entitled to use the boiler at the design pressure entered in the former certificate, pending the issue of 
orders on the application but this shall not be deemed to authorise the use of a boiler in any of the cases 
referred to in clauses (0), (c), (d), (e) and (f) of sub-section (4) of section 3 occurring after the expiry of 
the period of the certificate. 


(3) The boiler shall not be used at a pressure greater than the pressure entered in the certificate as the 
Design pressure nor with the safety valve set to a pressure exceeding such design pressure. 


(4) The boiler shall not be used otherwise than in a condition which the owner reasonably believes to be 
compatible with safe working. 


(5) Form XII shall be countersigned by the Chief Inspector at the time of registration only, as per the 


provisions of sub-section (6) of section 2 of the Act. 


Note: The particulars and dimensions regarding this boiler may be obtained by the owner on payment in the 
prescribed manner on application to the Chief Inspector.

APPENDIX-A 


INSPECTION AND TESTING OF BOILERS, BOILER COMPONENTS AND OTHER PARTS DURING 
MANUFACTURE 


GENERAL. —The Inspecting Authority or Competent Person shall have access to the works of the manufacturer at 
all reasonable times and shall inspect the manufacture of the boiler at least at the following stages and may reject any 
part that does not comply with the requirements of the Indian Boiler Regulations, 2026. In case of any doubt, the 
Inspecting Authority or Competent Person may examine at any stage other than the stages stipulated below. The 
manufacturer shall give at least four working days’ notice to the Inspecting Authority or Competent Person before 
reaching each stage. Before undertaking any of the stage inspections, the Inspecting Authority or Competent Person 
shall satisfy himself that the testing equipment/instrument has been properly calibrated. 


STAGES OF INSPECTION. — Each boiler shall be inspected during manufacture by a Competent Person nominated 
by the Inspecting Authority. Sufficient inspections shall be made to ensure that the materials, manufacturing and 
testing conform to the requirements of these regulations. 


Stages of Inspection During Manufacture. — 


A. Shell Type Boilers. —(a) 0) When the materials are ready for identification with the relevant material test 
certificates at boiler maker’s works; 


(ii) In laying out and cutting the plates, the plate identification mark shall be located so as to be clearly visible after 
the boiler part is completed. If the plate’s identification mark is unavoidably cut out, it shall be transferred by the 


manufacturer to another part of the component to the satisfaction of the Inspecting Authority or Competent Person; 


(iii) The Inspecting Authority or Competent Person shall identify weld test plate material if production weld tests are 
required; 


(b) When the Shell plate and end plates have been formed with plate edges prepared for welding and test plates are 
attached; 


(c) When the welding of main cylindrical shell is completed and checked for circularity; 
(d) To examine radiographs and/or reports of non-destructive testing; 


(e) When openings have been prepared and stand pipes and similar connections including end plates have been 
tackwelded in position and subsequently on completion; 


(f) When welding of drum or shell is completed and to check the records of heat-treatment when heat treatment is 
required under these regulations; 


(g) When weld test specimens have been prepared from the test plate, previously selected to witness the required 
testing; 


(h) During hydraulic test, followed by external and internal examination and stamping. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 964 


8. Water Tube Boilers. — 
(I) Welded drums, headers, separators and vessels. —(a) (i) When the materials are ready for identification with 
the relevant material test certificates at boiler maker’s works; 


(ii) In laying out and cutting the plates, the plate identification mark shall be located so as to be clearly visible after 
the boiler part is completed. If the plate’s identification mark is 

unavoidably cut out, it shall be transferred by the manufacturer to another part of the component to the satisfaction of 
the Inspecting Authority or Competent Person; 


(iii) The Inspecting Authority or Competent Person shall identify weld test plate material if production weld tests are 
required; 


(b) When the plates are formed to cylindrical shape with the edges prepared for welding and set up in readiness for 
commencement of welding and attachment of test plates; 


(c) When the welding of the main cylindrical shell is completed, the shell checked for circularity and the radiographic 
or ultrasonic test reports, records are available for scrutiny; 


(d) When the end plates are ready for identification with the mill certificate, formed to shape with weld edges prepared 
and set on to the cylindrical shell in readiness for the circumferential welding operation; 


(e) When the welding of the end plates to the drum or the header is complete and the radiographs or ultrasonic 
examination records are available for scrutiny; 


(f) When each drum or header is prepared to receive any compensation plates and attachments, and when at least 0% 
of each type of branch of tube stub is set up ready for welding; 


(g) When all welding on each drum or header is complete, the Inspecting Authority or Competent Person will check 
the records of heat treatment, and mark off of specimens for preparation and testing from test plates; 

(h) During non-destructive examination, after stress relieving, on alloy steel drums and carbon steel drums with carbon 
content exceeding 0.25 % or thickness more than 00 mm; 


(i) During hydraulic test followed by final examination and stamping. 


(II) Seamless drums, headers, separators and vessels. —(a) When materials are ready for identification with the 
relevant material test certificates, also when each cylinder is prepared for forming, or welding of separate end closures 
and to identify test plate material; 

(b) When the end plates are ready for identification with the mill certificate, formed to shape with weld edges prepared 
and set on to the cylindrical shell in readiness for the circumferential welding operation; 


(c) When the welding of the end plates to the drum or the header is complete and the radiographs or ultrasonic 
examination records are available for scrutiny; 


(d) When each drum or header is prepared to receive any compensation plates and attachments, and when at least [0% 
of each type of branch of tube stub is set up ready for welding; 


(e) When all welding on each drum or header is complete, the Inspecting Authority will check the records of heat 
treatment, and mark off of specimens for preparation and testing from test plates;

(f) During non-destructive examination, after stress relieving, on alloy steel drums and carbon steel drums with carbon 
content exceeding 0.25 % or thickness more than 00 mm; 


(g) During hydraulic test followed by final examination and stamping. 


C. Tubular and piping components. —(a) When the tubes or pipes are ready for identification with the relevant 
material test certificates at the boiler makers’ works; 


(b) When all welding of tubes or pipes and their attachments are complete and the non-destructive examination and 
stress relieving report/records are available for scrutiny; 


(c) During hydraulic test followed by final examination and stamping. 


D. Inspections and tests to be carried out at Steel Makers’ Works Foundry or Forging Units and pipe and tube 
makers’ works by the Inspecting Authority or Competent Person. —

Steel Maker as recognised under the Indian Boiler Regulations by the Central Boilers Board, these tests shall be carried

(iv) Final inspection and stamping

inspections shall be carried out and certified by the manufacturers of pipes and tubes themselves and records

(iii) Testing, final examination and stamping.

(b) Hydraulic test and stamping.

APPENDIX-B 
TRANSVERSE RUPTURE STRESS (MODULUS OF RUPTURE) 


The transverse strength of cast iron may be expressed by a figure shown as the Transverse Rupture Stress; 
this figure is obtained by dividing the maximum bending moment at failure by the modulus of the section. Thus, the 
Transverse Rupture Stress is the maximum stress which would have existed if the material had behaved in accordance 
with the assumptions made in the ordinary theory of bending, and in that event it would be independent of the size 
and shape of the section. Bars fractured in transverse, however, are stressed beyond the elastic limit, and under these 
conditions the theory of bending no longer holds good. Furthermore, the influence of rate of cooling in cast metals is 
such that the Transverse Rupture Stress of a Thick Bar is less than that of a thinner bar of the same metal. The 
Transverse Rupture Stress, therefore, is not strictly independent of the size and metal. The Transverse Rupture Stress, 
therefore, is not strictly independent of the size and shape, of the section, but nevertheless forces a convenient way of 
expressing the result of transverse tests without the necessity for giving full details of bar dimensions. The formula 
required is obtained as follows: 


A bar supported at both ends and centrally loaded with a load ‘W’ is subject to a bending Moment WL/4, ‘L’ 
being the distance between supports. The resistance offered by the bar may be expressed as fZ, ‘f? being the stress and 
‘Z’ the modulus of the section. At fracture, ‘f? becomes the breaking stress of Transverse Rupture Stress, and WL/4 = 
fZ, where f = (LW)/ (4Z). If ‘W’ is in tons and ‘L’ in inches, ‘f is in tons per square inch. For a round bar, Z = 
0.0982d?, where d diameter in inches. 


Since for a standard round bar ‘L’ and ‘Z’ are constant, the value WL/4Z is fixed and hence the Transverse 
Rupture Stress f= KW, where ‘K’ is a constant. 


The factor ‘K’ for converting actual breaking loads into Transverse Rupture Stress are given in the following 
tables both for the Standard test bars and the test bars varying within the limits of regulation 65. In the same table are 
given factors for converting actual breaking loads into equivalent breaking loads on the bars of Standard diameter. 


[भाग ॥|-खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 965

Diameter. 
(Equivalent Breaking Load on Bar of Standard Diameter = X x Actual Breaking Load). 
And 
Factors K for converting Actual Breaking Loads into Transverse Rupture Stresses. 
(Transverse Rupture Stress in tons per sq.in. = K x Actual Breaking Load in lbs.)

surfaces of the plates. Where the plates are not level with each other the metal many be cut away to bring them 
approximately level, provided that the thickness of the plate is not reduced by more than a total of | mm. 

The test specimens shall then be tested for tensile test as in Appendix-D. 


(6) Transverse bend test.— The bend test specimens shall be 38 mm in width. The upper and lower surfaces of 
the weld shall be filled, ground or machined level with the respective original surfaces of the plates, with the 
proviso as in item (6) above. The tool marks should be avoided as they lead to location of stress and may cause 
premature failure. For this reason the direction of machining of the surfaces should be along the specimens and 
transverse to the weld. The sharp corners of the test specimens shall be rounded to a radius not exceeding |.3 
mm. 


The test specimens shall be bent through an angle of !80° over a former having a diameter equal to three 
times the thickness of the specimen, as shown in Fig. 2/8. One test specimen shall be tested with the face of the 


weld in tension and one with the root of the weld in tension.

APPENDIX-E 


PROOF TEST FOR CREEP QUALITY OF CARBON STEEL BOILER QUALITY PLATE- 
SPECIFICATION 


l. NATURE OF TEST — The test shall consist of a tensile creep test carried out over a period of at 
least 48 hours at a temperature of 450°C and with stress of .25 kg/mm7?. Under these conditions 
the slope of the chord to the creep curve between the 247 and 48" hour shall not exceed 50 x 0 = 
4 strain per hour. 


2. CONDITION OF MATERIAL. — The test shall be made on the material in the normalized 
condition. The normalizing temperature shall be between 875°C — 925°C, and the plate sample 
shall be maintained at the normalizing temperature for one hour per inch of thickness and cooled 
freely in still air. 


3. TEMPERATURE OF TEST. — 

(4) Temperature Measurement. — (a) The temperature of the specimen shall be measured 
by thermocouples suitable for the temperature specified. Two thermocouples situated one at each end 
of the gauge length shall be used in the case of test pieces having gauge lengths upto 5l mm, and for 


longer gauge lengths and additional thermocouple situated at the middle of the gauge length shall be 
used. 


(b) Thermocouples shall make good thermal contact with the test piece and the protected from the direct 
heat of the furnace of being covered with asbestos tape or equivalent insulation. 


(c) The cold junction shall be maintained at a known temperature which shall be registered by a mercury 
thermometer. Alternatively, a suitable means shall be provided for correcting automatically errors 
in reading due to changes in temperature of the cold junction. 


(2) Temperature Control. —The two (or three) thermocouples specified in clause (a) shall 
agree with one another within 3°C and the average of these readings shall be taken as the test 
temperature which shall not vary from 450°C by more than + 2°C throughout the test. 


Either a continuous record of sufficient readings of the temperature shall be made to indicate that 
the temperature conditions have been satisfactory. 


(3) Heating period before loading. — The specimen shall be maintained at the specified temperature 
for at least an hour prior to the application of the load. 


4. STRESS. —The load required to produce the specified stress shall be gradually applied without 
shock during a period not exceeding five minutes and the stress shall be accurate to + 2 % percent. 


5. SENSITIVITY OF STRAIN-MEASUREING EQUIPMENT. —The sensitivity of the 
extensometer must be such that strains can be measured to the nearest 0.00002. 


6. READINGS. — A sufficient number of strain readings shall be taken clearly to define the creep 
curve upto 48 hours, and the chord slope shall be measured from a chord drawn between points on 
the curve at the 247 and 48" hours. 


7. REPEAT TEST. — If the materials fail to pass the test, but the chord slope does not exceed 60 x 
0 = 6° strain per hour, a retest may be made at the request of the manufacturer and shall be 
accepted if satisfactory, or at the Competent Person discretion a pass test at a stress 5 percent less 
than that specified may be accepted. 


978 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4]

STANDARD PIPE FLANGES 


The different tables of flange dimensions (Table F.T.) have been designed to suit pipes and vessels

maximum temperature of 427°C. 

In all cases the hydraulic test pressure should be twice the maximum allowable working pressure 
to which the pipes are subjected in use.

APPENDIX-G 
SAFETY VALVE DISCHARGE EFFICIENCY TESTING 


A. General. 


(i) The purpose and manner of testing shall be such as to provide suitable data from which a constant 'c' may be 
determined in Equation (5/7). To this end the following information shall be supplied to the Inspecting 
Authority before testing is undertaken: 


(a) Full particulars on the values to be tested and range of valves and springs which they represent. 
(b) Details of the testing rig including instrumentation and proposed calibration procedure. 


(c) Proposed source, capacity, pressure, temperature of steam used for the test. 
(ii) All testing shall be witnessed by Inspecting Authority or the Competent Person. 


(iii) Tests shall be made to determine the operative characteristics of the safety valves for which a constant is to 
be determined and also to establish the discharge efficiency of the safety valve. 


(iv) Where possible, the tests to determine operating characteristics and discharge efficiency shall be carried out 
using the same steam, the same pressure conditions and the same location. When the tests are carried out 
separately, the valves in each case shall be complete and shall include all internals, e.g. blow-down 
adjustments rings. 


(v) The set pressure at which the operating characteristics are determined shall be the minimum set pressure for 
which the spring used is designed. The tests shall be carried out using steam and shall determine the set 
pressure, the lift at the over pressure specified for the type of valve, as defined in regulations 93 to 95. 


(vi) The Inspecting Authority may dispense with Operating Characteristic tests described in A(v). 


(vii) Discharge efficiency tests shall be carried out using steam and shall be carried out relative to the operative 
characteristic tests described in A(v). 


(viii) When the Inspecting Authority is satisfied that the design of valve shall operate satisfactorily it shall if 
desired, be permissible to hold the valve head mechanically at the proven lift while carrying out the tests to 
ascertain the discharge efficiency. 


B. VALVES USED IN THE TEST PROGRAMME. — 


(i) The safety valves tested shall, as far as is practicable, be representative of the pressure and size range of valve 
manufactured. 

(ii) The tests for operative characteristics and the discharge efficiency test shall be carried out on the three sizes 
or half the number of sizes in the range, whichever is smaller, with a minimum of two sizes. 


(iii) When the range is extended, due consideration shall be given, in consultation with the Inspecting Authority, 
to whether further witnessed tests are necessary. 


988 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(iv) The test for operating characteristics shall be carried out at three significantly different set pressure for each 
size of valve. 


(v) The discharge efficiency tests shall be carried out relative to one set pressure for each size of valve. 

(vi) Each tests shall be carried out a minimum of three times to obtain acceptable average results. 

(vii) For the case of valves of either novel or special design of which one size only is being manufactured, tests at 
one set pressure are permitted by agreement with the Inspecting Authority. When the range of sizes or 
pressure is extended, due consideration shall be given in consultation with the Inspecting Authority, to 
whether further witnessed tests are necessary. 

C. DETERMINATION OF CONSTANT ‘C’. — 

Let 

E,; be the measure capacity, on test of saturated steam (Kg/h.) 

P, be the pressure at safety valve inlet at which the capacity was measured (bar gauge); 

A be the area appropriate to the type of valve (mm), [see regulation !96(])]. 


X be the allowable percentage over pressure for the type of valve under test. (See regulation !96) . 


Ct be the constant determined from test.

700 


To accommodate the permitted spread on test results, tolerance on valve parts and springs, this calculated 
value of ‘Ct’ shall be derated to 80% to obtain the value of ‘C’ to be used in equation (5/7) of regulation 96(l). This 
is to ensure that all production valves shall achieve their rated discharge capacity at not more than the over pressure 
allowed for the type of valve tested. 


The Inspecting Authority may accept a more favourable derating factor of up to 90% of the calculated value 
of ‘Ct’ where the performance of the valves under test and the manufacturing and spring tolerance applicable ensure 
that the allowable overpressure for the type of valve under test shall not be exceeded when a valve is discharging its 
rated capacity in service.

quality be provided.

APPENDIX-I 
[See regulation 295(8)] 
A. Waste Heat Boilers (Fired) upto twenty years of age used exclusively in continuous process plant. — 


(.) For Waste Heat Boilers (Fired) up to twenty years of age used exclusively in continuous process plant, at the 
expiry of twelve months and at twenty four months from the date of inspection carried out in accordance with the 
procedure provided in regulation 3! and certification of fitness issued by the concerned Competent Person in the 
State, and having satisfied with the operation records as given below received alongwith application in Form-IX duly 
filled in shall be allowed for running for another period of twelve months:— 


(a) Operation data for superheater and reheater temperature excursions from the output of Data Acquisition 
System (DAS) or operation data for superheater temperature excursions maintained in the log sheet 


temperature record; 
(b) History of shut downs during the previous year with their causes and actions taken; 
(c) Records of any Non-Destructive test carried out on the boiler pressure parts during the year; 


(d) Water quality to the boiler is maintained as per the requirement of such boilers and on line data of the quality 
be provided through Data Acquisition System (DAS) or through water quality record logbook maintained at 


plant or at source of water; 


(e) Boiler tube failure record (location, number of tubes repaired/replaced). 


(2) Inspection shall be carried out by the concerned Competent Person at the expiry of thirty six months as provided 
in regulation 3][. However, in case of shutdown of fifteen days or more any time before expiry of the certification 
period and after six months of the certification, Competent Person shall be duly informed so that inspection can be 


scheduled during the said shutdown period. 


B. Waste Heat Boilers (Unfired) up to twenty years of age used exclusively in continuous process plant. — 


(.) For Waste Heat Boilers (Unfired) up to twenty years of age used exclusively in continuous process plant, at the 
expiry of twenty-four months from the date of inspection carried out in accordance with the procedure provided in 
regulation 3! land certification of fitness by the concerned Competent Person in the State, and having satisfied with 
the operation records at paragraph “A”, shall be allowed for running for another period of twenty-four months. 


(2) Inspection shall be carried out by the concerned Competent Person at the expiry of forty-eight months as provided 
in regulation 3[. However, in case of shutdown of fifteen days or more any time before expiry of the certification 
period and after six months of the certification, Competent Person shall be duly informed so that inspection can be 
scheduled during the said shutdown period. 


C. Waste Heat Boilers (Fired) more than twenty years of age used exclusively in continuous process plant. — 


Boiler more than twenty years of age shall continue to be subjected to inspection as provided in regulation 3]] every 
year to the satisfaction of concerned Competent Person in the State. However, if Remnant Life Assessment (RLA) as 
per the provisions of these regulations is carried out on the boiler and if found satisfactory, then procedure as given at 
paragraph 'A' above shall be followed. 


D. Waste Heat Boilers (Unfired) more than twenty years of age used exclusively in continuous process plant. — 


Boiler more than twenty years of age shall continue to be subjected to inspection as provided in regulation 3]] every 
year to the satisfaction of concerned Competent Person in State. However, if Remnant Life Assessment (RLA) as per

paragraph 'B' above would be applicable.
